prs.title: fix(ci): skip bot suggestion if a maintainer already posted run-slow:
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49992)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## Summary

Before posting the \"Suggested jobs to run\" comment, check if a maintainer (MEMBER, OWNER, or COLLABORATOR) already posted a `run-slow:` comment **after the current merge commit**. If so, skip creating a new bot suggestion (they already saw the current state and acted on it).

The check uses `PR_MERGE_COMMIT_TIMESTAMP` from `get-pr-info` (same server-side timestamp used by the security check in `self-comment-ci.yml`) compared against `comment.created_at` — both GitHub server-side timestamps.

**Behavior:**

| Condition | Delete old bot comment | Create new suggestion |
|---|---|---|
| Bot comment is recent and unchanged | no | no |
| Needs refresh, no maintainer action | yes (if existed) | yes |
| Needs refresh, maintainer already posted | yes (if existed) | no |

This handles PR evolution correctly: if the PR gets new commits, the merge commit timestamp advances past the maintainer's comment, so the bot resumes suggesting on the next sync.

Fixes the race condition where a maintainer posts `run-slow:` just before the bot posts the same suggestion.

prs.title: Only treat marimo as a notebook environment when IPython is installed
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49919)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

Importing `Trainer` under marimo without IPython fails:

```sh
python -c "import marimo; import transformers.trainer"
# File ".../transformers/utils/notebook.py", line 20, in <module>
#     import IPython.display as disp
# ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'IPython'
```

`is_in_notebook()` returns `True` as soon as `marimo` is in `sys.modules`, because marimo registers itself as a notebook environment. `trainer.py` then picks `NotebookProgressCallback` and imports `transformers.utils.notebook`, which imports `IPython.display` at module level. marimo does not depend on IPython, so the import blows up instead of falling back to `ProgressCallback`.

The same failure hides behind lazy imports — with `sentence-transformers` it surfaces as `Could not import module 'Trainer'`, which is hard to trace back.

This makes the marimo branch conditional on IPython actually being installed, reusing the existing `is_ipython_available()` helper. Marimo sessions that do have IPython keep the notebook callbacks; marimo sessions without it get the plain progress bar instead of an `ImportError`.

Verified on Python 3.14, transformers `5.21.0.dev0`, marimo installed, IPython absent:

```python
import marimo, transformers
from transformers.utils import is_in_notebook
is_in_notebook()   # before: True -> import transformers.utils.notebook raises ModuleNotFoundError
                   # after:  False
```

With IPython installed the value stays `True` and `transformers.utils.notebook` imports normally. Added `test_is_in_notebook_requires_ipython` covering both directions.

Fixes #49881.

Fixes a dtype mismatch in the common `flash_attn_inference_equivalence` test helper.

The helper loads the model in bf16 and casts the main input and `pixel_values` to bf16. Inputs listed in `additional_model_inputs` are copied as-is, though. If a test lists a floating-point input there (e.g. `Aimv2ModelTest` uses `additional_model_inputs = ["pixel_values"]`), the bf16 `pixel_values` gets overwritten by the original fp32 tensor and the forward pass fails with:
```
RuntimeError: Input type (float) and bias type (c10::BFloat16) should be the same
```
Reproduce:
`RUN_SLOW=1 pytest tests/models/aimv2 -k flash_attn_2_inference_equivalence`

prs.title: fix: prevent empty frame sampling for short videos
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49908)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

Fixes #49907.

This PR prevents `default_sample_indices_fn()` from returning an empty frame selection when a non-empty video is sampled at a low, positive FPS.

Previously, the number of sampled frames was calculated using integer truncation:

```python
num_frames = int(total_num_frames / video_fps * fps)
```

For short videos, this could evaluate to zero even when valid frames were available. Empty frame selections may subsequently cause failures in video decoders such as PyAV and OpenCV.

## Changes

- Ensure at least one frame is selected when the source video is non-empty and the requested FPS is positive.
- Preserve existing behavior for ordinary sampling and empty videos.
- Add a focused regression test for a 10-frame video recorded at 30 FPS and sampled at 1 FPS.

The fix adds only two lines to the sampling implementation. No new dependencies or public API changes are introduced.

## Testing

Validated locally on Transformers `5.21.0.dev0`, Python `3.11.17`, and PyTorch `2.14.1+cpu`.

- **Regression test:** Failed before the fix and passed afterward.
- **Additional edge cases:** 5 passed, covering normal sampling, short videos, zero requested FPS, empty videos, and full-FPS sampling.
- **Video utility test suite:** 1 passed, 17 skipped due to unavailable optional dependencies.
- **Ruff formatting:** Passed.
- **Ruff linting:** Passed.
- **Git whitespace validation:** Passed.

End-to-end video decoding was not tested locally because the relevant optional dependencies were unavailable.

prs.title: Fine-grained FP8: DeepSeek-V4's expert_dtype in the quantization config
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49848)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

**What.** DeepSeek-V4.1 ships `expert_dtype: "fp4"` in its quantization config. V4 sets it on the model config, and that was the only place the FP8 experts read it. So V4.1's FP4 experts were allocated as FP8.

- `FineGrainedFP8Config` gets `expert_dtype` (`"fp8"` by default, or `"fp4"`). `FP8Experts` reads it there.
- `DeepseekV4Config.__post_init__` moves V4's model-config `expert_dtype` into the quantization config. A value the quantization config already ships, as V4.1's does, stays.

Masked expert parallelism for fine-grained FP8 moved to #49852.

**How tested.** The DeepSeek-V4 and fine-grained FP8 suites pass. `test_megamoe_takes_over_the_experts_ep_rule` already fails on main, since it calls `update_tp_plan`, which the quantizer no longer has.

[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49842)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## What does this PR do?

Fixes an out-of-bounds index in `MusicgenMelodySinusoidalPositionalEmbedding` during generation with long conditioning inputs.

The positional table only gets resized when `seq_len > weights.size(0)`, but `past_key_values_length` isn't taken into account. During decoding `seq_len` is 1, so the table never grows. Once `past_len` goes past `max_position_embeddings` (2048), `index_select` goes out of range.

Fix: also count `past_key_values_length` when deciding whether to expand the table.

## Repro

```python
import torch
from transformers import AutoProcessor, MusicgenMelodyForConditionalGeneration

model_id = "facebook/musicgen-melody"
processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id)
model = MusicgenMelodyForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(model_id, dtype=torch.bfloat16).to("xpu")

text = ("Hello, this is a test of the text to speech synthesis system. " * 85).strip()  # 1361 tokens
inputs = processor(text=[text], return_tensors="pt").to("xpu")
audio = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=1024)  # 235 + 1361 + 1024 > 2048 -> crash

prs.title: Fix Qwen4-Exp indexer position cache lifecycle
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49840)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## What does this PR do?

Fixes #49745.

This draft keeps Qwen4-Exp's indexer position history aligned with its cached keys when a cache is reset, cropped, or reordered. I followed the [maintainer's suggested direction](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/49745#issuecomment-6318974443) and moved ownership of that history into the indexed cache layers.

### Why this happens

Qwen4-Exp's QSA indexer needs the full position history to apply positional embeddings to historical key blocks. The model currently builds that history by concatenating the current positions with `past_key_values.position_ids`, an extra attribute attached to the top-level cache.

The cache's lifecycle methods operate on its layers and do not manage that extra attribute. After `reset()`, the layer state is empty, but the next forward still appends positions to the previous request's history. After `crop()`, the history still contains positions for discarded keys. Batch reordering can similarly leave the positions in a different sample order from the keys. When QSA selects among key blocks, these mismatches can affect its selection and the resulting model output.

### How this draft addresses it

I added an optional `indexer_position_ids` field to `DynamicIndexedLayer` and `StaticIndexedLayer`, and updated their existing operations to maintain it:

- Both layers clear the position history on reset and reorder its batch dimension during beam reordering.
- `DynamicIndexedLayer.crop()` removes the corresponding positions from the sequence dimension.
- Dynamic batch repetition and selection apply the same transformation to the position history.
- The field uses `[position_dims, batch_size, seq_len]`, so batch operations act on dimension 1.

The model reads and writes this field on the first indexed layer selected from `config.layer_types`. This matters for hybrid configurations where layer 0 uses linear attention. All Qwen4-Exp indexers consume the same position history, so one copy is sufficient; the model can continue computing the shared positional embeddings once per forward.

This places the state where the existing cache lifecycle dispatch can reach it. The generic `Cache` methods already delegate reset, crop, and batch operations to their layers, so no model-specific handling is needed in those methods.

### Scope

The production changes are limited to `cache_utils.py`, `modular_qwen4_exp.py`, and the regenerated `modeling_qwen4_exp.py`. The existing position concatenation, QSA scoring, and RoPE calculation remain in place. The generic cache classes and public update interfaces are unchanged, and this draft does not add crop support to static caches.

I'm keeping this as a draft to discuss the position-state ownership and the choice to share one history through the first indexed layer.

I used AI assistance for this change, supervised the work throughout, and discussed the diagnosis, scope, and implementation choices.

prs.title: docs(whisper): cast input features to model dtype in AutoModel example
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49837)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

The AutoModel example in `docs/source/en/model_doc/whisper.md` loads `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo` without a `dtype`, so it comes up in float16 (from `config.dtype`), while the feature extractor emits float32. Moving the features only to `model.device` makes `generate` raise:

```
RuntimeError: Input type (float) and bias type (c10::Half) should be the same
```

This casts the features with `input_features.to(model.device, dtype=model.dtype)`, the API recommended in the issue thread. The model side stays as is, as agreed there.

I ran the example block before and after the change: it raises the error above on main and transcribes the sample correctly with the fix.

Fixes #47805

prs.title: [CI] Verify fixed PIL-only import test (transformers-ci#341)
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49835)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## What this does

Temporarily points the `PR CI` workflow at the `fix-pil-only-import-test` branch of `huggingface/transformers-ci` ([PR #341](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers-ci/pull/341)) to validate the fix in CI.

## Background

The `check_repository_consistency` job has 4 backend-isolation import tests. The **"PIL only"** step was silently a no-op: the preceding **"torch only"** step removed Pillow and restored only `.[quality]` (which has no Pillow), so the "PIL only" step ran in an environment **without PIL**. Every vision class became a `DummyObject` placeholder → no crash → false pass.

This is the CI hole that let [#49748](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49748) (`Gemma4UnifiedProcessor` crashing on PIL-only import) slip through undetected.

The fix in transformers-ci#341:
- After the "torch only" step, restores PIL with `uv pip install Pillow -q`  
- Reorders "torch + PIL, no torchvision" before "PIL only" so each step starts from a correct, known state without needing to reinstall torch

## What to check

The `check_repository_consistency` job should pass (since #49748 is already merged). If it passes cleanly, it means:
1. The steps are now correctly sequenced
2. Each step actually tests the intended backend combination

Once transformers-ci#341 is merged, this PR should be **closed/reverted** (the `@main` ref will then include the fix automatically).

<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Fixes #41964 -- Improves typing in the `modeling_rope_utils.py` library

* Converts `config: Optional["PreTrainedConfig"] = None` to `config: "PreTrainedConfig"` in multiple locations where passing `config=None` would have raised an `AttributeError`.
    * `_compute_linear_scaling_rope_parameters`, `_compute_proportional_rope_parameters`, and `_compute_dynamic_ntk_parameters` all immediately dereference `config` and _will fail_ if a config is not provided.
    * None of these functions are called directly outside of this module
    * All calls to these functions are mediated by a call similar to `ROPE_INIT_FUNCTIONS[rope_type](<config, device, ...>)` where a `config` is always passed as the first argument.
* Adds type annotations where possible across the entire file
* Converts `RopeParameters` to `RopeParameters(TypedDict, total=False)`.
    * See the description of #41964 for examples of how using `total=False` can dramatically improve brevity across the codebase.
* Corrects and enhances the docstring for `RopeParameters` to cover more (I think all but who knows if that'll still be true by the time this is actually merged, stuff moves fast these days) RoPE types and configs.
* Adds modeling_rope_utils.py to `utils/check_types.py` to ensure consistency in the future

prs.title: Fix dynamic, yarn and longrope RoPE when config.head_dim is None
prs.body:
# What does this PR do?

`_compute_dynamic_ntk_parameters`, `_compute_yarn_parameters`, `_compute_longrope_parameters` and the longrope validation in `RotaryEmbeddingConfigMixin` read the head dim with `getattr(config, "head_dim", config.hidden_size // config.num_attention_heads)`. Configs that declare `head_dim: int | None = None` (Mixtral, Ministral, MiniMax, HunYuan dense/MoE/VL) always have the attribute, so these paths get `None` and fail with `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'NoneType' and 'float'`.

This switches those four lines to `getattr(config, "head_dim", None) or config.hidden_size // config.num_attention_heads`, the form already used by the default, linear, llama3 and proportional paths in the same file, and adds a regression test in `tests/utils/test_modeling_rope_utils.py` that checks `head_dim=None` gives the same inv_freq as an explicit `head_dim` for dynamic, yarn and longrope.

Tests:
- `pytest tests/utils/test_modeling_rope_utils.py`: 38 passed (the new test fails on main with the `TypeError` above)
- `pytest tests/models/mixtral -k "rope or config"`: 8 passed, 6 skipped
- `pytest tests/models/{llama,phi3,ministral,minimax,hunyuan_v1_dense,hunyuan_v1_moe} -k rope`: 28 passed, 11 skipped, 2 failed (`Phi3ModelTest::test_longrope_compiled_matches_eager_*`, which fail the same way on main on my machine because there is no C++ compiler for inductor)

prs.title: [Fetcher] Fix missing test deps for dynamically-resolved image processors
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49826)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## Problem

Since PR #43514 (multi-backend image processor refactor), \`test_image_processing_*.py\` files no longer statically import their image processor class. Instead, class resolution happens dynamically via \`IMAGE_PROCESSOR_MAPPING_NAMES\` + \`get_image_processor_class_from_name()\` in \`test_image_processing_common.py\`. The fetcher's static import analysis is blind to this, so changes to \`image_processing_<model>.py\` files no longer trigger their tests.

The problem is broader than just \`test_image_processing_*.py\`: \`test_processing_<model>.py\` files are also affected when \`processing_<model>.py\` doesn't statically import its image processor class (e.g. CLIP's \`processing_clip.py\` only imports \`ProcessorMixin\`, has zero deps).

## Fix

Add a naming-convention block in \`create_reverse_dependency_map\` that explicitly wires all \`image_processing*.py\` source files to their corresponding test files, covering two cases:
1. \`test_image_processing_<model>.py\` — uses \`_get_image_processing_classes()\` dynamically
2. \`test_processing_<model>.py\` — uses \`_get_component_class_from_processor()\` dynamically, when \`processing_<model>.py\` itself doesn't statically import the image processor

## Verification

**CI job comparison** — dummy change to \`image_processing_clip.py\` was used:

- **Without fix** — https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/actions/runs/39618040720/job/119283956253
  - Fetcher picked up the change but only triggered \`tests/models/auto/test_image_processing_auto.py\`, \`tests/models/auto/test_processing_auto.py\`, \`tests/models/kosmos2/test_processing_kosmos2.py\`
  - Missing ❌: \`tests/models/clip/test_image_processing_clip.py\` and \`tests/models/clip/test_processing_clip.py\`

- **With fix** — https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/actions/runs/39617414002/job/119281943859
  - Both \`tests/models/clip/test_image_processing_clip.py\` ✅ and \`tests/models/clip/test_processing_clip.py\` ✅ correctly triggered

**Regression test** — run on a real GPU runner (A10G, torch 2.14, Python 3.11):
- `tests/repo_utils/test_tests_fetcher.py::TestFetcherTester::test_image_processor_files_trigger_test_image_processing_and_test_processing`
- ✅ PASSED with fix (25s)
- ❌ FAILED without fix — assertion error showing only auto/kosmos2 tests triggered, clip tests missing

cc @raushan-tiwari

prs.title: Convert numpy scalars inside lists/tuples in to_py_obj
prs.body:
## What

`to_py_obj` is documented to "Convert a PyTorch tensor, Numpy array or python list to a python list." Its list/tuple fast path (added for performance in #36885) accepts `np.number`:

```python
elif isinstance(obj, (list, tuple)):
    if all(isinstance(x, (int, float, np.number)) for x in obj):
        return list(obj)   # numpy scalars pass through unconverted
```

So a list of numpy scalars is returned with the numpy types intact, while a *standalone* numpy scalar is correctly converted via `.tolist()` — the two cases disagree:

```python
to_py_obj([np.float32(1.5), np.int64(2)])   # -> [np.float32(1.5), np.int64(2)]  (bug)
to_py_obj(np.float32(1.5))                  # -> 1.5 (python float)
json.dumps(to_py_obj([np.int64(2)]))        # TypeError: Object of type int64 is not JSON serializable
```

This path is shared by tokenizer `pad`/`decode` and the Whisper, Wav2Vec2 and LUKE tokenizers, so anything passing a list of numpy scalars gets numpy types back.

## Fix

Restrict the fast path to python-native `int`/`float`; numpy scalars fall through to the existing element-wise recursion (which converts them via `.tolist()`):

```python
if all(isinstance(x, (int, float)) for x in obj):
    return list(obj)
```

`np.float64` is a subclass of `float`, so a list of `np.float64` still takes the fast path and is unchanged (it is already JSON-safe). Pure python-scalar lists are unaffected.

## Tests

Adds `tests/utils/test_generic.py::GenericTester::test_to_py_obj_numpy_scalars_in_list` (values + types for a list and a tuple of numpy scalars). Verified fail-on-revert: before the fix the list is returned with numpy types (not JSON-serializable); after, it is `[1.5, 2]` as python float/int. Full `tests/utils/test_generic.py`: 26 passed.

prs.title: Apply EXIF orientation in load_image_as_tensor with torchvision
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49794)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Fixes #49701

`load_image_as_tensor` decodes path, URL and base64 inputs with torchvision's `decode_image`, which ignores the EXIF Orientation tag unless `apply_exif_orientation=True` is passed. A phone JPEG therefore reached the torchvision image processors sideways, while `load_image` and the PIL backend rotate it upright with `exif_transpose`.

This PR binds `apply_exif_orientation=True` to torchvision's `decode_image` in the torchvision branch of `load_image_as_tensor`, so every string input comes back in the upright orientation, as discussed in the issue. The torchcodec branch is unchanged: torchcodec's decoders (0.16.0 and later, the minimum the loader uses) already apply the EXIF orientation for JPEG, PNG and WebP and have no switch for it. The PIL branch already called `exif_transpose`.

The new test `test_load_image_as_tensor_exif_transpose` builds the 40 by 20 JPEG with EXIF Orientation 6 from the issue in a temporary directory and checks that `load_image_as_tensor` on the path, the base64 string, a URL (with `httpx.get` patched to return the file bytes) and a PIL image each gives a `(3, 40, 20)` tensor matching `load_image` within JPEG rounding. Without the fix the path, base64 and URL cases fail with shape `(3, 20, 40)`. With it, the reproduction script from the issue prints `(3, 40, 20)` for both tensor loads and a difference of 0 between the torchvision and PIL image processors.

I ran the test with torchvision 0.29.1. torchcodec could not load its native library on my CPU-only machine, so I checked its behaviour in the torchcodec source rather than by running it.

prs.title: Fix duplicate code_revision when passed through model_kwargs
prs.body:
## Summary

`pipeline()` popped `code_revision` from `kwargs` but also passed it explicitly to `AutoConfig.from_pretrained` while forwarding `model_kwargs`, so `model_kwargs={"code_revision": ...}` raised:

```text
TypeError: transformers.models.auto.configuration_auto.AutoConfig.from_pretrained() got multiple values for keyword argument 'code_revision'
```

Pop it from `model_kwargs` (raising when both spellings are used) and carry it once through `hub_kwargs`, so every loader receives it.

Fixes #49272.

`tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_common.py::test_pipeline_code_revision_in_model_kwargs` builds a tiny local BERT pipeline with `model_kwargs={"code_revision": ...}` and asserts both spellings together raise `ValueError`. Fully offline.

```text
python -m pytest tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_common.py -k code_revision -q

Without the fix the test fails with the duplicate-keyword `TypeError`.

prs.title: Match a skip-list entry from the start only up to a module boundary
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49771)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

**What.** `should_convert_module` matched a skip-list entry with a bare `re.match`, so `"model.layers.1"` also skipped
layers 10 to 19. A match from the start now ends at a module boundary. An entry still covers its sub-tree, a regex
with its own boundary still works, and a name still covers the names ending in it (`"gate"` covers
`shared_expert_gate`).

**Why we need it.** Loading real FP8 checkpoints with the fine-grained FP8 support (#49777) blocked on it.
Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 lists its routers as `mlp.gate`, which also skipped the quantized `mlp.gate_proj`. Its FP8 weight
then reached a bf16 linear. Every quantizer that takes `modules_to_not_convert` uses this function, so main has the
same bug, and any skip-list naming a layer by index hits it too. The key is wrapped in a group so the boundary applies
to every alternative of a key with `|`.

Supersedes #47990, which anchors with `$` and so stops matching regex entries that carry their own boundary, such as
`^model\.audio_tower(?:\.|$)`.

**Behaviour change.** A skip-list entry no longer covers longer siblings (`model.layers.1` vs `model.layers.10`,
`mlp.gate` vs `mlp.gate_proj`).

**Depends on.** main. First PR of the fine-grained stack.

**How tested.** `tests/quantization/test_quantizers_utils.py`, a new general test file. `test_should_convert_module`
moves there from the MXFP4 suite, with the new cases.

The comments and docstrings that say why each change exists are there for readability. Feel free to ask for any of them to go if it's self-evident.

prs.title: Keep explicit processor kwargs in apply_chat_template
prs.body:
# What does this PR do?

`ProcessorMixin.apply_chat_template` treated every kwarg the chat template does not reference as a processor argument. If any such kwarg was present, it replaced the caller's `processor_kwargs`, so `max_length` and `truncation` were dropped. A kwarg that is neither a template variable nor a valid processor argument, such as `enable_thinking` on a template that does not use it, was forwarded to `processor.__call__` and warned about. `tokenizer.apply_chat_template` ignores those kwargs.

Explicit `processor_kwargs` are now kept. Only kwargs that are real processor arguments are forwarded, and they no longer replace the rest of the dict. Anything else is left for the template and otherwise ignored. `SmolVLMProcessor.apply_chat_template` puts its `num_frames` and `fps` defaults in `processor_kwargs` instead of `**kwargs`, so a normal call no longer warns.

Fixes #49760
Fixes #49761
Fixes #49762

prs.title: fix(parsing): decode escaped string delimiters in json content parser
prs.body:
## Problem

The `json` content parser's `string_delims` captures up to the first closing delimiter and never decodes escapes (huggingface/transformers#49674). A template that escapes its delimiter — LFM2.5 renders `'` as `\'` and escapes `\` and newlines — cannot round-trip its own tool-call arguments: `'Saint-Jean-d\'Angély'` is captured as the unparseable `'Saint-Jean-d\'Angély'`, and `'Paris\nFrance'` keeps a literal `\n`.

## Change

Adds an opt-in `string_escape` argument (single character, e.g. `"\\"`). When set, `open_d...close_d` regions are extracted by a character scan that treats `escape + char` as literal (so an escaped closing delimiter does not end the string) and decodes `\n`, `\t`, `\r`, escaped delimiters and the escape character itself; unknown escapes are kept verbatim. Without the option the existing regex path and behavior are unchanged.

Fixes #49674.

## Tests

## Problem

New GPU docker images (Python 3.11 migration, #49311) install packages into a uv-managed venv at `/opt/venv`. The Dockerfile sets `ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:..."`, which CI jobs inherit correctly.

However, interactive SSH sessions start a fresh shell that doesn't source Docker `ENV` variables, so `python3`, `pip`, and `pytest` are not found:

```

bash: pytest: command not found
$ python3 -m pytest
/usr/bin/python3: No module named pytest
```

## Fix

Prepend `/opt/venv/bin` to PATH in the SSH session env setup. Safe for all images: prepending a non-existent directory to PATH is a no-op, so old images without a venv are unaffected.

prs.title: Fix SAM device map offloading
prs.body:
Closes #49739

### What does this PR do?

Fixes the SAM and SAM-HQ device-map offloading issue caused by stale `_no_split_modules` declarations that do not match the concrete vision attention classes instantiated when SDPA is enabled.

The fix updates the no-split declarations to use the enclosing vision layer classes, ensuring compatibility across eager and SDPA attention implementations.

### Motivation

SAM currently declares `SamVisionAttention` in `_no_split_modules`, but the default SDPA implementation instantiates `SamVisionSdpaAttention` instead.

Accelerate matches no-split modules by their concrete class names. When no modules match the declared class names, its memory-balancing logic attempts to compute `max()` over an empty sequence, raising:

```
ValueError: max() arg is an empty sequence
```

SAM-HQ has the same underlying issue with its corresponding attention implementations.

Using the enclosing vision layer classes provides a stable no-split boundary that is independent of the selected attention implementation.

### Changes

| Change | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Fix SAM no-split declaration | Changes `SamVisionAttention` to `SamVisionLayer` |
| Fix SAM-HQ no-split declaration | Changes `SamHQVisionAttention` to `SamHQVisionLayer` |
| Update modular SAM-HQ source | Declares `SamHQVisionLayer` in `SamHQPreTrainedModel` |
| Regenerate SAM-HQ modeling file | Synchronizes the generated implementation with the modular source |

### Testing

- The full SAM modeling test suite passed: 205 passed, 190 skipped.
- All six focused CPU/disk-offload tests passed for `SamVisionModel` and `SamModel`.
- Both `.bin` and safetensors disk-offload tests passed.
- The two model-parallelism tests were skipped because multiple accelerators are required and were unavailable in the local environment.
- `git diff --check` passed.

### Scope

The changes address the no-split module declarations used during Accelerate device-map inference and memory balancing. No changes were made to SAM's attention computation or model weight-loading logic.

### Related issue

Closes #49739

prs.title: fix(cache): clear request position_ids on reset (fixes #49745)
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #49745, following the minimal, locally verified candidate from the issue.

`Qwen4ExpTextModel` stores request-specific `position_ids` on the cache object and concatenates any existing attribute in the next forward (`src/transformers/models/qwen4_exp/modeling_qwen4_exp.py`, lines 1438-1444). `Cache.reset()` only reset the layer tensors, so reusing a reset cache for a new request appended the new positions to the previous request's - with QSA pruning active, the stale prefix changed block selection and the model's logits compared with a fresh cache (up to ~0.03 max logit diff in the issue's deterministic CPU repro, seeds 0/1/2, both `DynamicCache` and `StaticCache`).

## Change (`src/transformers/cache_utils.py`, `Cache.reset()`)

After resetting the layers, delete the cache-level `position_ids` attribute:

- deleted rather than set to `None`, because the model checks `hasattr()` before concatenating and rebuilds the attribute on the next forward;
- runs at reset time for both `DynamicCache` and `StaticCache` (they share this method);
- no cache-length-dependent branch added to any model forward; normal cache continuation keeps accumulating positions as before (the issue verified a reset-and-continue sequence matches a fresh full forward at 1.49e-8 max logits diff).

## Regression tests

- `tests/utils/test_cache_utils.py` (`CacheTest.test_reset_clears_request_position_ids`): `Cache.reset()` removes a manually stored `position_ids` for `DynamicCache` and `StaticCache`, and resetting twice (or without the attribute) does not raise.
- `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_modeling_qwen4_exp.py` (`test_cache_reset_clears_position_ids`): runs the issue's reuse scenario on both cache types - forward, `reset()`, forward again with a 12-token request - and asserts the rebuilt metadata describes the current request only (`position_ids.shape[-1] == 12`).

Red/green: before the fix, after reset+reuse the attribute still exists (3 stale + 12 new = 15 positions), so both assertions fail; with the fix they hold. I don't have torch locally, so the two tests run in CI; the changed files pass `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `py_compile`.

@vaibhavs10 / model owners - since the shared `Cache.reset()` now clears `position_ids`, flagging in case any other model attaches request-scoped attributes and re-reads them across a reset intentionally (the issue says this is the only cache-level attribute store it found; happy to scope the deletion to `Qwen4Exp`'s cache subclass instead if preferred).

prs.title: Fix tests_fetcher backbone step (never worked since introduction)
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49742)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## Bug

`create_reverse_dependency_map()` has a backbone step that is supposed to ensure that when a backbone model (e.g. `modernvbert`) changes, tests for composite models that use it (e.g. `colmodernvbert`) are also fetched.

**This has never worked.** Three bugs, all present from day one:

1. **Wrong key**: `child_file.as_posix()` produces an absolute path; the rest of the system uses repo-relative paths → key is never looked up
2. **Wrong values**: `existing_backbone_files()` returns absolute paths → `reverse_map.get(absolute_path, [])` always returns `[]`
3. **Source files instead of test files**: even with correct paths, only source files were stored; `create_module_to_test_map` filters to `startswith("tests")` → zero tests selected

All three must be fixed together — any two fixes still yields ❌.

## Fix

```python
# Before
reverse_map.setdefault(child_file.as_posix(), []).extend(existing_backbone_files(parent_model))

# After
child_file_posix = child_file.relative_to(PATH_TO_REPO).as_posix()
for parent_file in existing_backbone_files(parent_model):
    parent_file_posix = Path(parent_file).relative_to(PATH_TO_REPO).as_posix()
    reverse_map.setdefault(child_file_posix, []).extend(
        reverse_map.get(parent_file_posix, [])
    )
```

Also fixes `test_multimodal_in_create_reverse_dependency_map`:
- `models_dir` was using an absolute path as a key → lookup always returned empty
- Expected values were source files (`src/`), which `create_module_to_test_map` always discards → the test was never actually verifying that tests get triggered

## Verified

- PR with a real `modernvbert` code change (no `colmodernvbert` change): CI fetcher log shows `colmodernvbert` tests **absent** on broken main → **present** after fix
- Each of the 3 fixes verified independently as necessary on an SSH runner

prs.title: [modular] Extend the "del self.xxx" pattern to match typed assignments
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49735)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

When inheriting form a class `Parent` in modular with an attribute `alpha`:

```
class Parent(nn.Module):

    def __init__(self):
        self.alpha = ...
```

the inheriting class `Children` can get rid of `alpha` by using this pattern:
```
class Children(Parent):

    def __init__(self):
        del self.alpha
```

The code that does checks the parents nodes and matches them to this a node of the form `m.Assign()` and retrieves the target of the assignment. This works well unless alpha is typed:


```
class Parent(nn.Module):

    def __init__(self):
        self.alpha: int = ...
```

then the node is of the form `m.AnnAssign()` and the `del self.alpha` in the `Children` class will be useless.

For instance, this happened to me when trying to inherit from `GlmMoeDsaIndexer` which declares `self.q_lora_rank: int = config.q_lora_rank`. 

To preserve the modular pattern while encouraging type hinting, this PR introduces a little helper `get_assign_target` which returns the assignment target whether it is typed or not.

That helper is also used at another call site where the pattern is exactly the same.

prs.title: Fix SmolVLM inputs_merger when image tokens are not a multiple of patch_size
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49725)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Fixes #49724

#49557 made `get_image_features` return a list of flattened per-sample features, and changed `SmolVLMModel.inputs_merger` to split them into blocks of `self.config.vision_config.patch_size`. That is the pixel patch size of the vision encoder, not the number of image tokens per image, so the forward pass with images fails whenever the number of image tokens per image is not a multiple of it, e.g. `HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM2-2.2B-Instruct` (81 tokens per image, patch size 14):

```
RuntimeError: shape '[-1, 14, 16]' is invalid for input of size 22032
```

With the features already flattened, the block indexing only fills the image tokens in order, so this PR removes `inputs_merger` and merges the image features directly in `forward` with `get_placeholder_mask` + `masked_scatter`, as in llava (also in `ModernVBertModel`, which inherits from `SmolVLMModel`). I did not compute the tokens per image from the config (as suggested in the issue) because the ModernVBert config has no `scale_factor`.

The token/feature count check of `get_placeholder_mask` exposed two test bugs, fixed here: the resize tests set `model.image_token_id` instead of `model.config.image_token_id` (so they ran with 0 image tokens), and the ModernVBert `test_resize_tokens_embeddings` reused the `inputs_dict` mutated by the previous model class.

The tester `image_size` goes from 16 to 24 (9 image tokens per image, patch size 4), so the common tests cover this case: without the fix, 62 SmolVLM tests fail. On the repro from the issue, the logits are identical to v5.20.0.

prs.title: fix(tokenizers): stop treating a missing transformers_version as Mistral
prs.body:
# What does this PR do?

Fixes #49623.

`_patch_mistral_regex` has two non-Mistral early exits, and both are gated on `transformers_version` **existing**:

```python
if transformers_version and version.parse(transformers_version) < version.parse("5.0.0"):
    ...
elif transformers_version and version.parse(transformers_version) >= version.parse("5.0.0"):
    return tokenizer
```

A checkpoint released before that field was written into `config.json` — deberta-v3 and mdeberta-v3, both 2021 — has no such key, so neither branch runs, control reaches `mistral_config_detected = True`, and the tokenizer is treated as Mistral.

The cost is not a stray warning. Following the warning's own advice (`fix_mistral_regex=True`) swaps the `Metaspace` pre-tokenizer for the Mistral `Split` pattern:

```
plain  : ['▁The', '▁quick', '▁brown', '▁fox', '▁jumps', ...]
patched: ['The', ' ', 'quick', ' ', 'brown', ' ', 'fox', ' ', 'jump', 's', ...]
```

Different ids, no exception, nothing to notice.

# What changed

A missing `transformers_version` means "older than the field", not "unknown, so assume Mistral". Treating `None` as `< 5.0.0` lets the existing `model_type` check run for these checkpoints:

```python
if transformers_version is None or version.parse(transformers_version) < version.parse("5.0.0"):
```

| config | behaviour |
|---|---|
| no version, `model_type: deberta-v2` | early exit, no patch |
| no version, `model_type: mistral` | still patched |
| no version, no `model_type` | still patched (conservative) |
| version >= 5.0.0 | early exit (unchanged) |
| remote, `base_model:*mistralai` | still patched (`is_local` guard, unchanged) |

# Tests

`PatchMistralRegexMissingVersionTests` in `tests/tokenization/test_tokenization_fast.py`. Each case is an offline load represented by a temp dir holding only a `config.json` and a `Metaspace` pre-tokenizer:

- `test_missing_version_non_mistral_model_is_not_patched` — fails on `main`, passes here
- `test_missing_version_mistral_model_is_still_patched`
- `test_missing_version_unknown_model_type_stays_conservative`

```
pytest tests/tokenization/test_tokenization_fast.py -k MistralRegex
5 passed (3 new + the 2 existing PatchMistralRegexHubCallTests)
```

I ran the first test against unpatched `main` to confirm it fails there, so it catches the regression rather than just describing current behaviour.

Reproduced on 5.21.0.dev0 / tokenizers 0.23.3 / Python 3.11, macOS, with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`.

Thanks @AmmarHassona for the mdeberta-v3 and Mistral-Nemo checks in the issue.

prs.title: Fix CohereCompass text RoPE to use Qwen3-VL interleaved M-RoPE
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49715)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Restores the text RoPE that `CohereLabs/North-Micro-Vision-Instruct` was trained with. Since v5.17.0, including v5.20.1 and `main`, the model runs with a different RoPE layout, and its outputs degrade to near-chance on image benchmarks.

#48105 rewrote `CohereCompassRotaryEmbedding` with two changes:
- `compute_default_rope_parameters` started pre-rotating `inv_freq` (even indices first, then odd).
- `recomposition_frequencies` started laying the lanes out as contiguous `[h | w | t]` sections.

The class comment says this is the "same mrope interleaving pattern as Qwen3VL", but it isn't equivalent. It changes which frequency each rotary lane gets, even for text-only inputs where all three position axes are equal. Qwen3-VL itself kept the interleaved layout in that PR.

This PR restores the v5.16 behavior:
- plain `inv_freq` in `compute_default_rope_parameters` (the pre-rotation is removed);
- Qwen3-VL's interleaved recomposition in `recomposition_frequencies`, applied per layer type;
- the `[24, 20, 20]` default `mrope_section` that v5.16 and Qwen3-VL use.

The edit is in `modular_cohere_compass.py`; `modeling_cohere_compass.py` is regenerated from it.

## Evidence

The model card pins `transformers==5.16.0`. Results with the same `CohereLabs/North-Micro-Vision-Instruct` weights, in bf16 on 8x B300:
- **AI2D:** the first 200 `AI2D_TEST` questions, greedy decoding, letter-extracted answers.
- **NLL:** teacher-forced on 1,024 tokens of the model card's prose.

| transformers | AI2D (200) | Natural-text NLL ↓ |
|---|---|---|
| v5.16.0 | 57.5% | 3.10 |
| v5.19.0 | 28.5% | 3.57 |
| `main` | 28.5% | 3.57 |
| `main` + this PR | **57.5%** | **3.10** |

Chance on AI2D is 25%. With this PR, `main` reproduces v5.16 exactly.

After the fix, `CohereCompassRotaryEmbedding` (sliding layers) produces cos/sin bit-identical to `Qwen3VLTextRotaryEmbedding` for the same rope parameters. That holds for both 3-D image positions and text positions.

## Tests

- Added `@slow` integration tests on `CohereLabs/North-Micro-Vision-Instruct` (greedy, 30 new tokens):
  - `test_small_model_integration_test`: a single image prompt.
  - `test_small_model_integration_test_batch`: an image prompt and a text-only prompt in one left-padded batch.
  - Expected outputs were recorded on B300 and stored as the default `(None, None)` expectation.
  - On current `main`, without the fix, both fail on the generated text.
- `RUN_SLOW=1 pytest tests/models/cohere_compass/ -k IntegrationTest`: 2 passed. `pytest tests/models/cohere_compass/`: 412 passed, 0 failed on 8x B300 (with flash-attn-4 and nvidia-cutlass-dsl installed).
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` and `utils/check_modular_conversion.py` are clean.

prs.title: Guard eager max_position_embeddings lookup in standardize_rope_params
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`dict.setdefault(key, value)` evaluates `value` **eagerly**. In `standardize_rope_params`, the line

```python
self.rope_parameters.setdefault("original_max_position_embeddings", self.max_position_embeddings)
```

therefore accesses `self.max_position_embeddings` even when `original_max_position_embeddings` is already present in `rope_parameters` and the call would be a no-op. Any config that exposes a scaling rope type (`yarn`/`llama3`/`longrope`) via `rope_parameters` without declaring `max_position_embeddings` at the same level raises `AttributeError` at `__init__` time.

This is not hypothetical: composite (vision-language) configs that copy the text sub-config's `rope_parameters` to the top level — e.g. the `Qwen4ExpConfig` vendored by the community vLLM builds used to serve `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` — crash at config parse time on the official 1M-token YaRN recipe (https://recipes.vllm.ai/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next), because the composite class keeps `max_position_embeddings` in `text_config` only:

```
ERROR Error parsing config for nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local:
'Qwen4ExpConfig' object has no attribute 'max_position_embeddings'
```

## Reproduction

```python
from transformers import PreTrainedConfig

class CompositeLike(PreTrainedConfig):
    model_type = "composite_like"
    def __init__(self, **kw):
        self.rope_parameters = {"rope_type": "yarn", "factor": 4.0,
                                "original_max_position_embeddings": 262144}
        super().__init__(**kw)

CompositeLike()  # AttributeError on main; constructs cleanly with the fix
```

## Fix

```diff
                 else:
-                    self.rope_parameters.setdefault("original_max_position_embeddings", self.max_position_embeddings)
+                    # NOTE: `setdefault` evaluates its second argument eagerly — guard the lookup so
+                    # configs that already carry `original_max_position_embeddings` in `rope_parameters`,
+                    # or composite configs that keep `max_position_embeddings` in a sub-config, do not
+                    # crash here.
+                    if "original_max_position_embeddings" not in self.rope_parameters:
+                        self.rope_parameters["original_max_position_embeddings"] = self.max_position_embeddings
```

Behavior is identical for every config that declares `max_position_embeddings`: key present → no-op (as before); key absent → same read, same `AttributeError` when the value is genuinely required and missing. For configs that already carry `original_max_position_embeddings` in the dict, the crash disappears.

## Proposed test

```python
def test_rope_standardization_without_max_position_embeddings(self):
    # composite configs may carry scaling rope_parameters without declaring
    # max_position_embeddings at the same level (it lives in the sub-config)
    class CompositeLike(PreTrainedConfig):
        model_type = "composite_like"
        def __init__(self, **kwargs):
            self.rope_parameters = {"rope_type": "yarn", "factor": 4.0,
                                    "original_max_position_embeddings": 128}
            super().__init__(**kwargs)

    config = CompositeLike()
    self.assertEqual(config.rope_parameters["original_max_position_embeddings"], 128)
```

Happy to add the test to `tests/test_modeling_rope_utils.py` (or wherever it fits best) on request.

prs.title: Fix grouped RMSNorm in Mamba2 non-fused path
prs.body:
# What does this PR do?

Fixes #49536.

In `Mamba2Mixer`, when executing via the non-fused PyTorch fallback path (CPU, inference evaluation, or environments without `mamba-ssm`/`causal-conv1d` kernels), `self.norm` previously normalized activations across the entire `intermediate_size` dimension, ignoring `n_groups`.

In contrast, the fused Triton kernel (`mamba2_split_conv1d_scan_combined`) receives `ngroups=self.n_groups` and computes RMSNorm within each independent head group of size `intermediate_size // n_groups`. For models configured with `n_groups > 1` (e.g., Mamba2-2.7B with `n_groups=8`), this discrepancy caused activations and generated logits to diverge significantly between fused training and non-fused evaluation.

### Solution
1. Add an optional `group_size=None` parameter to `MambaRMSNormGated.__init__` (defaulting to `hidden_size` if `group_size is None`), matching the existing pattern established in `Zamba2RMSNormGated`.
2. In `MambaRMSNormGated.forward`, reshape `hidden_states` to `(*input_shape[:-1], -1, self.group_size)` prior to calculating variance, and reshape back to `input_shape`.
3. In `Mamba2Mixer.__init__`, pass `group_size = self.intermediate_size // self.n_groups`.
4. Add deterministic CPU regression tests in `tests/models/mamba2/test_modeling_mamba2.py` covering:
   - Grouped normalization matching an independent mathematical reference across 2D, 3D, and 4D tensor layouts and multiple dtypes (`float32`, `float16`, `bfloat16`).
   - Bitwise legacy equivalence when `group_size=None` or `group_size=hidden_size`.
   - Autograd cross-group gradient isolation verifying that $\frac{\partial Y_{\text{group } 0}}{\partial X_{\text{group } k}} \equiv 0$ for $k \ge 1$ (with negative control).
   - Direct CPU non-fused `Mamba2Mixer` forward pass execution with `n_groups=2`.

### Backward & Checkpoint Compatibility
- Existing checkpoint weights (`self.norm.weight`) remain shape `(intermediate_size,)` with identical parameter names and state-dict paths.
- Subclasses such as `BambaRMSNormGated` and `FalconH1RMSNormGated` are unaffected and preserve legacy single-group behavior.

### Test Verification
- **New Regression Suite (`Mamba2RMSNormGatedTest`):** 4/4 tests passed in 0.046s.
- **Core Mamba2 Integration Tests:**
  - `Mamba2ModelTest.test_mamba2_chunked_prefill_cpu`: Passed.
  - `Mamba2ModelTest.test_kwargs_reach_mamba2_mixer`: Passed.
  - `Mamba2ModelTest.test_mamba2_caching`: Passed.
- **Code Quality:** `ruff check` passed cleanly (exit code 0); `git diff --check` passed with 0 whitespace errors.
- *Note:* The full 295-item `test_modeling_mamba2.py` module was not executed in this local environment due to a `pytest`/`pluggy` hook incompatibility (`pytest_configure_node` from `NetworkDebugPlugin` without `pytest-xdist`). All 7 relevant core unit and causal LM integration tests were executed directly via `python -m unittest` and passed.

prs.title: Fix expert-parallel token dispatch gradients on torch 2.7 to 2.10
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49710)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

With `ep_dispatch_experts`, both all-to-all exchanges used `all_to_all_single` from `torch.distributed._functional_collectives`, which has no autograd kernel before torch 2.11. On torch 2.7 to 2.10 training ran without any error, but the expert weights got no gradient and the hidden states got none through the MoE block.

This PR switches the dispatch and combine exchanges to `all_to_all_single_autograd`, which exists on every torch the dispatch check accepts (2.7 and later). The explicit wait on the received rows (kept so the experts get a plain tensor, see #49421) now goes through a small identity-backward `autograd.Function`, because calling `wait_tensor` directly on a tensor that requires grad hits torch's missing-kernel fallback on those versions and logs the "autograd kernel was not registered" deprecation warning.

The new test runs a `Qwen3MoeExperts` (4 experts, top-2) split over two gloo CPU ranks through the dispatch forward, with a different batch per rank, and checks that the expert weight gradients and the hidden-state gradient match an unsharded reference run on both batches, and that no warning is raised. On torch 2.10 it fails before the change with `gate_up_proj.grad` being `None`.

Fixes #49702

## What does this PR do?

Fixes #49622.

### Problem
In `transformers` v5, `DebertaV2Tokenizer` was migrated to `TokenizersBackend`. When loading from a SentencePiece `spm.model` file (e.g., `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("microsoft/deberta-v3-base")`, which has no `tokenizer.json` on the Hub), `SentencePieceExtractor.extract()` extracts `_spm_precompiled_charsmap` from `proto.normalizer_spec.precompiled_charsmap` and passes it in `init_kwargs` to `DebertaV2Tokenizer.__init__`.

However, `DebertaV2Tokenizer.__init__` did not accept `_spm_precompiled_charsmap` (allowing `TokenizersBackend.__init__` to pop and discard it via `**kwargs`) and only added `normalizers.NFC()` to `self._tokenizer.normalizer`. As a result, SentencePiece's precompiled NFKC character map in `microsoft/deberta-v3-*` and `microsoft/mdeberta-v3-*` was silently dropped, causing NFKC-decomposable characters (such as superscripts `⁰`, `¹` or ligatures `ﬁ`) to tokenize as `[UNK]` instead of their normalized equivalents.

### Solution
- Accept `_spm_precompiled_charsmap: bytes | str | None = None` in `DebertaV2Tokenizer.__init__` and append `normalizers.Precompiled(_spm_precompiled_charsmap)` to `list_normalizers` when present (matching `AlbertTokenizer` and `XLNetTokenizer`).

Thank you **@zucchini-nlp** for your kind review on this PR earlier, and I am truly sorry for the noise and frustration this caused.

## What does this PR do?

Fixes #49700.

### Problem
When `generate(..., prefill_chunk_size=K)` is used on a vision-language model (such as `LlavaForConditionalGeneration` or `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration`) whose prompt length exceeds `prefill_chunk_size`:
1. `_get_multimodal_encoder_outputs` precomputes `model_kwargs["mm_encoder_outputs"]` and pops `pixel_values` before the prefill step.
2. Inside `_prefill()` (`src/transformers/generation/utils.py`), each prefill chunk calls `self.prepare_inputs_for_generation(input_chunk, **model_kwargs)` without passing `is_first_iteration`.
3. Because `is_first_iteration` defaults to `False`, `prepare_inputs_for_generation` drops all keys in `MULTIMODAL_INPUTS_TO_DROP_OUTSIDE_PREFILL` (including `mm_encoder_outputs` and `pixel_values`), so no prefill chunk ever receives the visual features and `generate()` silently produces text-only outputs while ignoring the image/video input.
4. Furthermore, when placeholder tokens (e.g., `image_token_id` / `video_token_id`) are distributed across multiple prefill chunks, each chunk expects only the slice of `mm_encoder_outputs[modality].pooler_output` (and `deepstack_features` if present) corresponding to the placeholder tokens present in `input_chunk`.

### Solution
- In `GenerationMixin._prefill`, slice each modality's `pooler_output` (and `deepstack_features` if present) in `mm_encoder_outputs` per batch row according to the number of placeholder tokens in the current `input_chunk` (omitting the modality for chunks with zero placeholder tokens).
- Pass `is_first_iteration` to `self.prepare_inputs_for_generation` during chunked prefill so multimodal encoder outputs are preserved for chunks containing multimodal tokens.

### Verification
- Added `test_chunked_prefill_vision_language_model` in `tests/utils/test_cache_utils.py` verifying that chunked prefill on `LlavaForConditionalGeneration` where image placeholder tokens span multiple prefill chunks produces identical token sequences and logit scores to unchunked prefill, and depends on the image input.

### Credits & Acknowledgments
- Full credit to **@digit50** for reporting #49700, providing the reproduction script, diagnosing that `GenerationMixin._prefill` calls `prepare_inputs_for_generation` without `is_first_iteration` (causing `mm_encoder_outputs` / `pixel_values` to be dropped across prefill chunks), and proposing the `is_first_iteration` fix.
- Also acknowledging **@varunc12502-oss** on #49700 and thanking **@zucchini-nlp** for reviewing and guiding the multimodal chunk-splitting helper design.

prs.title: Preserve `ModelOutput` instances in `move_to_device` during `generate()`
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #49699.

### Problem
When `generate()` is called with input tensors residing on a different device than `self.device`, `move_to_device(model_kwargs, self.device)` is invoked after `_prepare_encoder_decoder_kwargs_for_generation` / `_get_multimodal_encoder_outputs` have populated `model_kwargs["encoder_outputs"]` or `model_kwargs["mm_encoder_outputs"]`.

Because `ModelOutput` inherits from `OrderedDict` (a `dict` subclass), `isinstance(value, dict)` matches `ModelOutput` instances in `move_to_device` (`src/transformers/pytorch_utils.py`) and reconstructs them via a plain dict comprehension `{k: move_to_device(v, device) for k, v in value.items()}`. That strips the `ModelOutput` type and attribute access (`encoder_outputs.last_hidden_state`, `image_outputs.pooler_output`), causing encoder-decoder models (such as `T5ForConditionalGeneration` and `BartForConditionalGeneration`) and vision-language models (such as `LlavaForConditionalGeneration`) to crash with:
```
AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'last_hidden_state'
```
or
```
AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'pooler_output'
```

### Solution
Check `isinstance(value, ModelOutput)` before `isinstance(value, dict)` in `move_to_device()`, shallow-copy the `ModelOutput` instance, and update its items in place so `ModelOutput.__setitem__` keeps both dict entries and dataclass attributes synchronized on the moved tensors.

### Verification
- Added unit test `test_generate_with_inputs_off_model_device_preserves_model_output` in `tests/generation/test_utils.py` covering `move_to_device` on `BaseModelOutput` as well as `generate()` when `input_ids` / `pixel_values` are passed on a device different from `model.device` for both encoder-decoder (`BartForConditionalGeneration`) and multimodal (`LlavaForConditionalGeneration`) models.

### Credits & Acknowledgments
- Full credit to **@digit50** for reporting #49699, providing the standalone CPU reproduction script, pinpointing that `move_to_device` strips `ModelOutput` subclass instances into plain `dict`s during `generate()`, and proposing the container-preserving fix (and thanks to **@Cyrilvallez** for #49731).

prs.title: fix(mask2former): register input_projections as nn.ModuleList (fixes #49698)
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49703)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## Summary

`Mask2FormerTransformerModule` stored `input_projections` in a plain Python list instead of an `nn.ModuleList`, so the input projection layers were never registered as submodules. Their parameters were therefore excluded from `model.parameters()`, optimizers and `state_dict()`, and `model.to(device)` left them on CPU, raising on CUDA:

```text
RuntimeError: Input type (torch.cuda.FloatTensor) and weight type (torch.FloatTensor) should be the same
```

Fixes #49698.

## Change

- `src/transformers/models/mask2former/modeling_mask2former.py`: `self.input_projections = []` → `self.input_projections = nn.ModuleList()`. All uses (append, indexing in forward, iteration in `_init_weights`) work unchanged with `nn.ModuleList`.

This matches:
- the sibling `Mask2FormerPixelDecoder`, which already builds the same structure with `nn.ModuleList` (`src/transformers/models/mask2former/modeling_mask2former.py`, lines 1266-1276), and
- the original Meta implementation (https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former/blob/main/mask2former/modeling/transformer_decoder/mask2former_transformer_decoder.py#L323).

Both branches of the projection construction (`nn.Conv2d` and the `nn.Sequential()` identity path) are handled: `nn.ModuleList()` starts empty, registration happens on append, and identity layers register no parameters, same as the pixel decoder.

## Regression test

Added to `Mask2FormerModelTest`:

- `test_input_projections_are_registered_modules` builds a tiny `Mask2FormerModel` / `Mask2FormerForUniversalSegmentation` with `enforce_input_projection=True` and asserts that `.input_projections.` parameters appear in `model.state_dict()` / `model.named_parameters()`.

Red/green: with the old code the key list is empty (the assertion fails, matching the unregistered-parameter count in the issue); with the fix the Conv2d weights and biases are present. I don't have torch on this machine, so the test runs in CI; the model change is verified with `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `py_compile`.

prs.title: Fix encoder logits processors when precomputed encoder_outputs lack token IDs
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49696)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## What does this PR do?

Fixes #49695

### Problem

When an encoder-decoder model is called with precomputed `encoder_outputs` but without the original encoder `input_ids`, generation creates dummy input IDs containing `-100`.

These dummy IDs can incorrectly pass the shape checks for encoder-side logits processors.

- `encoder_repetition_penalty` can crash with an out-of-bounds index error.
- `encoder_no_repeat_ngram_size` can operate on invalid dummy IDs without issuing the expected warning.

### Solution

Check that encoder input IDs do not contain negative sentinel values before initializing these logits processors. When valid source token IDs are unavailable, the processors are skipped and the existing warning behavior is used.

The check is evaluated only when one of the relevant encoder-side constraints is configured.

### Tests

- Added regression coverage for both encoder-side constraints when `encoder_outputs` are provided without `input_ids`.
- Verified that generation completes and emits the expected warnings.
- Added a control case with the original `input_ids` supplied.
- The targeted regression test passes.
- Ruff linting and formatting checks pass.

prs.title: Fix multi-zoom crops in the SAM mask-generation pipeline and related bugs (Fixes #35530)
prs.body: [![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49689) # Fix multi-zoom crops in the SAM mask-generation pipeline and related bugs Fixes #35530 and related previously undiagnosed issues. SAM, SAM-HQ, SAM2 and SAM3 use a `mask-generation` pipeline that has a parameter `crops_n_layers`. It adds zoom levels to the image to segment smaller details. E.g. with `crops_n_layers=1` they separate the image into 4 smaller images that overlap slightly and then segment the smaller images. Then the segmentation masks are put back in the full image. SAM and related models generally perform worse on small detail without this feature. All the logic surrounding this parameter has been broken since #22840 I detected 5 problems that this PR fixes: 1) Crops have different shapes. `torch.stack` tries to stack them and crashes. This issue is a result of #39385 + #41388 2) The pipeline treats 5 crops as 1 image as per #35530. It sent all the points in a single batch which crashed with "Got 5 and 1" error. Now it runs one crop/subimage at a time. 3) The pipeline the SAM family of models uses put point anchors uniformly around the image to serve as queries, whether or not there's an object there to be segmented. The calculation of these points was broken for cropped images (was based on the uncropped image). Result of #22840 4) Crop boxes have their coordinates in float. `_pad_masks` relies on them being integer and crashes when all other issues are solved. 5) Boxes of masks were returned in their crop coordinate space instead of the global one. Additionally: - crops_n_layers=0 gives identical output to main, 2 tests were implemented to cover the pipeline and image processor modifications. Both tests fail on main, pass on this PR's branch. - `pytest tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_mask_generation.py` - `tests/models/sam/test_image_processing_sam.py` - Since the fix requires images to be processed one after another, I detected 4% longer runtime for the feature extraction on CPU. (only when crops_n_layers > 0, which was broken before) #35627 proposed a similar fix, but it's incomplete and stale (wasn't updated in more than a year after the last reviewer's comments about the crash). It has a similar approach to the crop loop and fixing the float coordinate issue. ## LLM usage - [x] (First-time contributors only): I confirm that this PR description and code is not written by an LLM or code agent All the code in this PR is artisanal and hand-crafted by a human to ensure compliance with the code agent policy. Agents were used to track the issue, critique the code, this PR, and find similar PRs and to summarize the documentation of the repo. I also used agents to generate the illustrations for this pr. ## Who can review? @Rocketknight1 @molbap ## Before submitting - [ ] This PR fixes a typo or improves the docs. - [x] Did you read the contributor guideline and the PR checks? - [x] Was this discussed/approved via a Github issue? prs.title: Fix zero expert gradients in bfloat16 with expert parallelism and ep_size < fsdp_size
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49688)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

Fixes #49687

With token dispatch and `tp_size < ep_size < fsdp_size * tp_size`, the experts' gradient divide factor (`fsdp_size`) is not their FSDP group size, so FSDP2 reduces them with NCCL `PREMUL_SUM`, which returns zeros in bfloat16 up to torch 2.13 (pytorch/pytorch#190747). The experts never train. The expert modules now always sum and divide locally, as they already did on non-NCCL backends.

- Repro from the issue (4 B300s, torch 2.13.0): bfloat16 expert grad norm 0.0000 on main, 0.0889 here (0.0887 in float32).
- New `test_fsdp2_expert_parallel_bf16_expert_grads` (4 GPUs, `fsdp_size=4, ep_size=2`, bfloat16): each expert gradient norm matches the whole batch on one device.

prs.title: Add ColUltraVBERT
prs.body:
Adds ColUltraVBERT (`colultravbert`), a 254M-parameter late-interaction retriever for visual documents fine-tuned from
UltraVBERT. Each page and query token becomes a 128-dimensional L2-normalized vector, and
`ColUltraVBertProcessor.score_retrieval` scores pages against queries by MaxSim.

Checkpoint: [athrael-soju/ColUltraVBERT](https://huggingface.co/athrael-soju/ColUltraVBERT)

Depends on #49685, which adds `ultravbert`. This branch carries its commits; the ColUltraVBERT changes are
the last three.

`modular_colultravbert.py` builds on `colmodernvbert`:

- `ColUltraVBertConfig` holds an `UltraVBertConfig` as `vlm_config` and `embedding_dim`.
- `ColUltraVBertForRetrieval` puts ColModernVBERT's retrieval head on `UltraVBertModel`.
- `ColUltraVBertProcessor` uses ColModernVBERT's `process_images`, `process_queries` and `score_retrieval`, with a
  visual prompt that omits the begin-of-text token, which the UltraBERT tokenizer adds itself.
- Auto mappings for the config, the processor and `AutoModelForRetrieval`, model doc page and tests.

Tests in `tests/models/colultravbert`: model and processor tests, and a slow integration test that scores two queries

`test_sdpa_can_dispatch_on_flash` is skipped, as in `ultrabert`.

The checkpoint's embeddings match the training implementation at a per-token cosine of at least 0.9999998 in float32.
In bfloat16, ViDoRe nDCG@5 on DocVQA, TabFQuAD and InfoVQA is within 0.002 of it.

prs.title: Avoid a host-to-device copy in `eager_mask`
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49684)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

`eager_mask` builds the zero in its `torch.where` with `torch.tensor(0.0, device=mask.device, dtype=dtype)`. That copies a CPU scalar to the device, which blocks the host on every eager mask creation. This uses `torch.zeros((), device=mask.device, dtype=dtype)`, which fills on the device instead. The resulting mask is unchanged.

This became visible with #49404, which made the Gemma 4 audio encoder eager-only, so its mask now always goes through `eager_mask`. vLLM runs its tests with CUDA sync detection enabled, and Gemma 4 audio started failing on Transformers 5.20 (vllm-project/vllm#61983).

Checked on 1x B200 with `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")`:

| | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `eager_mask` (bf16, padded batch) | sync error | no sync |
| `Gemma4AudioModel` forward (random init, padded batch) | sync error | no sync |

The `eager_mask` output matches a reference mask, and the Gemma 4 audio tower output is bitwise identical to `main`. `tests/utils/test_masking_utils.py` passes (11 passed, 2 skipped).

Performance, on the same hardware: `Gemma4AudioModel`, random init, bf16, batch of 8 x 30 s clips (3000 frames), half padded. Medians over two runs each, which agreed closely:

| | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Forward, synced wall time | 30.40 ms | 30.16 ms |
| Host time to enqueue the forward behind ~8 ms of queued GPU work | 28.1 ms | 24.6 ms |
| `eager_mask` alone, idle GPU | 117 µs | 107 µs |

The forward gets about 1% faster. The bigger effect is on the host: the sync makes the host wait for already-queued GPU work to drain, which blocks CPU/GPU overlap. That stall grows with the depth of the queue.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this PR.

prs.title: Keep find_unused_parameters on with non-reentrant gradient checkpointing
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49682)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

Fixes #49443.

When `ddp_find_unused_parameters` is unset, `Trainer` turns it off under any gradient checkpointing (#4659). Only reentrant checkpointing needs that, and the default is now `use_reentrant=False`, so a model with unused parameters, like a VLM trained on text only, crashes under DDP with default arguments. This keeps it on unless checkpointing is reentrant.

- Reentrant is resolved like `train()` and `gradient_checkpointing_enable` do: no kwargs means non-reentrant, kwargs without `use_reentrant` fall back to torch's reentrant default, and legacy `_set_gradient_checkpointing(module, value)` models ignore the kwargs.
- #49443's repro (Qwen3.5-0.8B, 2x H100): main fails on both ranks with `Expected to have finished reduction in the prior iteration`, this branch trains. The new test fails on main.

prs.title: Fix/gemma4 tool names response template
prs.body:
# What does this PR do?

This PR addresses an issue in Gemma 4 tool-call parsing where valid tool names containing hyphens (`-`) or dots (`.`) may be incorrectly truncated.

### Problem

The existing Gemma 4 response-template regex uses `\w+` to capture tool names. However, this pattern only matches word characters, including letters, digits, and underscores. As a result, valid tool names containing other characters, such as hyphens or dots, are not captured completely.

For example:
- `get_weather` is parsed correctly.
- `get-weather` may be truncated to `get`.
- `weather.lookup` may be truncated to `weather`.

This can cause the parsed tool-call name to differ from the original function name, potentially preventing the intended tool from being resolved or invoked correctly.

### Changes

This PR updates the Gemma 4 tool-call matching pattern in the following locations:

- **Serving fallback template** (`src/transformers/cli/serving/utils.py`): Updates the regex used to parse Gemma 4 tool calls when the serving fallback template is selected.
- **Weight-conversion script** (`src/transformers/models/gemma4/convert_gemma4_weights.py`): Applies the corresponding regex update to the template generated during Gemma 4 weight conversion.
- **Regression test** (`tests/cli/test_serve.py`): Adds a test covering tool names with underscores, hyphens, and dots.

The updated pattern captures the tool name up to the argument delimiter, whitespace, or a relevant token boundary, rather than stopping at the first hyphen or dot.

### Testing

The new regression test checks that the parser preserves the complete tool name and correctly parses the associated arguments for examples such as `get_weather`, `get-weather`, and `weather.lookup`.

A separate matcher-level smoke test was also performed for these three examples, and all three passed. However, the full Transformers test suite has not yet been executed locally, so the official test results remain to be verified by the project's CI.

### Scope and compatibility

This change is intended to preserve existing behavior for tool names that use underscores while supporting names containing hyphens and dots.

Existing Gemma 4 tokenizer configurations published on the Hugging Face Hub may contain their own response templates. Those external configurations are not modified by this PR and may require separate updates if they contain the same regex limitation.

**Related issue:** #49422

prs.title: Load tokenizer.json once in TokenizersBackend (2-2.9x faster AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained)
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49667)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Fixes #49666

For tokenizers that load through `TokenizersBackend` (every Hub repo with `tokenizer_class: PreTrainedTokenizerFast`, e.g. Llama 3, GLM-4.x, Granite, OLMo-2), `convert_to_native_format` builds the Rust tokenizer with `TokenizerFast.from_file` and passes it as `tokenizer_object`. `__init__` then runs `copy.deepcopy(tokenizer_object)`, which pickles and re-parses the whole backend. On Llama 3 that copy is 0.46 s of a 0.75 s load.

The object is created internally, so the copy protects nothing. This passes `tokenizer_file` instead, and `__init__` loads it through its existing `from_file` branch. A user passing `tokenizer_object=` still gets a copy.

`AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained` from the local cache, median of 7 fresh processes (best of 5 warm loads each), Apple M5:

| tokenizer | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct | 646 ms | 224 ms |
| GLM-4.5-Air | 850 ms | 397 ms |
| OLMo-2-1124-7B-Instruct | 303 ms | 140 ms |
| granite-3.3-8b-instruct | 136 ms | 64 ms |
| Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 | 139 ms | 58 ms |

The serialized backend, `init_kwargs`, added tokens, encodings (ids, masks, special tokens mask), decode output, chat template output and every file written by `save_pretrained` are byte-identical before and after for these tokenizers and Qwen2.5. `tests/tokenization/` and the `tests/models/{auto,moshi,qwen3_5}` tokenization tests pass; `test_tokenization_class_priority` in `test_tokenization_auto.py` fails the same way on main. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean.

I used an AI coding assistant to help profile and benchmark this; I reviewed the change and ran the tests myself.
