prs.title: [Qwen3-VL] Bound vision RoPE inference FP32 intermediates
prs.body:
# What does this PR do?

The Qwen3-VL vision RoPE helper converts the entire concatenated Q/K sequence to FP32 and builds full-sequence FP32 products before restoring the input dtype. For long image/video inputs, those temporary tensors grow with the total number of visual tokens.

For the standard `(tokens, heads, head_dim)` layout under `no_grad`, process sequences longer than 4096 rows in chunks and write the results into output tensors with the original dtypes. Each chunk keeps the existing FP32 arithmetic and elementwise operation order. The dense path remains for gradient-enabled execution, short sequences, and other broadcast layouts.

The change is defined in the Qwen3-VL modular source. Regenerated copies also update Qwen3-VL-MoE, Qwen3.5, Qwen3.5-MoE, Qwen3-Omni-MoE, Qwen4-Exp, and Cohere-Compass; their helper implementation is identical. No new dependency is required.

## Validation

- Ran the new `Qwen3VLVisionRotaryEmbeddingTest` class in isolation on CPU with real PyTorch 2.14 and the modified repository module: exact output equality against the unchanged dense Qwen2-VL helper for FP16/BF16, contiguous/noncontiguous inputs, and lengths 4095/4096/4097; gradient equality for the dense training fallback; and FP32 intermediate tensor row bounds through `TorchDispatchMode`.
- The scratch-bound regression fails against the helper extracted from the fixed base commit and passes with this change.
- `torch.compile(..., backend="eager", fullgraph=True, dynamic=True)` captures the changed helper for lengths 4097 and 8193 and matches dense outputs. This checks Dynamo fullgraph capture only; Inductor/CUDA were not tested.
- Regenerated the modular dependency graph and checked that generated changes are confined to the RoPE helper. Focused Ruff lint/format checks pass for the changed files.

The repository command for these tests is `pytest tests/models/qwen3_vl/test_modeling_qwen3_vl.py -k Qwen3VLVisionRotaryEmbeddingTest`. It was not fully collected in this partial local checkout because unrelated test imports were unavailable; the new unit class was executed directly from that test file. `make style` was attempted but its repository-wide targets include absent directories in this partial checkout. No GPU peak-memory, latency, encoder/model integration (including the derived models), or CUDA backend results are claimed. This is a draft pending those checks and author review.

Related work checked: #48105 changes rotary frequency layout, and #47703 changes control-tensor synchronization; neither implements this row-chunked helper.

## Code Agent Policy

This draft and its code were prepared with a code agent at the author's explicit request. The author has not yet reviewed this new diff line by line or personally run the reported checks. No maintainer approval is claimed.

- [ ] Discussed/approved via a GitHub issue or forum thread.
- [x] Added focused regression coverage for the changed helper.
- [ ] Author review and GPU/model integration validation completed.

prs.title: Defer some imports
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49663)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

Fixes #49378

## What

Loading a config or tokenizer pulled in the generation stack and scikit-learn through module-level imports that only matter once a model generates, uses a watermark, or loads a GGUF file. This moves them to first use:

- `generation/configuration_utils.py`: `WatermarkLogitsProcessor` / `SynthIDTextWatermarkLogitsProcessor` now import inside `construct_processor` (type hint kept under `TYPE_CHECKING`).
- `models/auto/auto_factory.py`: `GenerationMixin` imports inside `add_generation_mixin_to_remote_model`, the only place it is used.
- `generation/candidate_generator.py`: `sklearn.metrics.roc_curve` imports where the ROC threshold is computed. The `is_sklearn_available()` check is unchanged.
- `configuration_utils.py`, `models/auto/tokenization_auto.py`: `load_gguf_checkpoint` imports in the GGUF branch only.

No behavior change for code that uses these features.

## Numbers

`AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B")` and `AutoConfig.for_model("llama")`, fresh process each, warm cache, offline, 6 interleaved runs, median wall time:

| | main (683b721) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| tokenizer | 7.6 s, sklearn imported | 4.7 s, sklearn not imported |
| config (llama) | 6.8 s, sklearn imported | 5.4 s, sklearn not imported |

`-X importtime` on main: `auto_factory` 2.9 s cumulative, of which `candidate_generator` -> `sklearn.metrics` 1.5 s. With this PR `auto_factory` is 1 ms.

Old, slow box: Intel i5-2430M (2011, 4 threads), Python 3.12.13, torch 2.14.1+cpu, scikit-learn 1.9.1, tokenizers 0.23.2. Absolute times will be much lower on modern hardware; the ratio is what matters.

## Not in this PR: torch itself

torch is still imported when available. On current main it comes in through other module-level imports on the config path, e.g. `modeling_rope_utils.py:28` and `utils/type_validators.py:17-19` (which imports `ACT2FN` from `activations`). The `type_validators` -> `activations` -> `integrations/hub_kernels` -> `integrations/flash_attention` -> `generation.continuous_batching` chain also still loads `generation.logits_process` for model configs like llama. Removing those touches a lot more modules, so I'd keep it for a follow-up if you want it. (My earlier comment on the issue said torch stays out; that was inaccurate.)

## Tests

- `tests/utils/test_import_utils.py`: new subprocess test that importing `AutoConfig`/`AutoTokenizer` and building a `PreTrainedConfig` leaves `sklearn`, `generation.logits_process`, `generation.candidate_generator` and `modeling_gguf_pytorch_utils` out of `sys.modules`, and that `AutoConfig.for_model("llama")` leaves `sklearn`, `candidate_generator` and the gguf loader out. Fails on main, passes here.
- First-use tests: both watermark configs still construct their processors, and `AssistedCandidateGenerator.update_candidate_strategy` still reaches `roc_curve` and updates the threshold (skipped without sklearn).
- Ran: `tests/utils/test_import_utils.py` 168 passed; `tests/generation/test_watermarking.py` + `test_candidate_generator.py` 37 passed; `test_logits_process.py -k "atermark or SynthID"` 12 passed; `test_configuration_utils.py -k "atermark or SynthID"` 1 passed; `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` (0.14.10) clean; `utils/check_dummies.py`, `check_inits.py`, `check_import_complexity.py` clean.
- Not run locally: GGUF loading tests (`tests/quantization/ggml`, need `gguf` and large downloads). The GGUF change is only moving the import into the branch that calls it.

cc @ArthurZucker @itazap

AI disclosure: I used Claude Code to write the change and tests; I reviewed the diff and the measurements.

Kolibri-1 was introduced in #49463 but the integration tests comparing logits was deactivating on ROCm because it was failing with the CUDA defaults.

```
vllm serve Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
```

prs.title: fix(tokenizers): do not assume missing transformers_version is Mistral
prs.body:
## Problem

In `_patch_mistral_regex`, the non-Mistral early return was guarded by:
```python
if transformers_version and version.parse(transformers_version) < version.parse("5.0.0"):
```
When an older local model config (such as `microsoft/deberta-v3-base`) has no `transformers_version` key, `transformers_version` is `None`. As a result, neither version comparison branch executed, and control fell through to `mistral_config_detected = True` (see #49623).

This caused `_patch_mistral_regex` to emit a false-positive Mistral warning on local non-Mistral models with large vocabulary sizes, and applying `fix_mistral_regex=True` altered their tokenization behavior.

## Solution

Update the condition to:
```python
if transformers_version is None or version.parse(transformers_version) < version.parse("5.0.0"):
```
This ensures older local models without a `transformers_version` in their `config.json` correctly evaluate the `transformers_model_type` check and bypass Mistral regex patching.

Fixes #49623

prs.body:

[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49657)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Second half of #49651. After #49652, `from_pretrained` works again on torch 2.7, but tensor-parallel loading still raises on both declared-floor versions:

```
AttributeError: type object 'Shard' has no attribute 'local_shard_size_and_offset'
```

`sharding_utils.py` aliases `Shard._local_shard_size_and_offset`, which only exists from torch 2.8. torch 2.6 and 2.7 expose the same computation as `Shard._local_shard_size_on_dim(size, num_chunks, rank, return_offset=True)` (checked: identical results for the same inputs), so this falls back to that when the newer name is missing.

`tests/utils/test_distributed_sharding_utils.py` (CPU, no GPU needed):

| torch | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 2.6.0 | 23 failed, 5 passed | 3 failed, 11 passed |
| 2.8.0 | 3 failed, 11 passed | unchanged |
| 2.14.1 | 14 passed | unchanged |

The 3 remaining failures on 2.6 are the `_StridedShard` cases, which also fail on 2.8 and 2.9 and only pass on recent torch, so they are not introduced here. If you would rather move `setup.py` to `torch>=2.8` instead, happy to turn this into that change.

prs.title: [CB] Various small fixes for MPS
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49654)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

This PR aims to fix a few things for CB when running on MPS:
- when a user runs continuous batching on an MPS device with torch < 2.14, throw a warning. The reason why is that before 2.14, torch had a few issues on MPS when using `index_select` and when allocating tensors, which are critical parts of CB.
- make the CB benchmark_overall script runnable on MPS by adding a `if torch.cuda.is_available()` for a CUDA-specific branch
- fix an issue where an empty decode compile config was created even though the decode fast path isnt available (always the case on MPS)
- lower the `max_memory_percent` automatic default from 0.9 to 0.6 on MPS, because RAM and VRAM are shared, and too much allocated memory for torch will force macOS to use swap -> bad performance 

This results in a throughput for Qwen 2.5 coder on M5 going from 7 tok/s to 137 tok/s

prs.title: Keep `enable_expert_parallel=True` expert-parallel only, as before v5.19
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49634)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Fixes #49628.

Up to v5.18, `DistributedConfig(tp_size=N, enable_expert_parallel=True)` applied the EP plan *instead of* the TP plan: only the experts were sharded, and attention stayed replicated. Since v5.19 the flag is a deprecated alias for `ep_size=tp_size`, which applies the TP plan next to the EP plan. So the same code now TP-shards attention, and models with fewer KV heads than ranks (Gemma 4, Qwen3.5/3.6-MoE, Qwen3-Coder-Next, ...) crash where they used to load.

- The alias now also sets `tp_plan={}`, so it keeps its pre-v5.19 meaning until it's removed in v5.20. The `FutureWarning` points to `ep_size=N, tp_plan={}`, or to dropping `tp_plan` to also shard the dense modules.
- `tp_plan={}` in `DistributedConfig` applies none of the model's TP rules. The `tp_size` ranks still form the group that shares each batch, which masking and all-reduce needs. Other `tp_plan` dicts still override individual rules as before, and `ep_plan` is unchanged.
- Docs: the expert-parallelism page shows `tp_plan={}` for models whose attention can't be split, and the alias tip says what it really does.

Checked on 4 CPU ranks:

| model | config | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| tiny Qwen3-MoE (issue repro) | `tp_size=4, enable_expert_parallel=True` | crash in the attention view | attention replicated, experts 1 of 4 per rank; same logits as v5.18 |
| tiny Gemma 4 (2 KV heads, 8 experts) | `tp_size=4, enable_expert_parallel=True` | crash | attention replicated, 2 of 8 experts per rank; logits match a single process to 3e-7 |
| both | `tp_size=4, ep_size=4` | crash | crash (TP+EP as requested: 2 KV heads can't be split 4 ways) |

A new unit test covers the alias (empty TP plan, experts still sharded) and the explicit `ep_size` case (TP plan kept).

prs.title: Fix MusicGen forward(labels=...) failing when decoder_start_token_id is None
prs.body:
Fixes #49095

## What does this PR do?

`MusicgenForConditionalGeneration.forward(labels=...)` raises `ValueError: Make sure to set the decoder_start_token_id attribute of the model's configuration` on the released checkpoints (e.g. `facebook/musicgen-small`). These checkpoints ship `decoder.decoder_start_token_id = null` and rely on `bos_token_id` instead.

Other code paths already handle this correctly: `prepare_decoder_input_ids_from_labels`, `generate()` and `musicgen_melody` all fall back to `bos_token_id`. Only `forward(labels=...)` read the field that is `None`.

## Fix

In `modeling_musicgen.py`, `forward` now falls back to `config.decoder.bos_token_id` when `decoder_start_token_id` is `None`, matching the existing convention. No other call sites are changed.

## Tests

Added `MusicgenTest::test_forward_with_labels_without_decoder_start_token_id` in `tests/models/musicgen/test_modeling_musicgen.py`. It sets `decoder_start_token_id = None` and checks that `forward(labels=...)` returns a loss. It fails before the fix with the `ValueError` above and passes after.

- [x] This was discussed in the issue (#49095).
- [x] I wrote a new test for this fix.

prs.title: fix(import): lazy packages_distributions to cut 1-3s import cost
prs.body:
## Summary
`src/transformers/utils/import_utils.py` built `PACKAGE_DISTRIBUTION_MAPPING = importlib.metadata.packages_distributions()` at module import. Since torch 2.14 no longer ships `top_level.txt`, stdlib infers top-level names from RECORD files (~14.7k lines for torch), costing 1-3s of every `import transformers` (measured 1.1-1.45s for the call alone, 1.9s of 3.8s import in #49591).

This PR makes the mapping lazy and cached:
- `src/transformers/utils/import_utils.py`: replace eager module-level dict with `@functools.cache _cached_packages_distributions()` + `get_package_distribution_mapping()` accessor, plus module `__getattr__` so `from transformers.utils.import_utils import PACKAGE_DISTRIBUTION_MAPPING` keeps working (pays cost only on access, not on import). Internal uses (`_candidate_distribution_names`, `is_flash_attn_{2,3,4}_available`, `is_flash_attn_greater_or_equal`) now go through the accessor. Respects test patches that set `PACKAGE_DISTRIBUTION_MAPPING` directly.
- `src/transformers/modeling_flash_attention_utils.py`: import the accessor instead of the dict; 3 `pkg_availability_check` lambdas now call it lazily.

## Test plan
- `python -m py_compile` on both files: OK.
- `ruff check --select F,E9`: All checks passed (one pre-existing `if-exp` lint in `_LazyModule` untouched).
- `ruff format --check`: clean after formatting.
- Isolated lazy/patch-compat check: import does not populate `PACKAGE_DISTRIBUTION_MAPPING` in module `__dict__`; `get_package_distribution_mapping()` and `__getattr__` return same cached object; `unittest.mock.patch(...PACKAGE_DISTRIBUTION_MAPPING, {...})` (as used in `tests/utils/test_import_utils.py`) is respected.
- Full `tests/utils/test_import_utils.py` not run locally (needs torch + full dev env); relying on CI. Change is small (38+/10- across 2 files) and preserves existing patch points.

Closes https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/49591
prs.author: Omarinho12345

prs.title: Fa packed sequence decode
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49610)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

This PR updates the `_is_packed_sequence` check that is used for FA. We return early when we are decoding as we know that the sequence is not packed in this case. This helps with speed as we don't sync again due to `(increasing_position_sequences - position_ids).abs().sum().bool()`. 

This was discovered when testing the `metal-flash-sdpa` attn on mac but it seems that it is also relevant for cuda.


### Testing

Qwen2.5-0.5B, bf16, `kernels-community/flash-attn2`, batch size 1, greedy, 256 new tokens, 1×H100:

```
  |           | tokens/s       |
  |-----------|----------------|
  | main      | 35.6           |
  | this PR   | 39.5 (+11%)    |

```
 <details>
  <summary>Benchmark script</summary>

Run with `python bench.py kernels-community/flash-attn2`.

```python 
  import sys, time
  import torch
  import transformers.modeling_flash_attention_utils as fau
  from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

  attn, model_id = sys.argv[1], "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct"
  tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
  model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, dtype=torch.bfloat16, attn_implementation=attn, device_map="cuda")
  inputs = tokenizer("Write a long story about a dragon who learns to code.", return_tensors="pt").to("cuda")

  branch = fau._is_packed_sequence


  def main_version(position_ids, batch_size):  # `_is_packed_sequence` on main
      if position_ids is None:
          return False
      increasing_position_sequences = torch.arange(position_ids.shape[1], device=position_ids.device) + position_ids.min()
      return batch_size == 1 and (increasing_position_sequences - position_ids).abs().sum().bool() 


  calls = {"total": 0, "decode": 0}


  def counted(fn):
      def wrapper(position_ids, batch_size):
          calls["total"] += 1
          calls["decode"] += position_ids is not None and position_ids.shape[-1] == 1
          return fn(position_ids, batch_size)
      return wrapper


  new_tokens = 256
  results = {}
  for name, fn in [("main", main_version), ("branch", branch)] * 3:
      fau._is_packed_sequence = counted(fn)
      calls.update(total=0, decode=0)
      torch.cuda.synchronize(); start = time.perf_counter()
      out = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=new_tokens, min_new_tokens=new_tokens, do_sample=False)
      torch.cuda.synchronize()
      results.setdefault(name, []).append(new_tokens / (time.perf_counter() - start))
      results[name + "_out"] = out
  print(f"{attn}: _is_packed_sequence calls per generate: {calls['total']} ({calls['decode']} in decode)")
  for name in ["main", "branch"]:
      print(f"  {name:6s} tokens/s: {max(results[name]):.1f} (runs: {', '.join(f'{r:.1f}' for r in results[name])})")
  print("  same generated tokens:", torch.equal(results["main_out"], results["branch_out"]))
```

</details>
prs.author: SunMarc

On ROCm without the `flash-attn` package, `attn_implementation="flash_attention_2"` falls back to `kernels-community/flash-attn2`, which has no ROCm build, so loading the model fails with `the package for FlashAttention2 doesn't seem to be installed`.

This PR makes `flash_attention_2` fall back to `kernels-community/aiter-flash-attn` on ROCm, as `flash_attention_3` already does. The `flash-attn` package is still preferred when it is installed, and nothing changes on CUDA or XPU.

### Tests (MI300X, ROCm 7.2)

- `test_kernels_fallback` fails on `main` and passes with this PR.
- Qwen2.5-0.5B in bf16, FA2 compared with SDPA: logits differ by about 1% and gradients by about 3% (relative), on both padded and unpadded batches, with no NaNs. Greedy generation gives the same tokens as eager attention.

prs.title: Build docs with the Python version from .python-version
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49603)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

The doc-builder reusable workflows (`build_pr_documentation.yml`, `build_main_documentation.yml`) run on `ubuntu-22.04` and, without the `python_version` input, create the build venv with the runner's system Python (3.10.12).

This blocks #49251 (min Python → 3.11), whose doc build fails with:

```
Using CPython 3.10.12 interpreter at: /usr/bin/python
Because the current Python version (3.10.12) does not satisfy Python>=3.11.0 ...
```

This PR reads the root `.python-version` and passes it as `python_version` to every doc-builder build call, so doc builds follow the repo's Python version instead of hardcoding one:
- `build_pr_documentation.yml`: the existing `check_links` job (already checked out) reads it and exposes it as a job output.
- `build_documentation.yml`: a small `python-version` job (sparse checkout of `.python-version`) feeds both `build` and `build_other_lang`.
- `pr_build_doc_with_comment.yml`: same small job, reading `.python-version` at the PR head SHA. It never runs PR code, and the value is format-checked (`X.Y[.Z]`) before use.

Also in `pr_build_doc_with_comment.yml` (flagged as `broken_auth_gate` by the security bot on this PR): `python-version` and `build-doc` now require `verify_pr_commit` to succeed, so nothing from the PR head is checked out or built if the PR was updated after the `build-doc` comment. `update_run_status` reports `custom-doc-build` as failed in that case, instead of treating the skipped build as success.

The pinned doc-builder commit already supports the input. `.python-version` is currently `3.11`, which satisfies today's `>=3.10` requirement too, so this can land before #49251.

prs.title: Experts implementation: detect the dispatcher by its forward, and reach sub-config experts
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49600)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## What does this PR do?

Makes `set_experts_implementation` reliable for the models that support it.

- `_can_set_experts_implementation` asks whether the class's experts `forward` *is* the dispatcher `use_experts_implementation` installs (`integrations.moe.dispatches_experts_implementation`), instead of grepping the module source for the decorator's text. The source check misfired on code that merely mentions the decorator, and failed outright without readable source.
- `set_experts_implementation` also sets the implementation on sub-configs whose experts are built straight from the sub-config (no owning `PreTrainedModel`), which the submodule loop never reached; their experts kept dispatching on the stale value. Submodels without switchable experts are still skipped, but registered, so they aren't set a second time.
- Warns when no model or submodel could take the requested implementation, instead of silently doing nothing.

Split out of the exporters runtime work (#48986), which switches MoE experts to export-friendly implementations.

## Tests

`tests/utils/test_modeling_utils.py` and the Qwen3-MoE / Mixtral / Qwen3-VL-MoE / GPT-OSS tests matching `experts or implementation`: 17 passed, 15 skipped.

prs.title: Combine Nvidia+AMD run-slow CI comments into one
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49598)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## Summary

Currently, each `run-slow` comment on a PR generates 5 bot comments:
1. `## Nvidia CI` — trigger acknowledgment
2. `## AMD CI` — trigger acknowledgment
3. CI recap (fast CI, unchanged)
4. `## CI Results (Nvidia)` — results
5. `## CI Results (AMD)` — results

This PR reduces that to **2 comments** by consolidating all 4 slow-CI comments into a single `## CI (Nvidia + AMD)` comment that is **updated in-place** via `PATCH` as each workflow stage completes.

## How it works

The combined comment evolves through 4 states:
1. **Nvidia trigger fires** → POSTs the comment with Nvidia section + AMD placeholder (`⏳ Starting...`)
2. **AMD trigger fires** (after 30s sleep to avoid race condition) → PATCHes to fill AMD section with `⏳ Running...`
3. **Nvidia results done** → PATCHes Nvidia section with full commit info + ✅/❌
4. **AMD results done** → PATCHes AMD section with full commit info + ✅/❌

The comment is never deleted and re-posted — it stays anchored at the same position in the PR timeline. Old-format comments (`## Nvidia CI`, `## AMD CI`, etc.) are cleaned up for backward compatibility.

> Note: `issue_comment`-triggered workflows always run from `main`, so this takes effect immediately after merge.

prs.title: Integrate the UltraBERT architecture
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49596)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

Hello!

# What does this PR do?

Add the UltraBERT architecture. Sources:
* Blog: https://huggingface.co/blog/dmis-lab/ultrabert
* Collection: https://huggingface.co/collections/dmis-lab/ultrabert
* 150M Encoder: https://huggingface.co/dmis-lab/UltraBERT-150M
* 380M Encoder: https://huggingface.co/dmis-lab/UltraBERT-380M
* 150M Embedding model: https://huggingface.co/dmis-lab/UltraBERT-Embed-150M

Here's the custom code that this is all based on:
* https://huggingface.co/dmis-lab/UltraBERT-150M/blob/main/modeling_ultrabert.py
* https://huggingface.co/dmis-lab/UltraBERT-150M/blob/main/configuration_ultrabert.py

## Details
The architecture, although inspired by ModernBERT, is quite similar in a few ways to EuroBERT and Llama as well, so I used those as superclasses where possible in the modular, to keep the modular as compact as possible while matching the custom code behaviour w. bf16 disrepancies at most. 

In the end, only a few real changes remains, and that's how this model has different attention windows and (notably) rotary embedding setups for each layer. In practice there's only 2: local (128 window & 10k rope theta) and global (no window & 2.560.000 rope theta). This means initializing multiple rotary embeddings, one for each unique rope theta (so, 2) and storing them under a rotary_emb `ModuleDict`. 

But other than this global/local different rotary embedding setup, this is not much different than ModernBERT or EuroBERT as far as I can tell. 

Also, this PR only covers the PreTrained, the AutoModel, the MaskedLM head, and the SequenceClassification heads. The original custom code also has TokenClassification and QuestionAnswering, but there's no checkpoints for those. 
There's also technically no checkpoints for SequenceClassification by the original authors, but I trained a few in my experiments to figure out if this architecture is good: https://huggingface.co/models?pipeline_tag=text-ranking&other=ultrabert&sort=trending

## Comparison

```python
import torch

from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer


checkpoint = "dmis-lab/UltraBERT-Embed-150M"
revision = "367d5343b5a0164d57b810cedf5de4b8983d5984"

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(checkpoint, revision=revision, trust_remote_code=True)
inputs = tokenizer(
    ["The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. " * 30, "Hello world!"],
    padding=True,
    return_tensors="pt",
)

for attn_implementation in ["eager", "sdpa", "flash_attention_2"]:
    is_flash = attn_implementation == "flash_attention_2"
    device = "cuda"
    kwargs = {
        "revision": revision,
        "dtype": torch.float16 if is_flash else torch.float32,
        "attn_implementation": attn_implementation,
    }
    reference = AutoModel.from_pretrained(checkpoint, trust_remote_code=True, **kwargs).to(device).eval()
    native = AutoModel.from_pretrained(checkpoint, trust_remote_code=False, **kwargs).to(device).eval()

    if is_flash:
        # The remote code checks this exact name instead of recognizing the Hub kernel fallback.
        reference.config._attn_implementation = "flash_attention_2"

    assert type(reference).__module__.startswith("transformers_modules.")
    assert type(native).__module__.startswith("transformers.models.ultrabert.")

    device_inputs = inputs.to(device)
    with torch.inference_mode():
        expected = reference(**device_inputs).last_hidden_state
        actual = native(**device_inputs).last_hidden_state

    valid_tokens = device_inputs.attention_mask.bool()
    actual, expected = actual[valid_tokens], expected[valid_tokens]
    rtol, atol = (1e-4, 1e-3) if attn_implementation == "sdpa" else (0, 0)
    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=rtol, atol=atol)
    max_diff = (actual - expected).abs().max().item()
    print(f"{attn_implementation}: non-padding tokens match, max absolute difference = {max_diff:.8g}", flush=True)
    del reference, native, expected, actual
```

Ignoring the weight load logs etc, this gives:
```
eager: non-padding tokens match, max absolute difference = 0
sdpa: non-padding tokens match, max absolute difference = 0
flash_attention_2: non-padding tokens match, max absolute difference = 0
```

Not my first time. Codex helped set this up & helped with the tests/experiments. I handwrote the PR description.

prs.title: Fix flaky streamer timeout tests
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49583)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

The test is time-based so gets flaky on CI environements.

Why it fails: the test assumes no text reaches the streamer's queue within the 1 ms timeout, but:

1. the prompt is queued: `skip_prompt` defaults to `False`, so the prompt text goes into the queue as soon as generate starts.
2. The GIL: Python hands the GIL between threads every 5 ms, five times the timeout. When the reading thread's 1 ms wait ends, it often can't run again until the generating thread has added more text. `Queue.get` then finds that text and returns it instead of timing out.

prs.title: Fix numpy/pyarrow conflict in the XPU Docker image
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49582)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

The XPU image fails on any import that touches pyarrow:

```
ImportError: ... pyarrow requires NumPy 2.0 or newer.
```

`pyarrow 26.0.0` is the first pyarrow requiring NumPy 2, and it declares no numpy dependency, so the check only fires at runtime. The resolver conflict is really between `pyctcdecode 0.5.0` (`numpy<2.0.0`, last released in 2023) and `gptqmodel` (`numpy==2.2.6`); resolving it in pyctcdecode's favour pins numpy to 1.26.4, which pyarrow 26 then rejects.

This PR overrides pyctcdecode's stale pin with `UV_OVERRIDE`. pyctcdecode itself works fine on numpy 2 — only its metadata is stale, and upstream [pyctcdecode#118](https://github.com/kensho-technologies/pyctcdecode/pull/118) has been open since 2025-10 on an unmaintained project.

Resolved versions:

| package | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| numpy | 1.26.4 | 2.2.6 |
| pyarrow | 26.0.0 | 26.0.0 |
| gptqmodel | 4.2.5 | 7.6.0 |
| librosa | 0.11.0 | 1.0.0 |
| scipy | 1.17.1 | 1.18.1 |

The old resolution also silently downgraded gptqmodel, librosa and scipy.

Verified on an Intel Arc Pro B60: text generation, distilbert logits, wav2vec2 + librosa transcription, pyctcdecode decoding and a pyarrow/datasets roundtrip all work, and `tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_automatic_speech_recognition.py` (pyctcdecode subset) passes.

Using Apple Silicon as an example for a potential template:

```md
# {Hardware name}
```

prs.title: 🚨 TP: give embeddings their own style, shard input embeddings by default, and shard widths that don't divide by the TP size
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49570)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->
## What does this PR do?

Gives embeddings their own tensor-parallel style, shards every model's input embeddings by default, and lets layers shard widths that don't divide by the TP size. `ColwiseParallel` and `RowwiseParallel` now only handle linear layers.

> [!WARNING]
> **Breaking:** custom TP plans must use `embedding_rowwise` (vocabulary sharding) or `embedding_colwise` (hidden-dimension sharding) for embeddings. Linear styles (`colwise*` / `rowwise*`) now raise on embeddings. Eligible models also shard `embed_tokens` by default, including untied models; explicit plan entries take precedence.

### Embeddings get their own style

`ColwiseParallel` and `RowwiseParallel` used to branch on `isinstance(module, nn.Embedding)` in their parameter sharding, input handling and validation. Those branches move to a dedicated `EmbeddingParallel(shard_dim)`, which keeps the token ids replicated:

| Plan entry | Style | Shards | Output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `embedding_rowwise` | `EmbeddingParallel(shard_dim=0)` | the vocabulary (vocab-parallel, the usual choice: it shares its layout with a tied, vocab-sharded `lm_head`) | partial lookups are all-reduced |
| `embedding_colwise` (new) | `EmbeddingParallel(shard_dim=1)` | the hidden dim (for large untied tables, e.g. Qwen4-Exp's `ngram_embedding`) | slices are all-gathered |

`ColwiseParallel` and `RowwiseParallel` are now linear-only: applying them to a module without `out_features` / `in_features` raises a clear error instead of silently taking the embedding path.

Plans that targeted embeddings with linear styles move to the embedding ones:

- Doge: `mlp.down_embed` / `mlp.up_embed` → `embedding_rowwise` (was `rowwise_split_input`).
- Qwen4-Exp: `ple.ple_embedding.ngram_embedding` → `embedding_colwise` (was `colwise_gather_output`).
- Gemma4 vision: the plan targets the `.linear` inside the clippable-linear wrappers, which have no `in_features`/`out_features` themselves.

### Input embeddings are sharded by default

Almost every model replicated its input embeddings while sharding its `lm_head`. A replicated embedding costs `vocab x hidden` on every rank (~1 GiB for Llama-3-8B in bf16, ~2 GiB for Llama-3-70B), and a tied model's vocab-sharded `lm_head` doesn't match the replicated embedding it shares a weight with.

The config used to add `"embed_tokens": "embedding_rowwise"` only for tied models. That default moves to `init_parallel_plans`, without the `tie_word_embeddings` condition: a base model with a TP plan and an `nn.Embedding` named `embed_tokens` shards it on the vocabulary, unless its plan already names it. Untied models (most large checkpoints) benefit the most. Composite models (VLMs, encoder-decoders) pick the entry up from their text sub-model's plan, e.g. `model.language_model.embed_tokens`. Vision towers and models without an `embed_tokens` embedding (GPT-NeoX's `embed_in`) get nothing, so no plan carries a key that matches no module.

No model plan is edited for this, and Inkling's and MuseGlimmer's explicit entries are removed as redundant. Models whose only plan is a class-level `lm_head` entry (AFMoE, DBRX, GPT-OSS, HunYuan, LFM2, PhiMoE) are unchanged: they need full plans first, in a follow-up.

### Divisibility

Real vocab sizes often don't divide by the TP size (GPT-2's 50257, Whisper's 51865, GotOcr2's), and `colwise_gather_output` used to reject them outright. `distribute_tensor` already splits a parameter unevenly (the last rank holds a shorter slice), and DTensor ops track the real shape. The one gap was the local fast path (inference and quantized kernels): `DTensor.from_local` assumes every rank holds an equal slice. A small `TensorParallelLayer._from_local_last_dim_shard` helper wraps the local tensor with its real width, taken from the module's `out_features` / `in_features` (or `embedding_dim`).

| Style | Width that doesn't divide by the number of ranks |
| --- | --- |
| `colwise*`, `rowwise*` | supported |
| `embedding_rowwise`, `embedding_colwise` | supported |
| `packed_colwise`, `packed_rowwise` (MoE experts' fused `gate_up_proj`) | supported: the strided split and the checkpoint loader both give each rank matching ceil-sized slices of gate and up. Verified with a TP forward and backward of a tiny Qwen3-MoE whose expert intermediate size splits 8/8/8/8/4 over 5 ranks. |
| expert parallelism | rejected, as before (`num_experts` must divide by `ep_size`) |

**Cost.** Divisible sizes run exactly as before. An uneven width only costs anything where it is gathered (a `colwise_gather_output` `lm_head`, `embedding_colwise`), where DTensor pads and unpads around the all-gather; layers that reduce a full-size `Partial` (attention, MLP, packed experts, vocab-parallel embeddings) are unaffected. Gathering bf16 logits over 2 GPUs (NCCL), vocab 128257 vs 128256:

| Logits gathered | Even | Uneven |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 token (a decode step) | 530 µs | 676 µs |
| 2048 tokens | 82.6 ms | 101.3 ms |

`generate` only gathers the last token's logits, so that's about 0.15 ms per decode step.

### Tests

- New `test_tp_plan_shards_input_embeddings` in the TP mixin: a static check that a model whose TP plan covers more than the `lm_head` shards its `nn.Embedding` input embeddings. With `test_tp_plan_matches_params`, it passes for every model (258 passed).
- The TP mixin no longer rounds the tester's vocab up to a multiple of the world size: `vocab_size=99` exercises the uneven `lm_head` in every TP test. The backward test slices the reference gradients (plain and packed) with ceil-sized shards to match.
- Unit tests cover the linear-only check and uneven local shapes for both embedding shardings.
- CPU TP/EP mixin tests, with the allowlist forced off: Llama, Qwen3, Gemma3, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen3-MoE pass. Inkling still fails: its embedding module applies a norm to the partial lookup before it's reduced, which `main` already hits with its explicit `embedding_rowwise` entry (Inkling isn't in the CI allowlist).

<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

`Gemma3nVision2TextModelTest::test_model_parallelism` has failed on every multi-GPU daily run since #44040 removed the class-level skip (2026-02-20):

```
AttributeError: 'Gemma3nModel' object has no attribute 'hf_device_map'
```

The vision tower (`TimmWrapperModel`, in `_no_split_modules`) is 60.4% of the tiny test model. With `model_split_percents = [0.5, 0.6]` GPU 0 gets 60%, the tower does not fit, and `device_map="auto"` resolves to `{"": 1}`. A single-device map is never dispatched, so `hf_device_map` is never set.

Computed with `_get_device_map(model, "auto", max_memory, None)` on the test config: at 0.6 both `Gemma3nModel` and `Gemma3nForConditionalGeneration` map to `{"": 1}`; at 0.7 they split across `{0, 1}`. So this sets `[0.5, 0.7]` on the vision test class only (the text class keeps `[0.5, 0.6]` and passes).

Not run on a multi-GPU machine yet.

prs.title: Fix Whisper timestamp processor with single-element EOS collections (#49556)
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49559)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## What does this PR do?

Fixes #49556

`WhisperTimeStampLogitsProcessor` uses `eos_token_id` as a slice boundary when masking text-token scores. When the EOS token ID is provided as a single-element list, tuple, or tensor, it may not be a valid slice index. The existing initialization also evaluates the EOS value in a boolean context, which can raise an ambiguity error for multi-element tensors.

This PR:
- Uses an explicit `None` check when selecting `eos_token_id`, falling back to `bos_token_id` only when EOS is not configured.
- Normalizes single-element lists, tuples, and tensors to scalar values.
- Adds regression tests for scalar EOS IDs and single-element list, tuple, and tensor inputs.

This change does not add support for arbitrary multi-element EOS collections as slice boundaries.

## Testing

- Focused regression test passed.
- Neighboring logits-processor tests passed.
- `tests/generation/test_logits_process.py`: 49 passed locally on Windows with Python 3.13.1.

prs.title: Make longrope compileable
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49555)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

Fixes #31339 (edit from @qgallouedec)

`longrope_frequency_update` branches on a tensor (`if seq_len > original_max_position_embeddings`). So `fullgraph=True` fails on every longrope model, and the default static-cache auto-compile graph-breaks on every step. This PR picks the long or short frequency set with `torch.where` instead.

It also fixes two longrope bugs:

- The long-frequency cache used the wrong key, so it was recomputed every forward, or raised `UnboundLocalError` with per-layer-type `rope_parameters`.
- `yarn_apply_mscale` read `rope_parameters["factor"]` unconditionally, so `openbmb/MiniCPM3-4B` (no `factor`) failed to load with `KeyError`.

A phi3 test covers both branches under `fullgraph=True` and fails on main. Eager logits are bitwise identical to main. No new test failures.

A100, `torch==2.14.0+cu130`, bf16, 128 new tokens, tok/s before → after:

| | Phi-3.5-mini | MiniCPM3-4B |
| --- | --- | --- |
| eager | 43.4 → 44.0 | 16.3 → 16.8 |
| auto-compiled | 122.1 → 129.7 | 79.8 → 83.0 |
| `fullgraph=True` | fails → 128.6 | fails → 82.8 |

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

```python
import sys

import torch

from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
from transformers.generation.configuration_utils import CompileConfig


model_id = sys.argv[1]
device = torch.accelerator.current_accelerator().type

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, dtype=torch.bfloat16).to(device).eval()

inputs = tokenizer("The capital of France is", return_tensors="pt").to(device)
with torch.no_grad():
    eager = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=16, do_sample=False, disable_compile=True)
    out = model.generate(
        **inputs,
        max_new_tokens=16,
        do_sample=False,
        cache_implementation="static",
        compile_config=CompileConfig(fullgraph=True),
    )
print(tokenizer.decode(out[0], skip_special_tokens=True))
print("tokens identical to eager:", torch.equal(eager, out))
```

Before:

```
# Phi-3.5-mini-instruct
torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported: Data-dependent branching
  File "transformers/modeling_rope_utils.py", line 64, in longrope_frequency_update

# MiniCPM3-4B
  File "transformers/models/minicpm3/modeling_minicpm3.py", line 188, in yarn_apply_mscale
    scaling_factor = rope_parameters["factor"]
KeyError: 'factor'
```

After: both models generate and print `tokens identical to eager: True`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Benchmark</summary>

`python bench.py MODEL_ID {eager,compiled,fullgraph}`

```python
import sys
import time

import torch

from transformers import AutoConfig, AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
from transformers.generation.configuration_utils import CompileConfig


# One mode per process: torch.compile state leaks between configs otherwise.
MODES = {
    # `cache_implementation="static"` auto-compiles on CUDA, so the eager baseline needs `disable_compile`
    "eager": {"disable_compile": True},
    "compiled": {"cache_implementation": "static"},
    "fullgraph": {"cache_implementation": "static", "compile_config": CompileConfig(fullgraph=True)},
}
model_id, mode = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
device = torch.accelerator.current_accelerator().type
NEW_TOKENS, WARMUP, RUNS = 128, 2, 5

config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(model_id)
rp = config.rope_parameters
# Only needed to load MiniCPM3-4B before this PR. This is the value longrope derives when `factor` is absent.
rp.setdefault("factor", config.max_position_embeddings / rp["original_max_position_embeddings"])

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, config=config, dtype=torch.bfloat16).to(device).eval()
inputs = tokenizer("The capital of France is", return_tensors="pt").to(device)


def run():
    return model.generate(
        **inputs, max_new_tokens=NEW_TOKENS, min_new_tokens=NEW_TOKENS, do_sample=False, **MODES[mode]
    )


for _ in range(WARMUP):
    run()
torch.cuda.synchronize()

times = []
for _ in range(RUNS):
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    run()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    times.append(time.perf_counter() - t0)

median = sorted(times)[RUNS // 2]
print(f"{mode:10s} {median:.3f} s   {NEW_TOKENS / median:6.1f} tok/s")
```

</details>

<summary>Logits check</summary>

Run before and after, then compare the saved tensors with `torch.equal`.

```python
import sys

import torch

from transformers import AutoConfig, AutoModelForCausalLM


model_id, out_path = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
device = torch.accelerator.current_accelerator().type

config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(model_id)
rp = config.rope_parameters
# Only needed to load MiniCPM3-4B before this PR. This is the value longrope derives when `factor` is absent.
rp.setdefault("factor", config.max_position_embeddings / rp["original_max_position_embeddings"])
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, config=config, dtype=torch.bfloat16).to(device).eval()

orig = rp["original_max_position_embeddings"]
g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
logits = {}
with torch.no_grad():
    # short stays on `short_factor`, long crosses `original_max_position_embeddings` and uses `long_factor`
    for tag, n in [("short", 512), ("long", orig + 512)]:
        ids = torch.randint(100, config.vocab_size - 100, (1, n), generator=g).to(device)
        logits[tag] = model(ids, use_cache=False).logits[0, -64:].float().cpu()
torch.save(logits, out_path)
```

prs.title: Only tie MM Grounding DINO decoder heads when the config shares them
prs.body:
Fixes #49529.

## Problem
`MMGroundingDinoForObjectDetection._tied_weights_keys` tied every decoder layer's box head and class head to layer 0 unconditionally. Published checkpoints (`iSEE-Laboratory/llmdet_{tiny,base,large}`, `openmmlab-community/mm_grounding_dino_*`) set `decoder_bbox_embed_share: false` and `decoder_cls_embed_share: false` and store per-layer heads (in llmdet_large, heads 1–5 differ from head 0 by 1.1–1.4× the norm of head 0). After loading, layers 1–5 silently used layer 0's heads — e.g. LLMDet-tiny put the first cat's box 41px above the image and cut it at x=472 on a 640px-wide image. `GroundingDinoForObjectDetection.__init__` already drops its box-head tie when `config.decoder_bbox_embed_share` is False; the MM class never looked at the config. The stale `# class embed has no weights` comment was also wrong: `MMGroundingDinoContrastiveEmbedding` has a learnable `bias`, which was tied too.

## Fix (`modular_mm_grounding_dino.py` + regenerated `modeling_`/`configuration_`)
- New `MMGroundingDinoConfig` fields `decoder_bbox_embed_share: bool = True` and `decoder_cls_embed_share: bool = True` (defaults preserve current behavior for configs that don't specify them).
- `__init__` copies `_tied_weights_keys` to the instance and deletes the bbox/class entries when the corresponding flag is False — same pattern as `GroundingDinoForObjectDetection`.
- Removed the stale `# class embed has no weights` comment: `MMGroundingDinoContrastiveEmbedding` has a learnable `bias`.

## Verification
- New `test_decoder_heads_tying_follows_config`: defaults keep heads tied (identity checks incl. class bias); with both flags False, per-layer heads are independent tensors and `get_expanded_tied_weights_keys()` contains zero cross-layer ties. **Fails on unfixed code, passes with the fix** (verified via stash round-trip).
- End-to-end with the real hub config: `MMGroundingDinoConfig.from_pretrained('iSEE-Laboratory/llmdet_tiny')` yields flags False/False and an untied model.
- Full fast suite `tests/models/mm_grounding_dino/test_modeling_mm_grounding_dino.py -m "not slow"`: **76 passed, 0 failed** (initial 5 failures were missing env deps — timm/scipy/CPU-torchvision — all resolved, confirmed unrelated by error messages).
- Repo checkers `modular_conversion` and `config_docstrings,config_attributes` pass; ruff format clean (one ruff-lint hit is pre-existing line 601, untouched).

## Update (ea03e75): load published decoder head keys + value test

Reviewer testing caught a second half to this bug: untying alone left layers 1-5 on init values, because the published files store heads 1+ only under the model.decoder prefix while head 0 sits at top level, and the old tied map let the top-level heads 1+ be wiped and re-initialized with no missing-keys trace.

- The untie step now swaps in reverse-scoped tied entries: the head-0 decoder copies point back at the top-level head 0, and the top-level heads 1+ point at their model.decoder copies. Remap lives in the tied map (not weight mapping), so only the modular file changed, with modeling/configuration regenerated via the official converter. Save path round-trips back to the published layout.
- New test_decoder_heads_load_values_from_published_layout loads a state dict in the published layout and compares head tensors value-by-value. It fails on ea03e75's parent (untied but not remapped) with exactly the reported symptom. Note the limit of that round-trip: taken alone the comparison also passes on unfixed code, because tying collapses the per-layer values first. The untied precondition is now asserted at the top of the test, which makes both new tests fail on unfixed code and pass here.
- Fast suite, modular/config checkers, and ruff on touched files all green. I verified with unit tests and checkers locally; hub-checkpoint rerun of the reviewer's script is invited below.

## Independent verification on published checkpoints

Reported by others on this PR, on checkpoints from the list above:

- `@MustafaOrhon`: ran `ea03e75` on `iSEE-Laboratory/llmdet_tiny` and `llmdet_large`. All decoder heads load from the checkpoint with no missing keys, `save_pretrained` writes every head back out, and on large the boxes and scores match 5.18 with each layer's heads restored by hand — including the second remote that the tied heads used to drop.
- `@Kaus1ubh`: ran `01601dd` on `openmmlab-community/mm_grounding_dino_large_all`, CPU fp32, 8 RefCOCO val expressions, top box vs gold: **5.19.0 scores 0/8, this branch scores 7/8**. Heads 1-5 match the checkpoint tensors, loading reports no missing keys, and the boxes are identical to restoring each layer's heads by hand. Separately, with each layer's heads restored by hand the same checkpoint reaches 75.6% acc@0.5 over 4,729 RefCOCO val expressions.

I checked that checkpoint's safetensors header directly: head 0 is stored only top-level (`bbox_embed.0.*`, `class_embed.0.bias`) and heads 1-5 only under `model.decoder.*`, which is the pair of layouts the remap handles. The single miss in the 7/8 run is therefore not attributable to parameter loading.

## Update (0f55ada): untied precondition asserted, branch merged up to main

- The value test now asserts the untied precondition before building the published-layout state dict. Both new tests fail on unfixed code and pass here; previously the value test alone passed on unfixed code.
- Merged `main` (110 commits) so CI runs against the current base.
- Re-ran on the merged tree: `tests/models/mm_grounding_dino/test_modeling_mm_grounding_dino.py` **79 passed, 0 failed** (6832 subtests); `check_modular_conversion` 0 diff lines; `check_config_docstrings` and `check_config_attributes` clean; ruff 0.14.10 check and format clean.
- Re-verified `iSEE-Laboratory/llmdet_tiny` after the merge: all 1015 checkpoint tensors match, each layer's class bias and box head equal the file, `save_pretrained` round-trips to the published layout.

Anyways, there are 3 case:

2. Dequantize: you want the full weight
3. Quantize: you do it on the fly from a bf16 ckpt. 

Those 3 cases each have a different injection point in core model loading:

3. We should probably do it before all conversion ops to reduce loading imbalance. But today it goes through the get quantize ops?

prs.title: Accept whole-number floats for integer tool arguments in parse_response
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49547)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

When tool schemas are passed to the response parser, an `integer` argument written as a whole-number float like `"3.0"` is now cast to `3` instead of being left as the raw string.

- JSON Schema (draft 6 onward, including 2020-12) defines `integer` as any number with a zero fractional part, so `3.0` is a valid `integer` value. `jsonschema` (Draft 7 and 2020-12 validators) and Pydantic v2 both accept it, and Pydantic returns `3`.
- Models do sometimes write integer arguments this way, and the tool then receives a string where its schema declares an integer.
- Values with a fractional part (`"3.5"`), `inf` and `NaN` still fail the `integer` cast, so they fall through to the next declared type or stay raw, as before.
- Adds a unit test next to the existing argument coercion tests.

Cc @Rocketknight1

prs.title: Add `MtpModel` helpers for frameworks that own the drafting loop
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49544)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Factors three pieces out of `MtpModel` so that frameworks which own the drafting loop (e.g. vLLM, which serves `MtpModel` as a speculative decoding draft in its Transformers modeling backend) can reuse them instead of duplicating them:

- `forward_layer(layer_idx, inputs_embeds, last_hidden_states, position_ids, **kwargs)`: one step of the drafting loop (rotary, MTP layer, shared post norm). `forward` now calls it.
- `get_mtp_weights_regex(main_model)`: the regex selecting the MTP weights, previously local to `from_pretrained`.
- `get_weight_conversions(main_model)`: the ordered weight conversions (layer offset renamings, `"MtpModel"` mapping, main model conversions), previously local to `from_pretrained`. Falls back to `get_model_conversion_mapping(main_model)` when the main model was not loaded with `from_pretrained`.

No behaviour change for Transformers. With this, per-layer changes such as #49468 (per-layer-type RoPE) only need to touch `forward_layer` to reach vLLM.

vLLM side: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61270

Tests: `pytest tests/models -k mtp`: 10 passed, 2 failed (`InklingVision2TextModelTest`/`InklingAudio2TextModelTest::test_generate_with_mtp`, which also fail on `main` locally). Also checked that the vLLM draft loads its weights through these helpers.

prs.title: fix(distributed): bind TPU ranks to device index 0, not LOCAL_RANK
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49543)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Follow-up to #49502. On TPU, `from_pretrained(..., distributed_config=DistributedConfig(tp_size=N))` under `torchrun` crashes on every rank but 0:

```
RuntimeError: Device index 1 is out of bounds of the number of addressable devices 1
```

Rank 0 then hangs on a collective that never completes.

`distributed/utils.py` binds the device with `torch.accelerator.set_device_index(LOCAL_RANK)`, which is the CUDA convention. torch_tpu gives each torchrun process a single chip, and the process always sees it as index 0 (`PjrtBackend` binds `addressable_devices[0]`), so any index above 0 is rejected. #49502 switched to the right API but kept `LOCAL_RANK` as the index.

This PR adds a `_local_device_index(device_type, local_rank)` helper. It returns the current device index on TPU and `local_rank` everywhere else. It is used everywhere the device is bound: `_ensure_torch_distributed`, `initialize_distributed_mesh`, and the deprecated `initialize_tensor_parallelism` / `initialize_fully_sharded_data_parallelism`. Each call site still reads `LOCAL_RANK` as before, so CUDA/XPU/HPU behaviour is unchanged.

Why it worked in v5.17.0: when the caller passed a `device_mesh`, `initialize_tensor_parallelism` skipped `set_device` entirely. Since v5.18.0, `from_pretrained` goes through `initialize_distributed_mesh`, which always binds the device.

prs.title: Use mlp_layer_types for AXK1 so the MoE layer layout honours moe_layer_freq
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49518)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

- Replace `first_k_dense_replace` on `AXK1Config` with `mlp_layer_types` (`"dense"` / `"sparse"` per layer), like AXK2
- When `mlp_layer_types` isn't given, derive it from the legacy `first_k_dense_replace` / `moe_layer_freq` kwargs (`i >= first_k_dense_replace and i % moe_layer_freq == 0` → `"sparse"`), so the official checkpoint's `config.json` loads unchanged
- `AXK1DecoderLayer` chooses the MoE block from `config.mlp_layer_types`

The model ignored `moe_layer_freq` before, so a config with `moe_layer_freq > 1` built the wrong layers without any error. With the default of 1 nothing changes.

`AXK1Config` inherits from `DeepseekV3Config`, which doesn't declare `moe_layer_freq`. It only existed on a config when its `config.json` set it, so downstream code that read it failed with `AttributeError` on minimal configs. vLLM hit this after switching to this config class and had to work around it with `getattr` fallbacks: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60954. With this change, downstream code can read `mlp_layer_types`, which is always set.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

prs.title: Make the SDPA position_bias mask contiguous so T5-style models use fused kernels
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49517)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Before #47014 (first in 5.15.0) T5-style models ran eager attention; since then they use SDPA by default, and
sentence-t5-base / gtr-t5-base encode takes 7.4% to 7.7% more time (bisected to 560f36c).

`create_position_bias_mask` returns `position_bias` (plus the attention mask) as the SDPA `attn_mask`. For T5-style
models `position_bias` comes from `compute_bias`, which returns `values.permute([2, 0, 1]).unsqueeze(0)` (udop:
`RelativePositionBiasBase.forward`, `values.permute([0, 3, 1, 2])`), a non-contiguous view. Fused SDPA kernels reject
a mask with stride(-1) != 1, so SDPA falls back to MATH.
This PR adds `.contiguous()` to the return of `create_position_bias_mask`, one line in
`src/transformers/integrations/sdpa_attention.py`. The mask values are unchanged; only the memory layout changes.

AI assistance: I used Claude Code to help run the verification scripts.
I reviewed every changed line and the results below.

Fixes #49516

## SDPA backend

Mask passed to SDPA by models that call `create_position_bias_mask`, main vs this PR:

| model | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| sentence-t5-base, gtr-t5-base encode | MATH | fused |
| t5-small, mt5-small, umt5-small, udop-large generate | MATH | fused, except the first decoder step (mask (1, heads, 1, 1)) |
| pix2struct-textcaps-base generate | MATH for 32 of 65 distinct q / mask shapes | fused, except the first decoder step |
| pop2piano forward | MATH for 2 of 3 distinct q / mask shapes | fused |
| seamless-m4t-v2-large speech-to-text | MATH | fused |
| w2v-bert-2.0 encoder (default relative_key) | mem-efficient (mask not contiguous, but stride(-1) = 1) | mem-efficient, plus one mask copy per attention call |
| hf-seamless-m4t-medium, wav2vec2-conformer-rel-pos-large | already contiguous | unchanged |

prs.title: Deprecate rope_scaling assignment and normalize legacy RoPE keys
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49515)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Assigning v4-style `rope_scaling` on a v5 config replaced the whole `rope_parameters` dictionary: `rope_theta` and `partial_rotary_factor` were dropped, the legacy `type` key was not normalised, so rotary-embedding construction failed with `KeyError: 'rope_type'` and a save/load round trip silently came back with the default theta (#49519).

Following the review, the setter now emits a `FutureWarning` pointing callers to `rope_parameters`, assigns the supplied value, and calls `standardize_rope_params()` only when the value is not `None`. It no longer tries to infer missing parameters or adds its own `rope_theta` validation. A complete dictionary still works and legacy `type` is normalised to `rope_type`; assigning `None` leaves `rope_parameters` as `None`.

The two regression tests cover the deprecation warning and legacy-key normalisation on a complete dictionary, and assigning `None` without standardisation.

Linux x86_64 and macOS, CPU, Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.14.

prs.title: [CB] Fix the CPU memory budget used to size the paged cache under NUMA binding
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49512)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## What's wrong

On CPU, `get_device_and_memory_breakdown()` takes the cache budget from `psutil.virtual_memory().total`, which is the whole machine's RAM. A process bound with `numactl --membind` can only allocate from the bound nodes, so the paged cache is sized above what it can actually get.

Since #47809 the cache is a single `torch.zeros(...)` tensor, so every page is touched at creation instead of lazily. The oversized budget is no longer harmless: the process is OOM-killed during cache initialization, before generating a single token.

## Reproduction

```bash
numactl --membind 0 python examples/generate/continuous_batching_simple.py --samples 16 --max-new-tokens 8 --attn sdpa
```

**Before** — the budget is a share of the whole machine, so the cache does not fit in node 0:

```
Killed                                                                   # exit 137

$ dmesg
oom-kill:constraint=CONSTRAINT_MEMORY_POLICY,nodemask=0,...,task=python
```

**After** — the budget is a share of node 0, and the run completes:

```
--- Finished CB Generation Example ---                                   # exit 0
```

## The fix

The CPU total is capped by the size of the NUMA nodes the process is bound to, computed by a private `_get_numa_bound_memory()` in `continuous_batching/requests.py`:

- The policy comes from the second field of `/proc/self/numa_maps`, e.g. `default`, `bind:0-1,3`, `bind=static:0,2`, `interleave:0-5`, `prefer:1`. Only `bind` (with or without mode flags) is a hard limit, so only it lowers the budget.
- Each bound node's size comes from the first line of `/sys/devices/system/node/node<N>/meminfo`.
- If a file is missing or malformed, it returns `None` and the budget stays at the machine total, as before. If a bound node's size can't be read, it also logs a warning.

CUDA, XPU and MPS are untouched, and without a `bind` policy the total is identical to before.

## Tests

Unit tests cover the policy formats (single node, list and range, `static` / `relative` / combined flags), the non-bind policies, and malformed or missing files.

Checked on a 6-node machine (about 252 GiB per node, 1511 GiB total):

| launched with | policy | CPU total |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no `numactl` | `default` | 1511.47 GiB |
| `--membind 0` | `bind:0` | 251.64 GiB |
| `--membind 0-1,3` | `bind:0-1,3` | 755.59 GiB |
| `--balancing --membind 1` | `bind=balancing:1` | 251.98 GiB |

# What does this PR do?

Fixes #49510

Pass the resolved backend-specific class reference to the remote video processor loader. `AutoVideoProcessor.from_pretrained` already resolves string, dict, and list auto_map entries, but then overwrites the result with the original container. Dict/list entries therefore reach the dynamic loader's string operations and raise `AttributeError`.

The production change removes that assignment, matching the existing AutoImageProcessor path. It does not change backend selection or fallback rules, register signatures, trust handling, or the dynamic module loader.

The regression uses two independent tests in `tests/models/auto/test_video_processing_auto.py`: one writes a backend dict to the processor JSON, and the other writes a backend list. Each uses the existing CustomVideoProcessor fixture and real local dynamic modules to check loading, saving, and reloading. The previous trust, cache, and fallback subcases are removed from these new tests; existing tests are unchanged.

This is independent of #49458's lazy lookup fix and #49470's registration migration documentation. No dependencies or public arguments are added.

## Tests

Both new tests fail with the original dict/list `AttributeError` on unchanged source `fa40619176` and pass with the one-line correction. The five related official test files give 94 passed and 11 existing skips on CPU. All 26 native repository checks and all five native style checks pass, without unrelated formatting changes.

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/models/auto/test_video_processing_auto.py tests/models/auto/test_image_processing_auto.py tests/models/auto/test_processing_auto.py tests/models/llava_onevision/test_video_processing_llava_onevision.py tests/models/qwen3_vl/test_video_processing_qwen3_vl.py

make style
git diff --check
```

The skipped cases are existing slow compile, unsupported/not-applicable processor mixin, and staging publication tests. This is processor-loading and CPU preprocessing validation, not model inference, GPU, or performance validation.

prs.title: Complete PR #49285: remove unused device=None from rope __init__ in 7 remaining model families
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49508)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Follow-up to #49285, which removed the orphaned `device` parameter from rope `__init__` in 11 model families
after #49228 stopped forwarding it to `rope_init_fn`. Seven families were not covered by that sweep and still
carry the parameter.

The split is visible inside a single file. In `modeling_qwen3_omni_moe.py`, #49285 fixed the text rope but not
the vision rope earlier in the same file:

```python
# line 1234, fixed by #49285
class Qwen3OmniMoeThinkerTextRotaryEmbedding(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: Qwen3OmniMoeTextConfig):

# line 981, still on main
class Qwen3OmniMoeVisionRotaryEmbedding(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: Qwen3OmniMoeVisionEncoderConfig, device=None):
```

The seven remaining classes are all the non-text rope modules, six of them named `*VisionRotaryEmbedding`:

| model | class | `__init__` line |
|---|---|---|
| sam2_video | `Sam2VideoVisionRotaryEmbedding` | 752 |
| sam3_tracker_video | `Sam3TrackerVideoVisionRotaryEmbedding` | 752 |
| edgetam_video | `EdgeTamVideoVisionRotaryEmbedding` | 143 |
| qwen2_5_omni | `Qwen2_5OmniVisionRotaryEmbedding` | 936 |
| qwen3_omni_moe | `Qwen3OmniMoeVisionRotaryEmbedding` | 988 |
| gemma4 | `Gemma4VisionRotaryEmbedding` | 720 |
| evolla | `EvollaSaProtRotaryEmbedding` | 165 |

In all seven, the class is flattened to `nn.Module`, `super().__init__()` takes no arguments and `device` is
never read in the body, so the parameter is dead. In the six corresponding `modular_*.py` templates,
`super().__init__(config, device=device)` forwards to a parent whose signature is `__init__(self, config)`.

`ty`, pinned at `ty==0.0.20` in `setup.py` and wired into `utils/checkers.py` as the `types` checker, already
reports this on `main`. Over the files this PR touches it goes from 460 diagnostics to 456, with four removed
and none added:

```
src/transformers/models/gemma4/modular_gemma4.py:797:34: error[too-many-positional-arguments] Too many positional arguments to bound method `__init__`: expected 2, got 3
src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_omni/modular_qwen2_5_omni.py:1361:34: error[unknown-argument] Argument `device` does not match any known parameter of bound method `__init__`
src/transformers/models/qwen3_omni_moe/modular_qwen3_omni_moe.py:1065:34: error[unknown-argument] Argument `device` does not match any known parameter of bound method `__init__`
src/transformers/models/sam2_video/modular_sam2_video.py:945:34: error[unknown-argument] Argument `device` does not match any known parameter of bound method `__init__`
```

`modular_sam3_tracker_video.py` is not on that list because its parent is `Sam2VideoVisionRotaryEmbedding`,
which still declares `device` on `main`, so the call is currently well typed. This PR fixes both ends in the
same change, which is why no new diagnostic appears.

I checked every rope `__init__` in the repository rather than only the ones I found first. Walking
`src/transformers/models/**/modeling_*.py` with `ast` and classifying each `__init__(self, config, ..., device)`
by whether `device` is read in its body:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| rope `__init__` with a `device` parameter | 26 | 19 |
| `device` is read in the body | 19 | 19 |
| `device` is dead | 7 | 0 |

The 19 live ones are untouched. They are the `layer_type`-keyed families that genuinely pass it through, for
example `modernbert`, `olmo3`, `laguna`, `mimo_v2_flash`, `deepseek_v4` and `neomme`, all of which call
`rope_init_fn(self.config, device, layer_type=layer_type)`.

`gemma4` is the one that makes the distinction concrete, because it holds both cases in the same file.
`Gemma4VisionRotaryEmbedding` (line 720) never reads `device` and is fixed here; `Gemma4TextRotaryEmbedding`
(line 1080) reads it at line 1106 and is deliberately left alone, since removing it there would raise
`NameError`.

No caller passes `device` to any of these classes: grepping `src/`, `tests/` and `examples/` for a rope class
instantiated with `device=` returns nothing, and `test_model_rope_scaling_frequencies` builds the module with
`rope_class(config=text_config).to(torch_device)`.

## Checks

- `python utils/check_modular_conversion.py --files <the 7 modular files>` passes, so the seven generated files
  are exactly what the converter produces from the edited templates. `modular_edgetam_video.py` is included
  because `EdgeTamVideoVisionRotaryEmbedding` is declared there as `pass` over the sam2_video class, which is
  why its generated file changes without its template needing an edit.
- `python utils/checkers.py` over the repository consistency set: 22 checkers pass, including `copies`,
  `ruff_check` and `ruff_format` at the pinned `v0.14.10`, `noisy_comments`, `modeling_structure`,
  `modeling_rules_doc`, `inits`, `init_isort`, `imports`, `repo`, `dummies`, `doc_toc`, `config_attributes`,
  `config_docstrings`, `pipeline_typing`, `doctest_list`, `update_metadata`, `deps_table`, `add_dates`,
  `sort_auto_mappings`, `import_complexity` and `reviewers`. `git diff --check` is also clean.
- `python utils/tests_fetcher.py --print_dependencies_of` reports no dependents for any of the 13 files, so the
  seven model test files above are the full test surface for this change.
- Two checkers fail for reasons that are not this change. `auto_mappings` fails identically on a clean
  checkout, and its regenerated diff is about `detr`/`MaskFormerDetrConfig` and the
  `SPECIAL_MODEL_TYPE_TO_MODULE_NAME` table. `docstrings` cannot run on Windows as soon as any diff exists:
  `check_docstrings.py` does `str(object_file).split("/src/")[1]`, and a Windows path is
  `C:\...\src\transformers\...`, so it raises `IndexError` on the first object it inspects, `BertModel`, which
  this PR does not touch. It only passes on a clean checkout because the diff-filtering branch is skipped
  there. The `types` checker also fails on its own fixed file list, on two Windows-only diagnostics in
  `src/transformers/cli/chat.py` for `pwd.getpwuid` and `os.getuid`, which this PR does not touch either.
- `pytest` on the seven model test files: 770 passed, 924 skipped, 13950 subtests passed, 16 failed. All 16
  failures are environmental on my machine and unrelated to this change: 15 are
  `InductorError: InvalidCxxCompiler: Compiler: cl is not found` because `torch.compile` cannot find MSVC, and
  the last one was `test_causal_lm_can_accept_training_kwargs` needing `accelerate`, which passes once
  `accelerate` is installed. `sam2_video`, `sam3_tracker_video`, `edgetam_video` and `evolla` have no failures
  at all. I could not run the GPU-only tests.

cc @ydshieh since this completes #49285, and @Cyrilvallez for #49228.
