prs.title: [fix][Qwen3-Omni] Respect generation_mode in audio generation
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49505)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

`AnyToAnyPipeline(..., generation_mode="audio")` fails with Qwen3-Omni because `generation_mode` reaches the thinker as an unused argument. This handles it in the outer model and maps it to `return_audio`, following Qwen2.5-Omni. An explicit `return_audio` still takes precedence.

<details>
<summary>End-to-end reproduction and results</summary>

Base: `536ecc007387a50e77603bb5d92100e9b07514cc`. The reproduction uses the public 30B checkpoint pinned below, Python 3.12, one NVIDIA H200, PyTorch `2.11.0a0+eb65b36914.nv26.02`, bfloat16, and SDPA. Generation is limited to 20 thinker tokens and 10 talker tokens. This checks the audio output contract, not speech quality.

From a Transformers checkout with CUDA PyTorch installed:

```bash
python -m pip install -e . accelerate librosa soundfile pillow
REPRO=$(mktemp -d)
cat > "$REPRO/repro.py" <<'PY'
import numpy as np
import torch
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
from transformers import AutoProcessor, Qwen3OmniMoeForConditionalGeneration
from transformers.pipelines.any_to_any import AnyToAnyPipeline

print("torch", torch.__version__, "CUDA", torch.cuda.get_device_name(0), flush=True)
model_path = snapshot_download(
    "Qwen/Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct",
    revision="26291f793822fb6be9555850f06dfe95f2d7e695",
)
processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_path)
model = Qwen3OmniMoeForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(
    model_path, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="cuda:0", attn_implementation="sdpa"
).eval()
pipe = AnyToAnyPipeline(
    model=model, processor=processor, tokenizer=processor.tokenizer, task="any-to-any"
)
conversation = [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Say hi."}]}]
result = pipe(
    text=conversation,
    generation_mode="audio",
    generate_kwargs={
        "thinker_max_new_tokens": 20,
        "thinker_do_sample": False,
        "talker_max_new_tokens": 10,
        "talker_do_sample": False,
    },
)
audio = np.asarray(result[0]["generated_audio"])
assert audio.size > 0 and np.isfinite(audio).all()
print("audio shape", audio.shape, "finite", bool(np.isfinite(audio).all()), flush=True)
inputs = processor.apply_chat_template(
    conversation, tokenize=True, return_dict=True, return_tensors="pt", add_generation_prompt=True
).to("cuda")
with torch.no_grad():
    reference = model.generate(**inputs, return_audio=False, thinker_max_new_tokens=2, thinker_do_sample=False)
    explicit = model.generate(
        **inputs, generation_mode="audio", return_audio=False, thinker_max_new_tokens=2, thinker_do_sample=False
    )
torch.testing.assert_close(explicit, reference)
print("PASS: audio pipeline returns finite waveform; explicit return_audio=False preserves text output", flush=True)
PY
python "$REPRO/repro.py"
```

Run the same script on the base and PR checkout. The base fails before generating audio:

```text
ValueError: The following `model_kwargs` are not used by the model: ['generation_mode'] (note: typos in the generate arguments will also show up in this list)
```

Patched source exited successfully. Raw output excerpt:

```text
audio shape (16725,) finite True
PASS: audio pipeline returns finite waveform; explicit return_audio=False preserves text output
after exit 0
```

Restoring the base source reproduced the same `generation_mode` error and exited 1. The script also compares explicit `return_audio=False` with the existing text-only call and checks that their token outputs match.

The existing audio integration test now passes `generation_mode="audio"`. The script above passed on H200. Local code-quality, repository-consistency, and style checks also passed. The full slow integration test and platform CI have not been run.

</details>

prs.title: [Cache] Fix get_max_length on empty cache and add missing properties to EncoderDecoderCache
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49504)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

This PR fixes two related issues in `transformers.cache_utils`:

1. **`Cache.get_max_length()` crashes on empty cache:**
   Calling `get_max_length()` or accessing `cache.max_cache_len` on a fresh `DynamicCache()` (which starts with `self.layers = []`) raised `ValueError: max() iterable argument is empty`. Per the docstring (`-1` indicates no maximum or undefined maximum), it now safely returns `-1` when `len(self.layers) == 0`.

2. **`EncoderDecoderCache` contract violation (`AttributeError` on properties):**
   `EncoderDecoderCache` inherits from `Cache`, but previously lacked implementations for `batch_size`, `is_initialized`, and `is_linear` (as well as `early_initialization`, `prefetch`, and `offload`), which fall back to `Cache` methods that expect `self.layers`. These properties and methods now properly delegate to the underlying `self_attention_cache` and `cross_attention_cache`.

3. ~~**`DynamicCache.batch_size` always returning `-1`**~~ — removed from this PR. Tracking `batch_size` on dynamic layers changes the `generate` cache-reuse path, so I'd rather discuss it in a separate issue first.

prs.title: Fix: use torch.accelerator device APIs so TP loading works again on TPU
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49502)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Recent torch_tpu nightlies make the `torch.tpu` device APIs that have a `torch.accelerator` equivalent internal. Calling them from outside `torch`/`torch_tpu` now raises:

```
RuntimeError: set_device is internal to TorchTPU and can only be called by the
PyTorch framework (torch and torch_tpu). Use torch.accelerator.set_device_index instead.
```

This breaks every `from_pretrained(..., distributed_config=DistributedConfig(tp_size>1))` on TPU before any weight is loaded, because `initialize_distributed_mesh` calls `getattr(torch, device_type).set_device(...)`. The affected APIs are `set_device`, `current_device`, `is_available`, `device_count`, `synchronize`, `set_stream`, `current_stream` and the `device()` context manager.

In this PR we swtch these calls to the more generic `torch.accelerator` API, which has existed since torch 2.6 (our minimum) and dispatches to the current accelerator.Notes for other backends:

- Every function used here is in `torch.accelerator` in torch 2.6. It covers CUDA, XPU, MPS, HPU, MTIA and PrivateUse1 backends, going through the same `DeviceGuardImpl` the per-backend calls use.
- One difference on torch 2.6 only: `torch.accelerator.is_available()` is `device_count() > 0` and lazily initializes the device, while `torch.cuda.is_available()` does not. The only non-TPU caller is continuous batching, which runs with the model already on the device. From torch 2.7, `is_available()` delegates to the backend's own `is_available()`.

prs.title: Save the PEFT adapter of a load-time sharded model from its own parameters
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49500)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

With a model sharded at load time (`DistributedConfig`) and a LoRA adapter, the checkpoint save at `save_steps` hangs with PEFT 0.21.2.

The Trainer saves PEFT models from the main process only. PEFT 0.21.2's `get_peft_model_state_dict` builds the state dict from `model.state_dict()` and, because the model has `_tp_size`, gathers every `DTensor` in it with `gather_state_dict_for_save`, i.e. `full_tensor()` on each sharded base weight. That is a collective only the main process enters (the other ranks wait in `store_flos`), and it would gather the whole model to CPU anyway.

This hands PEFT the adapter's trainable parameters as the state dict. They are plain tensors (attached after sharding), so the main process saves them alone.

Repro (2 GPUs, tiny Qwen3 + LoRA): the script below. main: hangs at the step-2 save (killed after 240 s); this branch: `train + save OK`.

Test: `test_fsdp2_peft_trainer_save` in `test_fsdp_mixin.py` trains one step with LoRA and `save_steps=1`, then checks the saved adapter tensor for tensor against the live one. Passes here on Qwen3 and Llama (2 H100s); on main it hangs in the save until the 300 s timeout (PEFT 0.21.2).

```python
# torchrun --nproc_per_node 2 repro_peft_save.py
# Saving a LoRA adapter with `Trainer` on a model sharded at load time.
import torch
from datasets import Dataset
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, Trainer, TrainingArguments
from transformers.distributed import DistributedConfig

model_id = "trl-internal-testing/tiny-Qwen3ForCausalLM"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    model_id, dtype=torch.bfloat16, distributed_config=DistributedConfig(fsdp_size=2)
)
model = get_peft_model(model, LoraConfig(r=8, target_modules=["q_proj", "v_proj"]))
dataset = Dataset.from_dict({"input_ids": [[1, 2, 3, 4]] * 8, "labels": [[1, 2, 3, 4]] * 8})
args = TrainingArguments(
    output_dir="/tmp/repro_peft_save", max_steps=2, save_steps=2, save_only_model=True, report_to="none", per_device_train_batch_size=1
)
trainer = Trainer(model=model, args=args, train_dataset=dataset)
trainer.train()  # hangs in the checkpoint save at step 2
if torch.distributed.get_rank() == 0:
    print("train + save OK")
```

# What does this PR do?

This PR addresses the mixed BOS prefix issue in `WatermarkDetector`, related to #49293.

Previously, `WatermarkDetector` only checked the first sequence in a batch to determine whether to remove the BOS token. This could cause inconsistent detection behavior when some sequences contained a leading BOS token and others did not.

The original behavior for batches with consistent BOS prefixes remains unchanged.

prs.title: Fix group_images_by_shape to key on full shape, not spatial dims only
prs.body:
## Motivation

`group_images_by_shape` keys groups by `image.shape[1:]` - the spatial dims only, excluding the leading channel dimension. When a request mixes images that share a spatial size but differ in channel count (e.g. a 1-channel grayscale and a 3-channel RGB image at the same H x W), both land in the same group and the per-group `torch.stack` fails:

```
RuntimeError: stack expects each tensor to be equal size, but got [1, 700, 1000] at entry 0 and [3, 700, 1000] at entry 1
```

This is triggered through the Qwen2-VL image processor path (grayscale + same-size RGB JPEG in one request) and surfaces in downstream serving stacks - see sgl-project/sglang#26751 (with the full server traceback and live verification).

## Modifications

- `src/transformers/image_transforms.py`: key the grouping on the full `image.shape` instead of `image.shape[1:]`. Groups only ever split finer, so same-channel behavior is unchanged; mixed-channel images are grouped separately, keeping every group uniform and stackable.
- `tests/test_image_transforms.py`: new `test_group_images_by_shape_mixed_channels` - fails on the pre-patch code with the exact production error above, and asserts that mixed-channel inputs group correctly, same-channel images of the same shape are still batched into one group, and `reorder_images` preserves the original per-image order.

## Validation

- New test reproduces the crash on the unpatched code (`stack expects each tensor to be equal size, [1, 700, 1000] vs [3, 700, 1000]`) and passes with the fix.
- Full `tests/test_image_transforms.py` suite passes (25 tests).
- Live: the one-line change applied (via docker volume mount) to a transformers 5.12.1 serving stack (sglang v0.5.21, Qwen3-VL) turns the failing 2-image grayscale+RGB repro from 500 to 200, per the update on sgl-project/sglang#26751.

---
The above was generated by Qwen 3.8 on behalf of @bornmw and was validated.

prs.title: Make sinusoidal position embeddings compileable
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49482)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## What does this PR do?

`SinusoidalPositionalEmbedding` grows its weight table when the sequence outgrows it:

```python
max_pos = self.padding_idx + 1 + seq_len + past_key_values_length
if max_pos > self.weights.size(0):
    self.make_weights(max_pos + self.offset, self.embedding_dim, self.padding_idx)
```

With a compileable cache `past_key_values_length` is a tensor, so this becomes data-dependent branching and compilation fails on the first decoding step. The growth itself is not traceable either, since `make_weights` replaces the `self.weights` buffer.

This PR skips the check only while tracing, so eager and the non-compileable caches keep growing the table as before. The block is shared through `# Copied from` by `xglm`, `m2m_100`, `nllb_moe`, `kosmos2`, `kosmos2_5`, `seamless_m4t` and `seamless_m4t_v2`, so all of them are updated.

`_can_compile_fullgraph` is turned on for `m2m_100` (its `False` comment pointed at exactly this branch), `xglm` and `kosmos2_5`, which enables the existing compile and export tests for them. The others keep it off because this was not their only blocker: `nllb_moe` cannot specialize the unbacked `u0` in its expert routing loop, `kosmos2` unpacks a 4D mask as 2D in `_expand_mask`, and the two `seamless_m4t` test classes have no `GenerationTesterMixin`.

### Known limitation

Past `max_position_embeddings` a compileable cache now reaches the index instead of the reallocation and fails with an out-of-range index. That combination did not work before either, since tracing stopped at the branch, and `generate` clamps the default `max_length` to `max_position_embeddings`.

## Verification

A100 80GB, `torch 2.14.0+cu130`, fp32.

```python
import torch

from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
from transformers.generation.configuration_utils import CompileConfig

model_id = "facebook/xglm-564M"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, dtype=torch.float32).to("cuda").eval()
inputs = tokenizer("The capital of France is", return_tensors="pt").to("cuda")

kw = dict(max_new_tokens=20, min_new_tokens=20, do_sample=False)
eager = model.generate(**inputs, **kw, disable_compile=True)
comp = model.generate(**inputs, **kw, cache_implementation="static", compile_config=CompileConfig(fullgraph=True))
print("match:", eager[0].tolist() == comp[0].tolist())
```

Before, this raises `torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported: Data-dependent branching` at `modeling_xglm.py:99`. After, it prints `match: True`. `facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M` behaves the same at `modeling_m2m_100.py:141`.

Reverting the fix while keeping the flags makes the 15 compile and export tests of the three models fail, so they cover it. They only cover the `torch.is_tensor(max_pos)` half of the condition though: narrowing the guard to `if not torch.is_tensor(max_pos) and ...` leaves them green while breaking eager with a compileable cache, where `max_pos` is a tensor but nothing is being traced and the table must still grow. The added `XGLMModelTest::test_sinusoidal_embeddings_grow_in_eager_with_compileable_cache` pins that case down.

Full suites for `xglm`, `m2m_100` and `kosmos2_5` are green apart from failures that reproduce on `main`. `utils/check_copies.py` is clean.

prs.title: Fix BLOOM crash with static cache / compiled generate
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49481)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

generate(..., cache_implementation="static") (or any compile_config, which implies a static cache) crashes on BLOOM when no attention_mask is passed:
```
File "transformers/models/bloom/modeling_bloom.py", line 62, in build_alibi_tensor
    batch_size, seq_length = attention_mask.shape
ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)
```
Repro:
```
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("bigscience/bloomz-560m")
inputs = tok(["hello world"], return_tensors="pt")
model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=8, cache_implementation="static")
```
Cause: BLOOM needs a 2D mask for ALiBi, so BloomForCausalLM.prepare_inputs_for_generation overwrites the 4D mask created by GenerationMixin. But that override is guarded by attention_mask is not None, while the 4D conversion in GenerationMixin runs on attention_mask is None or ndim == 2 — i.e. it also injects a 4D mask when none was passed. So in the None case the corrective branch is skipped and the 4D mask reaches build_alibi_tensor.

Fix: drop the attention_mask is not None guard and build a 2D all-ones mask from input_ids when it is None.

prs.title: Keep packed sequences apart in the torch references of the conv, gated delta rule and Mamba2 scan
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49477)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

Fixes #49472.

The torch references of `causal_conv1d_fn`, `chunk_gated_delta_rule` and `mamba_chunk_scan_combined` now take `seq_idx` / `cu_seqlens`, so packed sequences stay apart when causal-conv1d, flash-linear-attention or mamba-ssm isn't installed, instead of leaking into each other.

- `causal_conv1d_fn` (qwen3_next, mamba2): masks the conv window where `seq_idx` differs from the position's, like #46633 did for LFM2.
- `torch_chunk_gated_delta_rule` (qwen3_next): with `cu_seqlens`, runs each sequence on its own, with one initial and final state per sequence like flash-linear-attention.
- `mamba2_chunk_scan` (mamba2): with `seq_idx`, scans each sequence of a row on its own.

The other models get these through modular (Qwen3.5, Qwen3.5-MoE, Olmo-hybrid, LFM2, Bamba, Falcon-H1, GraniteMoeHybrid, Nemotron-H, Zamba2, ...).

A document packed after another vs the same document alone, max |Δlogp|, fp32, none of the three packages installed (packed first in parentheses, no leak possible):

| model | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 6.8 (1.4e-5) | 1.1e-5 (1.1e-5) |
| tiny Qwen3.5 | 9.1e-3 (9.5e-7) | 9.5e-7 (9.5e-7) |
| tiny Qwen3.5-MoE | 8.4e-4 (9.5e-7) | 9.5e-7 (9.5e-7) |
| tiny Nemotron-H | 1.2e-2 (9.5e-7) | 0 (0) |
| tiny LFM2 | 3.7e-2 (0) | 0 (0) |

Against the kernels on random packed inputs: the conv matches `kernels-community/causal-conv1d` with `seq_idx` to 1.4e-6 (5.6 without the boundaries), and the delta rule matches flash-linear-attention with `cu_seqlens` to 4.4e-4, the same gap as on a single sequence.

The delta rule and the Mamba2 scan loop over the sequences, which takes a host sync on the boundaries. These are the reference paths, already more than an order of magnitude slower than the kernels.

With #49474, a reference that declares `seq_idx` / `cu_seqlens` receives them instead of raising, so the two PRs compose: this one fixes the three references, #49474 keeps raising for any reference that doesn't handle them.

New tests (packed matches each sequence run on its own) for the three references: fail on main, pass here.

prs.title: Trainer: retain unused-parameter detection with non-reentrant checkpointing
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49476)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Keep DDP unused-parameter detection enabled for Trainer-managed non-reentrant gradient checkpointing. Disabling it for every checkpointing mode makes training fail when a model component receives no gradients, such as a vision component during text-only training.

Fixes #49443

Explicit `ddp_find_unused_parameters` settings still take precedence. Reentrant checkpointing, legacy setters that ignore checkpoint kwargs, and checkpointing enabled outside Trainer retain their conservative defaults. The decision follows Trainer's normalization of `every_n_layers` and `offload`, including the distinction between empty kwargs and nonempty kwargs without `use_reentrant`. TrainingArguments documentation describes the revised defaults.

## Validation

- The default-checkpointing regression fails on untouched upstream `429e69162e2944922e45c2cea24887d32e96fbe7` and passes with this patch.
- Related DDP, gradient checkpointing and gradient accumulation tests: 18 passed, 1 skipped (requires multiple accelerators).
- Real CPU/Gloo training with two processes, tiny GPT-2 and an unused projection: upstream fails with `Expected to have finished reduction`; the patch completes three steps on both ranks.
- Reentrant/no-unused control: both ranks complete three steps with detection still disabled.
- All five `make style` equivalent checks passed. The branch was updated to main `536ecc007387a50e77603bb5d92100e9b07514cc`; range-diff confirms the patch is unchanged by the rebase.

```bash
python -m pytest tests/trainer/test_trainer.py -k 'TrainerDDPKwargsTest or TrainerGradientCheckpointingTest or TrainerGradientAccumulationTest' -q
```

The reported Qwen VLM/B300 workload, GPU performance, and full test/repository consistency suites were not run. Earlier broad typing checks on the original base returned the same 81 diagnostics on the patch and untouched source under the local dependency environment; no clean repository-wide typing result is claimed. Unused-parameter traversal has a potential runtime cost; no speedup is claimed. Explicit `ddp_find_unused_parameters=False` remains the opt-out when appropriate.

<details>
<summary>CPU two-process reproducer</summary>

Save as `repro.py` and run `python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node=2 repro.py` against the upstream and patched source. This requires no model download.

```python
import torch
from transformers import GPT2Config, GPT2LMHeadModel, Trainer, TrainingArguments

torch.set_num_threads(1)
torch.manual_seed(0)
model = GPT2LMHeadModel(
    GPT2Config(n_layer=1, n_head=2, n_embd=8, vocab_size=32, n_positions=16, use_cache=False)
)
model.unused_projection = torch.nn.Linear(8, 8)
dataset = [
    {"input_ids": torch.tensor([1, 2, 3, 4]), "labels": torch.tensor([1, 2, 3, 4])}
    for _ in range(16)
]
args = TrainingArguments(
    output_dir="ddp-repro",
    use_cpu=True,
    gradient_checkpointing=True,
    gradient_checkpointing_kwargs=None,
    ddp_find_unused_parameters=None,
    max_steps=3,
    per_device_train_batch_size=2,
    save_strategy="no",
    logging_strategy="no",
    report_to="none",
    disable_tqdm=True,
    dataloader_pin_memory=False,
)
trainer = Trainer(model=model, args=args, train_dataset=dataset)
trainer.train()
assert trainer.state.global_step == 3
```

prs.title: Raise when a torch fallback would drop packed-sequence boundaries
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49474)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

Fixes #49472.

The torch references of `causal_conv1d_fn`, `mamba_chunk_scan_combined` and `chunk_gated_delta_rule` don't take `seq_idx` / `cu_seqlens`, and `use_kernel_func_from_hub_with_fallback` dropped them, so packed sequences silently leaked into each other whenever causal-conv1d, flash-linear-attention or mamba-ssm wasn't installed. This raises instead and names the package to install.

The repro from the issue with this PR: 0.0007 with both packages, and with one or none:

```
ValueError: `causal_conv1d_fn` can't keep packed sequences apart without `causal_conv1d`. Install `causal_conv1d` to train on packed sequences.
```

Unpacked padded batches still train on the fallback (Qwen3.5-0.8B, neither package).

As suggested, any `seq_idx` / `cu_seqlens` reaching a reference now raises, including ones that mark a single sequence. Your call on this one: it also breaks callers that pass them for unpacked inputs without the package, e.g. `test_kwargs_reach_mamba2_mixer` (mamba2, nemotron_h), which now accepts the refusal since it only checks that `seq_idx` is delivered. Exempting a single sequence avoids that, at the cost of the checks you wanted gone.

New test `test_fallback_raises_on_packed_sequence_boundaries` fails on main, passes here, along with the other fallback tests.

prs.body:

# What does this PR do?

Adds [Kolibri 1](https://huggingface.co/Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1) (`kolibri1`), modular on top of Qwen3-MoE.

Fixes #49281. Aleph Alpha said in [Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1 discussion #2](https://huggingface.co/Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1/discussions/2) (2026-10-03) that they are working on native Transformers support; there was no PR as of 2026-10-09. @hmellor agreed on Slack that I open this one.

Differences from Qwen3-MoE:
- Four sliding-window layers per full-attention layer; RoPE only on the sliding-window layers (EXAONE 4 attention).
- Sandwich norms (GLM-4 decoder layer).
- Router: top-k on `logits + e_score_correction_bias`, weights `sigmoid(logits)`. Logits are fp32; on CUDA with torch >= 2.8 and grad disabled they come from `torch.mm(x, w.t(), out_dtype=torch.float32)` instead of upcasting both operands.
- Ungated shared expert added to the routed output (DeepSeek-V3 MoE block).
- `conversion_mapping.py`: qwen2_moe expert merge plus renames of `moe.router.expert_bias`, `post_attn_norm` and `post_ffn_norm`.

Tests:
- CPU (main `5c9f079ca0`, torch 2.14.1): `pytest tests/models/kolibri1` 155 passed, 157 skipped; `make check-repo` passes except `types`, which fails identically on main.
- The Hub `config.json` loads with `AutoConfig`, and every weight key in the Hub `model.safetensors.index.json` maps onto the model through the conversion mapping.
- GPU (DGX Spark, torch 2.13): the `torch.mm` path gives the same logits as the upcast path, and a backward pass works. Through vLLM's Transformers backend, the real FP8 weights score 94.2% on GSM8K (1242/1319), the same as vLLM's native Kolibri implementation.

prs.title: Ernie4.5-VL-MoE: shard the text and vision experts under TP and EP
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49462)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

Its expert plans named `layers.*.mlp.experts`, which never matched the text and vision experts under `mlp.text_moe` / `mlp.vision_moe`, so every expert stayed replicated. The plans now name both.

Loading needed one change, kept generic: the checkpoint stores text then vision experts in one list, which `ErnieFuseAndSplitTextVisionExperts` splits into two stacks. The loader now hands the sharding op each tensor's position in the list its converter collects, and `DtensorShardOperation` treats that position as a first-dim slice index only when the tensor has one dim fewer than the parameter, wrapping it around the parameter's first dim. So each stack is indexed on its own and expert-parallel loading keeps whole experts on their rank. No conversion op or loader code knows about experts or Ernie; a list tensor that isn't a slice takes the full-tensor path as before.

prs.body:

<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Keep AutoVideoProcessor class lookup lazy after the backend registration update in #48984.

Loading a single built-in video processor currently resolves every entry in `VIDEO_PROCESSOR_MAPPING`. For a local LLaVA-OneVision or Qwen3-VL configuration, this imports 32 video processor modules instead of one. The legacy image configuration path also resolves unrelated configuration classes.

This changes the two built-in lookup loops to use `VIDEO_PROCESSOR_MAPPING_NAMES`, while keeping explicitly registered classes and backend overrides first. This follows the name-only lookup already used by AutoImageProcessor. There is no change to processor outputs, public signatures, registration, or supported backends.

Fixes #49451

## Tests

The added test uses real local configuration files and the public `AutoVideoProcessor.from_pretrained` path. A wrapping spy verifies that the full registry is not resolved. Both configuration cases fail before the fix and pass afterward. Existing custom-backend, missing-dependency, remote-code, and save/reload tests remain in place.

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/models/auto/test_video_processing_auto.py tests/models/auto/test_image_processing_auto.py tests/models/auto/test_processing_auto.py tests/models/llava_onevision/test_video_processing_llava_onevision.py tests/models/qwen3_vl/test_video_processing_qwen3_vl.py

ruff format --check src/transformers/models/auto/video_processing_auto.py tests/models/auto/test_video_processing_auto.py

```

On main revision `4cc2aa8430`, the five official CPU test files pass with 92 passed and 11 existing skips using pytest 8.4.2. `make check-repo` passes all 26 checks, with 23 run and 3 successful content-hash cache entries reused. Changed-file Ruff lint and format checks and `git diff --check` also pass.

Fresh-process CPU measurements on main revision `fa40619176`, without a registry spy, reduce the legacy image-config loading median from 2.270 s to 0.002 s for LLaVA-OneVision and from 2.207 s to 0.018 s for Qwen3-VL. prs.title: Fix a port allocation race in FSDP tests
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49455)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# PR body

## What does this PR do?

I ran into intermittent FSDP failures while looking at the CI results for #49446. The first rank would fail with `EADDRINUSE`, and the other ranks would then report Gloo connection errors.

The test helper currently finds a free port by binding a temporary socket and immediately closing it. The distributed workers are spawned afterwards, so another pytest-xdist worker can take the same port in between.

This change lets the parent process create the rendezvous `TCPStore` on an OS-assigned port and keeps that store alive until `mp.spawn` finishes. The child processes connect to it as clients and pass the store directly to `init_process_group`. That removes the window where the selected port was unreserved.

The change is limited to the FSDP test helper.

- Observed failure: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/actions/runs/37881644584/job/113662990603

## Validation

- `make check-repo`
- `make style`
- Re-ran the two FSDP tests that failed in the original CI shard: `2 passed in 25.30s`
- Ran the new `TCPStore` setup under concurrent load: 1,280 parent/client round trips completed successfully with 32 workers

Targeted test command:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src RUN_FSDP_TESTS=1 python -m pytest -q -rs -m is_fsdp_test \
  tests/models/cohere2_moe/test_modeling_cohere2_moe.py::Cohere2MoeModelTest::test_fsdp2_sharding_structure_0_untied \
  tests/models/cohere2_moe/test_modeling_cohere2_moe.py::Cohere2MoeModelTest::test_fsdp2_save_load
```

prs.title: Fix loading legacy remote-code models without `all_tied_weights_keys`
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49454)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

**Description**

This PR makes model loading tolerant of legacy remote-code models that do not define the runtime `all_tied_weights_keys` attribute.

Current loading code assumes `model.all_tied_weights_keys` is always present in a few loading paths, including caching allocator warmup and missing-key handling. Native Transformers models normally get this attribute from `PreTrainedModel.post_init()`, where it is expanded from `_tied_weights_keys`.

Some remote-code wrapper models do not call `post_init()` after composing their submodules, and therefore the top-level model may not have `all_tied_weights_keys`. For example, `openbmb/MiniCPM-V-4_5` fails during loading with:

```text
AttributeError: 'MiniCPMV' object has no attribute 'all_tied_weights_keys'
```

This PR treats a missing `all_tied_weights_keys` attribute as an empty mapping in the relevant loading code paths:

```python
getattr(model, "all_tied_weights_keys", {})
```

This preserves existing behavior for native models and models that do define tied-weight metadata, while allowing older remote-code models without top-level tied-weight metadata to load.

prs.title: fix bridgetower cross-attn mask shape bug
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49447)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

`extend_image_masks` is built from the full image sequence, so it has q_len == num_image_tokens. But it's also passed as encoder_attention_mask to `cross_modal_text_layers`, where the query is the text sequence — the scores are [B, heads, text_len, num_image_tokens] and the add blows up:


RuntimeError: Attempting to broadcast a dimension of length 442 at -2!Mismatching argument at index 1 had torch.Size([1, 1, 442, 442]);but expected shape should be broadcastable to [1, 16, 2, 442]
The text mask right above already slices to q_len == 1 for exactly this reason ("weird case where the mask always wants q_len == 1"). This applies the same to the image mask, which then broadcasts correctly in both uses — image self-attention/link towers and text cross-attention.

It wasn't caught before because pixel_mask is all ones, so SDPA skips mask creation entirely. The skip is disabled under torch.compile (padding_mask.all() is data-dependent), which is where it surfaces — and in eager it would break as soon as the padding mask isn't all ones.

Repro, fails before / passes after:
```
model = torch.compile(BridgeTowerModel.from_pretrained("BridgeTower/bridgetower-large-itm-mlm-itc"))
model(**tokenizer(["a photo"], return_tensors="pt", add_special_tokens=False),
      pixel_values=torch.randn(1, 3, 294, 294))
```

prs.title: [Model] Add native Ling 3.0 Flash support
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49446)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

This PR adds native Transformers support for
[`inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash`](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash).

Ling currently ships its modeling code in the checkpoint repository and therefore needs
`trust_remote_code=True`. This integration adds the `bailing_hybrid` architecture to Transformers, including
`BailingHybridConfig`, `BailingHybridModel`, and `BailingHybridForCausalLM`, so the released checkpoint can be loaded
through the regular `AutoModelForCausalLM` path.

The model uses a 5:1 pattern of Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) and Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) layers. Most of the
building blocks already exist in Transformers, so the implementation reuses the KDA and causal-convolution path from
`glm5_next`, the decoder structure from Kimi Linear, the model forward from Qwen3 Next, and the MLA and MoE components
from DeepSeek-V3. The remaining Ling-specific parts are the hybrid layer layout, gated MLA output, direct-projection KDA
forget gate, checkpoint mapping, and cache and mask handling.

One detail worth calling out is the short-convolution weight layout. The released checkpoint stores separate q, k,
and v convolution kernels, while the native KDA implementation uses one packed depthwise convolution. These weights
are packed once during checkpoint loading rather than concatenated on every forward or decoding step. The mapping
also supports native-key checkpoints and save/load round trips.

The released checkpoint contains an auxiliary MTP layer after the 42 inference layers. It is used during pretraining
and is intentionally ignored by the standard causal language model.

Documentation, AutoClass registration, parallelism plans, and model tests are included. The KDA path has a PyTorch
fallback and can use compatible optimized KDA and causal-convolution kernels when they are installed.

## Testing

On the rebased head (`367f7d842`), I ran the `bailing_hybrid` model test suite on AIStudio/H20-3e:

```text
160 passed, 155 skipped, 1 deselected, 0 failed
```

The single deselected item is the shared `test_training_overfit`: this environment has the optional CUDA-only `causal-conv1d` package installed, while that generic test forces the model onto CPU. The regular training/backward test and all three gradient-checkpointing variants pass. I also exercised the pure PyTorch fallback forward/backward separately and observed a finite loss with all 33 gradient tensors finite.

This includes generation, training and backward, gradient checkpointing, cached decoding, padding-mask continuation,
save/load, loading already-mapped keys, CPU offload, safetensors disk offload, and FP32 handling for sensitive KDA
state.

After the review refactor, I reran the targeted compile and cache regressions. Fullgraph generation now completes two
sequential generation calls without a graph break or recompilation, including a second call with a smaller maximum
length. Cached decoding still matches the cacheless full forward.

I also checked every key in the official checkpoint index against a meta-initialized native model:

```text
source keys: 63783
mapped keys: 819
native target keys: 800
ignored training-only MTP keys: 19
missing keys: []
unexpected keys: []
```

### Full-checkpoint parity

I ran an end-to-end comparison with the full Ling 3.0 Flash checkpoint on H20-3e GPUs in BF16. The baseline used the
model repository's remote code with Transformers 4.56.2 and `fla-core==0.5.2`; the candidate used the native
implementation from this PR. Both runs used the same config, tokenizer, weights, prompt, eager MLA, and cached greedy
decoding.

The local formal checkpoint used for this run has the same 63,783 tensor keys and the same total tensor size
(`254,973,142,144` bytes) as the published safetensors index. I could not compare shard hashes because the public
weight CDN was unavailable from the test environment.

The remote-code baseline only enables the auxiliary MTP training layer when labels are supplied, so MTP was naturally
excluded from both inference paths.

The native and remote-code paths produced the same greedy token at all 32 decoding steps:

| Metric | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| Greedy tokens | 32 / 32 identical |
| Logit argmax | 32 / 32 identical |
| Logit cosine similarity | 0.99894 |
| Mean KL divergence | 0.0001266 |
| Mean total variation distance | 0.001022 |
| Mean top-10 overlap | 94.06% |
| Mean absolute logit difference | 0.1222 |
| Maximum absolute logit difference | 2.5938 |
| NaN / Inf | 0 / 0 |

I repeated a full-vocabulary, 8-token forward after the review changes. It produced a cosine similarity of `0.999196`,
a mean absolute logit difference of `0.07761`, and a maximum absolute difference of `0.96289`. Top-10 overlap was
`92.5%`, and top-1 matched at 7 of 8 positions. At the only differing position, the baseline's two leading logits
were separated by `0.0625` and the native path swapped those same two candidates. All logits were finite.

The raw BF16 differences accumulate across the 42 layers because the native path uses the packed causal-convolution
and KDA interfaces, but the resulting probability distributions and greedy output remain closely aligned.

I also recorded wall-clock time for the same 32-token generation run:

| Measurement | Remote-code baseline | Native implementation | Observed change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Weight loading | 166.33 s | 52.00 s | 68.7% faster |
| 32-token cached generation | 23.99 s | 16.99 s | 29.2% faster |

These are single-run measurements from the same machine rather than a formal benchmark. The two paths use different
Transformers loading implementations, so the loading result in particular should be treated as an observation, not
as a general performance claim. In a separate post-review run, the native 8-token full forward took `0.220 s` after
kernel warmup; the first call included kernel initialization and compilation and was therefore not used as a steady-
state measurement.

Ruff, the modular-model consistency check, the config-attribute check, and `git diff --check` pass as well.

prs.title: Stop treating HunYuan's DynamicNTKAlpha RoPE as dynamic
prs.body:
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49445) ## What does this PR do? HunYuan configs declare `rope_type="dynamic"`, but when `alpha` is set the model uses its own DynamicNTKAlpha variant: ```python base = rope_theta * alpha ** (head_dim / (head_dim - 2)) inv_freq = 1.0 / (base ** (torch.arange(0, dim, 2) / head_dim)) ``` `inv_freq` is derived from `alpha` alone and never depends on the sequence length, so it does not need to be recomputed in the forward pass. The rotary embedding kept advertising itself as dynamic though, so `@dynamic_rope_update` still ran the standard NTK update on every forward. That update branches on `torch.max(position_ids) + 1`, which is a tensor, so `fullgraph=True` fails and the default static-cache path pays a graph break per step. It is also incorrect past `max_position_embeddings`, where it overwrites the alpha-derived frequencies with standard NTK ones. This PR gives the variant its own rope type, `ntk_alpha`, set on the module when the config asks for `dynamic` with an `alpha`. The config itself is left untouched, so checkpoints keep round-tripping as `dynamic`. The formula moves into `compute_ntk_alpha_rope_parameters`, next to `compute_default_rope_parameters`, and `ntk_alpha` joins `axial` and `default` in the rope init registry used by `_init_weights`. That lets all three models drop their `_init_weights` copy of the formula above. A plain `dynamic` config without `alpha` is unaffected and still has its frequencies recomputed every step. The hand-written part is 4 files, +37/-59 — `modeling_utils.py` gains one registry entry and the rest is deletion. The other three files in the diff are regenerated by the modular converter. This is the same bug as #48960, extended to `hunyuan_v1_dense` and `hunyuan_v1_moe` as asked for there. ## Reproduction
repro.py ```python import torch from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer from transformers.generation.configuration_utils import CompileConfig model_id = "tencent/HY-MT1.5-1.8B" device = torch.accelerator.current_accelerator().type tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id) model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, dtype=torch.bfloat16).to(device) inputs = tokenizer("Machine translation is", return_tensors="pt").to(device) out = model.generate( **inputs, max_new_tokens=8, do_sample=False, cache_implementation="static", compile_config=CompileConfig(fullgraph=True), ) print(tokenizer.decode(out[0], skip_special_tokens=True)) ```
Before: ``` torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported: Data-dependent branching Explanation: Detected data-dependent branching (e.g. `if my_tensor.sum() > 0:`). Dynamo does not support tracing dynamic control flow. The branch condition involves a tensor computed as follows: # File "transformers/modeling_rope_utils.py", line 88, in dynamic_frequency_update, code: seq_len = torch.max(position_ids) + 1 max_1 = max(l_kwargs_position_ids_) seq_len = add(max_1, 1) # File "transformers/modeling_rope_utils.py", line 100, in dynamic_frequency_update, code: if seq_len > max_seq_len_cached: # growth gt = gt(seq_len, 262144) ``` After: ``` Machine translation is a process of interpreting the source text into ``` ## Speedup One A100 80GB, `torch==2.14.0+cu130`, bf16, batch 1, 128 new tokens, greedy, median of 5 runs after 2 warmups. | | before | after | | --- | --- | --- | | eager | 36.7 tok/s (3.489 s) | 37.0 tok/s (3.461 s) | | static cache, auto-compiled | 152.8 tok/s (0.838 s) | 167.9 tok/s (0.762 s) | | static cache, `fullgraph=True` | fails to compile | 169.5 tok/s (0.755 s) | Removing the graph break is worth 1.10x on the default static-cache path, and `fullgraph=True` reaches 4.58x over eager.
bench.py — run as python bench.py {eager,compiled,fullgraph} ```python import sys import time import torch from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer from transformers.generation.configuration_utils import CompileConfig # One mode per process: torch.compile state leaks between configs otherwise. MODES = { # `cache_implementation="static"` auto-compiles on CUDA, so the eager baseline needs `disable_compile` "eager": {"disable_compile": True}, "compiled": {"cache_implementation": "static"}, "fullgraph": {"cache_implementation": "static", "compile_config": CompileConfig(fullgraph=True)}, } mode = sys.argv[1] model_id = "tencent/HY-MT1.5-1.8B" device = torch.accelerator.current_accelerator().type NEW_TOKENS, WARMUP, RUNS = 128, 2, 5 tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id) model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, dtype=torch.bfloat16).to(device).eval() inputs = tokenizer("Machine translation is", return_tensors="pt").to(device) def run(): return model.generate( **inputs, max_new_tokens=NEW_TOKENS, min_new_tokens=NEW_TOKENS, do_sample=False, **MODES[mode] ) for _ in range(WARMUP): run() torch.cuda.synchronize() times = [] for _ in range(RUNS): t0 = time.perf_counter() run() torch.cuda.synchronize() times.append(time.perf_counter() - t0) median = sorted(times)[RUNS // 2] print(f"{mode:10s} {median:.3f} s {NEW_TOKENS / median:6.1f} tok/s") ```
## Correctness and scope Eager greedy decoding of 128 tokens on `tencent/HY-MT1.5-1.8B` gives identical token ids before and after, and `inv_freq.sum()` is `4.464970302122e+00` on both sides. Only `rotary.rope_type` changes, from `dynamic` to `ntk_alpha`. The one numerical difference appears past `max_position_embeddings`, which is exactly the overwrite this PR removes. Calling the rotary embedding once with `position_ids` starting at `max_position_embeddings`, `inv_freq.sum()` becomes `7.459945343318e+00` before — the alpha-derived frequencies silently replaced by standard NTK ones — and stays at `4.464970302122e+00` after.
check.py ```python import torch from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer model_id = "tencent/HY-MT1.5-1.8B" device = torch.accelerator.current_accelerator().type tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id) model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, dtype=torch.bfloat16).to(device) rotary = model.model.rotary_emb print("rope_type:", rotary.rope_type) print("inv_freq.sum():", f"{rotary.inv_freq.double().sum().item():.12e}") inputs = tokenizer("Machine translation is", return_tensors="pt").to(device) out = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=128, do_sample=False, disable_compile=True) print("tokens:", out[0].tolist()) # force the dynamic branch: position_ids past max_position_embeddings offset = model.config.max_position_embeddings ids = inputs["input_ids"] position_ids = torch.arange(offset, offset + ids.shape[1], device=ids.device).unsqueeze(0) with torch.no_grad(): rotary(model.get_input_embeddings()(ids), position_ids=position_ids) print("inv_freq.sum() after:", f"{rotary.inv_freq.double().sum().item():.12e}") ```
All three families ship affected checkpoints. `tencent/Hunyuan-A13B-Instruct`, `Hunyuan-7B-Instruct` and `Hunyuan-1.8B-Instruct` declare `rope_scaling={"type": "dynamic", "alpha": 1000.0, ...}`. `tencent/HunyuanOCR` declares `rope_type="xdrope"`, which `HunYuanVLTextConfig` normalizes to `dynamic`, and it carries `alpha=1000.0` as well, so `hunyuan_vl` takes the same branch. `tests/models/hunyuan_v1_dense tests/models/hunyuan_v1_moe tests/models/hunyuan_vl` passes: 536 passed, 496 skipped, 3487 subtests passed.

prs.title: Derive packed-sequence boundaries from position_ids in gated-DeltaNet models
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49441&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49441) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49441&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49441)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

Fixes #49440

Gated-DeltaNet layers (Qwen3.5, Qwen3.5-MoE, Qwen3-Next, OlmoHybrid) only separate packed sequences when they get `cu_seq_lens_q` (delta rule) and `seq_idx` (short conv). Attention layers derive the boundaries from `position_ids`, linear-attention layers don't, so a padding-free batch described by `position_ids` only, e.g. `DataCollatorWithFlattening()` with its defaults, silently mixes documents.

This derives `cu_seq_lens_q/k`, `max_length_q/k` and `seq_idx` once per forward from packed `position_ids` when the caller passed none (one packed row, no cache), with a new `packed_sequence_kwargs` helper in `masking_utils`. Attention layers then reuse them instead of re-deriving them in every layer.

Second document packed after the first vs alone, Qwen3.5-0.8B: max |Δlogp| 1.96 on main, 0.044 (bf16 noise) with this PR.

```python
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, DataCollatorWithFlattening

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B")
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B", dtype=torch.bfloat16).cuda().eval()
a = tok("The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. " * 20).input_ids
b = tok("Paris is the capital of France, and Berlin is the capital of Germany.").input_ids
batch = DataCollatorWithFlattening()([{"input_ids": a}, {"input_ids": b}])
batch = {k: v.cuda() for k, v in batch.items() if k != "labels"}
with torch.no_grad():
    packed = model(**batch, use_cache=False).logits[0, len(a):]
    alone = model(input_ids=torch.tensor([b]).cuda(), use_cache=False).logits[0]
lp = lambda x: torch.log_softmax(x[:-1].float(), -1).gather(-1, torch.tensor(b[1:]).cuda()[:, None])
print((lp(packed) - lp(alone)).abs().max())
```

`test_padding_free_matches_padded_fast_path_regression` now also runs with the collator's defaults (`position_ids` only), in Qwen3.5, Qwen3.5-MoE and Qwen3-Next; that case fails on main.

Not covered: Qwen4-exp (indexed attention with hyper-connections), and the pure-torch fallbacks (no fla / causal-conv1d), which ignore the boundaries altogether.

prs.title: Use the Hub rotary kernel for inference only on CUDA
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49439&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49439) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49439&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49439)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

With `use_kernels=True`, CUDA training uses `kernels-community/rotary` (`apply_rotary_transformers`, v2). Its forward is right, its backward is not: relative error 2e-3 on the output, 0.98 on the gradient.

```python
import torch
from kernels import get_kernel
from transformers.models.llama.modeling_llama import apply_rotary_pos_emb

fn = get_kernel("kernels-community/rotary", version=2).layers.apply_rotary_transformers()
torch.manual_seed(0)
q0 = torch.randn(2, 16, 1024, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
k0 = torch.randn(2, 8, 1024, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
pos = torch.arange(1024, device="cuda").float()
inv = 1.0 / (1e6 ** (torch.arange(0, 128, 2, device="cuda").float() / 128))
emb = torch.cat([pos[:, None] * inv] * 2, -1)[None]
cos, sin = emb.cos().to(torch.bfloat16), emb.sin().to(torch.bfloat16)
gq, gk = torch.randn_like(q0), torch.randn_like(k0)

def run(f):
    q, k = q0.clone().requires_grad_(), k0.clone().requires_grad_()
    qo, ko = f(q, k, cos, sin)
    ((qo.float() * gq).sum() + (ko.float() * gk).sum()).backward()
    return qo.float(), q.grad.float()

(yr, gr), (yk, gk_) = run(apply_rotary_pos_emb), run(fn)
print(((yk - yr).norm() / yr.norm()).item())   # 2.25e-03
print(((gk_ - gr).norm() / gr.norm()).item())  # 0.98
```

It affects every model with the `rotary_pos_emb` hook (Llama, Qwen3, LFM2, ...). Training still converges, so it goes unnoticed: Qwen3-8B ends 300 steps with a +0.002 loss offset vs eager.

This makes the CUDA entry inference-only, like xpu and rocm. `use_kernels=True` training keeps most of its speedup: +14-27% over eager on Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B and MiniCPM5-2B (one B300).

Root cause in the kernel: huggingface/kernels-community#1212 (the in-place op has no autograd formula, so the backward is the identity). Once a fixed version ships, the CUDA training entry can come back.

prs.title: Port Llama 4's MoE to the shared experts interface
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49432&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49432) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49432&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49432)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

`Llama4TextExperts` ran every expert densely on every token and had no `@use_experts_implementation`, so `grouped_mm`/`batched_mm` and expert parallelism could not apply. It now takes `(hidden_states, top_k_index, top_k_weights)` like every other experts class and each token runs only its routed expert.

The router score scales the experts' input, not their output, so `Llama4TextMoe` scales the input and passes each (token, slot) pair as a top-1 route with unit weight. The router returns
`(logits, scores, indices)`; the logits recorder follows.

The EP plan is the standard experts plan (`grouped_gemm` + `ep_dispatch_experts`): main's plan matched no EP mode and was never applied. The shared-expert add is out of place, since the TP rowwise output is a view autograd forbids modifying in place.

The fbgemm and sequential (compressed-tensors / bnb) Llama 4 experts take the same routed signature.

prs.title: Fix DeepGEMM Mega MoE under expert parallelism
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49428)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

Since DeepSeek-V4 declares `ep_dispatch_experts`, the Mega MoE override left that rule in place: token dispatch wrapped the Mega MoE experts and called them without a process group, so `tp_size=ep_size` runs raised on the first forward. The older `ep_router` + `moe_tp_experts` plan was never applied either, since the override renamed both styles and the mixin matched neither.

Mega MoE dispatches inside its kernel, so it takes over the experts rule (`ep_dispatch_experts` -> `megamoe_experts`), runs on the TP group like masked EP, and requires `ep_size == tp_size`.

prs.title: Fix CI slack reporting: surface crashed/missing model jobs in model_results.json
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49427&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49427) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49427&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49427)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## Problem

When a model CI job crashes hard (OOM kill, container init failure, OCI exec error on upload), it produces no artifact. Currently `notification_service.py` uses artifact presence as the source of truth for which jobs ran — so crashed jobs are completely invisible in `model_results.json`, `job_links.json`, and the Slack report.

## What this fixes

- **Jobs with no artifact are invisible** — `matrix_job_results` was filtered by artifact presence; crashed jobs never appeared in `model_results.json` or `job_links.json`
- **`n_model_jobs_errored_out` undercounted** — crashed jobs weren't counted since they weren't in `model_results`
- **No `job_link` for crashed jobs** — the GitHub job URL was available in already-fetched data but never used for error cases
- **Partial crash undetected** — if one GPU slot crashed and the other succeeded, the crashed slot was silently ignored
- **No per-GPU error signal** — impossible to tell which GPU slot failed or why

## How

Single file changed (`utils/notification_service.py`):

- Build `matrix_job_results` from the full `job_matrix` (not filtered by artifact presence)
- Add `MACHINE_TYPE_TO_GPU` mapping + `matrix_name_to_github_jobs` lookup from already-fetched `github_actions_jobs`
- For all-crash jobs: set `error=True`, populate `job_link` via two-tier lookup (`artifact_name_to_job_map` → `matrix_name_to_github_jobs` fallback)
- For partial crash (one slot missing): detect via `actual_gpus` diff, same treatment
- Add `error_type` per-GPU dict alongside existing `error` bool — values: `"crashed"` / `"incomplete_artifact"` (backwards compatible)

## Note

`error_type: "crashed"` is intentionally vague for now — distinguishing OOM kill / silent exit / container init failure requires log inspection, to be discussed with @tarekziade (transformers-ci PR [#180](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers-ci/pull/180)).

prs.title: Optimize Whisper generation for TPU and device sync
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49426&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49426) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49426&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49426)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## What does this PR do?

This PR optimizes the Whisper generation pipeline to reduce device synchronization points and recompilation on backends like TPU that compile per shape, otherwise it is unusable. The changes convert per-row/per-token device operations into batched fixed-shape operations that can be compiled once and reused.

I modified only two files, with the help of Claude.

**In `logits_process.py` (WhisperTimeStampLogitsProcessor):**
- Moved timestamp validation logic from per-row tensor operations to host-side Python loops, avoiding device syncs
- Converted per-row masking operations into a single batched `masked_fill_` call with fixed shape
- Optimized the timestamp probability check to operate on the entire batch at once instead of per-row loops

**In `generation_whisper.py`:**
- `_postprocess_outputs`: Convert beam indices to host list once instead of indexing with device tensor per step
- `_retrieve_avg_logprobs`: Use `gather` operation to collect all token logprobs in one op, then move to host for summation
- `_retrieve_segment`: Replace `torch.where` and tensor operations with host-side Python list comprehensions to avoid device syncs and shape-dependent recompilation

### Performance Impact

On TPU: these changes are game changing: whisper tests were taking more than h to run; on this branch now they take 52 min (9x faster).
On GPU I run some of the tests (on a T4 via HF jobs) and performance is slightly enhanced (10%), the output is the same as before and the peak CUDA memory is unchanged. 
The only drawback is the host memory usage on CUDA, that in the beam-search case it peaks 124 MB higher (3809 -> 3933 MB).

The optimizations maintain identical functionality while improving performance on TPU and other shape-sensitive backends (I haven't tested, but I guess this might be beneficial for neuron too).
prs.author: tengomucho

prs.title: [tests] Some fixes for test suite failures on TPU
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49425)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

This is a follow-up on #49207.
The idea is to increase the success rate of tests suite passing on TPU (`torch_tpu`). It has few small changes to the shared test infra and adds TPU entries to the integration test expectation of several models.

- full precision fp32 matmul: that is required because `torch_tpu` reads the  `float32_matmul_precision` and sets it to medium, so fp32 matmul are run at reduced precision. Hence the change here.
- `run_test_using_subprocess` runs in process on TPU, because the TPU is locked by the process that opens it, and since pytest already holds it, the subprocess can never open it and the tests fail.
- SDPA tolerances on TPU are set as in CUDA.
- Restore the default device in the global-device save/load test with a try/finally. Before, a failure inside the test left `torch.set_default_device` pointing at the accelerator, and that broke every test that ran after it.
- added `Expectations` in the integration tests for gemma3, gemma3n, gpt2, internvl, llama, mistral3 and qwen2.

Note that there should be no change for CPU/CUDA.

prs.title: Expert-parallel dispatch hands the experts the received rows, not the all-to-all's pending result
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49421)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

The token dispatch's all-to-all is a functional collective: its result is an `AsyncCollectiveTensor`, whose own pointer is null until a torch op waits on it. Experts that go through the torch dispatcher (aten ops, `torch.library` custom ops, a compiled graph) wait implicitly, but a kernel launched straight from Python reads the null pointer and faults with an illegal memory access (Triton-launched expert kernels in eager). The dispatch now always waits on the received rows (`wait_tensor`), once, before any experts implementation sees them, so every implementation gets a plain tensor and the code no longer depends on quantization.

Waiting by default is free or faster ([full benchmarks and profiles](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49421#discussion_r4249715216); Qwen3-MoE shape, 8 layers, A100 over NVLink, `tp_size=ep_size` 2 and 4, median of 100 interleaved runs):

| experts implementation | inference | training |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `grouped_mm` (default) | +1.4% at 4×1024 on 2 ranks (lost overlap of the expert-id sort with the all-to-all), noise elsewhere | noise (≤ +0.4%) |
| `batched_mm` | 2–4% faster | out of memory without this change too |
| `eager` | 15–20% faster | about 5% faster |

The `eager` and `batched_mm` gains are host-side: without the wait, every op on the rows (and on views of them) goes through the wrapper's Python `__torch_dispatch__`. `wait_tensor` passes gradients through unchanged, and the EP forward/backward tests pass with it for eager, `grouped_mm` and `batched_mm`.

# What does this PR do?

prs.body:

[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49419&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49419) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49419&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49419)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

Fixes #49403

In this issue WhisperTokenizer.decode() didn't correctly handle batched torch.Tensor or NumPy array inputs with decode_with_timestamps=True. When receiving a 2D tensor, the code would treat it as a single sequence (rather than batch of sequences), leading to either merging of rows or raising an error. This change makes sure that filtered_ids is converted to a Python object before timestamp batch detection logic so that tensors/array are handled in the same way as list-of-lists inputs
A regression test was added to verify the fix.
Tests:
- uv run python -m pytest tests/models/whisper/test_tokenization_whisper.py -k "decode_with_timestamps_batch_tensor" -v
- uv run python -m pytest tests/models/whisper/test_tokenization_whisper.py -v

The issue was discussed in #49403 and @tarekziade confirmed that I should proceed with the patch.

<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## What does this PR do?

Fixes #49393.

I check the incoming key length together with the existing residual length, treating the empty residual as length zero. This flushes the full-precision cache when a cached-prefix continuation reaches or exceeds `residual_length`.

The regression uses the real Quanto backend and covers empty/nonempty residuals, exact/oversized updates, repeated flushes, below-threshold updates and single-token decoding. It also checks that the complete keys, values and sequence length are preserved.

Coordinated with a maintainer [here](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/49393#issuecomment-6056432217). The issue timeline and independent QuantizedCache/residual searches did not find an overlapping fix. AI assistance was used. I reviewed the full diff and ran the CacheTest suite and cached-prefix generation reproducer locally.

## Validation

- New scenarios: 4 failed / 2 passed before; all 6 passed after.
- `python -m pytest tests/utils/test_cache_utils.py::CacheTest -q -o addopts= --disable-warnings`: 18 passed / 1 skipped on CPU.
- Llama `test_generate_with_quant_cache` and `test_generate_continue_from_past_key_values`: 2 passed.
- The original cached-prefix generate reproduction retains 0 full-precision and 272 quantized tokens, with cache length 272 and output length 273.
- `make fix-repo`, `make check-repo`, `make style` and `git diff --check`: passed.

GPU/HQQ and the full selector-generated suite were not run. A broader offline cache test attempt encountered 3 failures and 22 setup errors while loading uncached pretrained checkpoints; those integration/export cases remain unvalidated locally.

prs.title: PR CI: grant actions: read to the reusable workflow
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49417&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49417) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49417&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49417)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

When a PR CI test shard's pod is OOM-killed (exit 137), the whole job container dies, so no step of that job can report the tests it was running, and the CI dashboards show the PR with no failure. #48282 hit this: `tests_torch` and `tests_generate` shard 2/8 were killed in every run since Oct 1, but the dashboard showed no test failure.

huggingface/transformers-ci#180 adds a follow-up job that reads the killed shard's GitHub log and reports the tests that were running when it died. Reading job logs needs `actions: read` on `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Anonymous access gets a 403, and a secret isn't an option because fork PRs don't receive secrets.

**Merge order:** this PR must merge before huggingface/transformers-ci#180. A job in a reusable workflow that asks for a permission the caller doesn't grant makes the whole PR CI run fail to start.

prs.title: Fix Inkling moe_intermediate_size when dense_intermediate_size is present
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49416&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49416) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49416&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49416)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

Fixes #49411

## What does this PR do?

For checkpoints that ship `dense_intermediate_size` (Inkling-Small), `intermediate_size` holds the
routed experts' width and `dense_intermediate_size` holds the dense MLP width.
`InklingTextConfig.__post_init__` replaced `intermediate_size` with the dense value without saving the
expert width first, so `moe_intermediate_size` stayed at its class default of 3072. For Inkling-Small
the expert weights are 2048 wide (for example `experts.w2_weight` is `[256, 4096, 2048]`), so the
config and the weights disagree.

This copies `intermediate_size` into `moe_intermediate_size` before it is overwritten.

| Config | intermediate_size | moe_intermediate_size |
|---|---|---|
| Inkling-Small (2048, dense 16384) | 16384 | 2048 (was 3072) |
| Full Inkling (3072, dense 24576) | 24576 | 3072 (unchanged) |
| No `dense_intermediate_size` | unchanged | unchanged |

The change is in `modular_inkling.py`, and `configuration_inkling.py` is regenerated from it.
The regression test is `InklingTextModelTests.test_dense_intermediate_size_keeps_expert_width` in
`test_modeling_inkling.py`. It fails without the fix (`3072 != 2048`) and passes with it.

Known limit: a config with both `dense_intermediate_size` and an explicit `moe_intermediate_size`
would have the explicit value overridden. I don't know of a checkpoint like that. If you would
rather support it, I can switch to a `None` default for `moe_intermediate_size`.

I have not run a full `from_pretrained` on the 527 GB checkpoint. The check is the resolved
config against the tensor shapes in the files.

prs.title: Fix SinglePositionMultiTokenCandidateGenerator signature
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49413&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49413) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49413&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49413)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## What does this PR do?

#48982 removed `input_ids`, `model_kwargs`, `inputs_tensor` and `logits_processor` from the `SinglePositionMultiTokenCandidateGenerator` call site and marked them as deprecated, but `input_ids` and `model_kwargs` are still declared as required positional parameters. `@deprecate_kwarg` only emits a warning, it does not supply a default, so every Gemma 4 assistant speculative decoding run raises a `TypeError`.

Both arguments are unused in the body, so this PR gives them a default and moves them after the required ones, matching `MTPCandidateGenerator` and `DFlashTokenCandidateGenerator`.

## Reproduction

```python
import torch

from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer


target_id = "google/gemma-4-E4B-it"
assistant_id = "google/gemma-4-E4B-it-assistant"

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(target_id)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(target_id, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="auto")
assistant = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(assistant_id, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="auto")

messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}]
inputs = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
    messages, add_generation_prompt=True, return_tensors="pt", return_dict=True
).to(model.device)

plain = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=20, do_sample=False)
assisted = model.generate(**inputs, assistant_model=assistant, max_new_tokens=20, do_sample=False)
print("PLAIN   :", tokenizer.decode(plain[0, inputs["input_ids"].shape[1] :], skip_special_tokens=True))
print("ASSISTED:", tokenizer.decode(assisted[0, inputs["input_ids"].shape[1] :], skip_special_tokens=True))
print("MATCH   :", torch.equal(plain, assisted))
```

Before:

```
TypeError: SinglePositionMultiTokenCandidateGenerator.__init__() missing 2 required positional arguments: 'input_ids' and 'model_kwargs'
```

After:

```
PLAIN   : The capital of France is **Paris**.
ASSISTED: The capital of France is **Paris**.
MATCH   : True
```

prs.title: Fix ValueError when loading a fusion-enabled checkpoint twice
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49412)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

…same process


`_register_module_fusion` appends the fusion's converters to the **global** `model_type -> converters` mapping, and raises if a source pattern is already taken. But that check can't tell a real conflict from the converters this same fusion registered last time. Since `from_pretrained` re-runs `register_fusion_patches` on every load, loading the same checkpoint twice always collides with itself:
```python
from transformers import AutoModelForImageTextToText

model_id = "CohereLabs/North-Micro-Vision-Instruct"
AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_pretrained(model_id)   # ok
AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_pretrained(model_id)   # ValueError
```
This PR tries to fix it by making fusion registration idempotent.

prs.title: Fix Parakeet TDT zero-duration stall with max_symbols_per_step guard
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49402&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49402) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49402&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49402)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Fixes #49388.

Parakeet TDT decoding can repeatedly emit non-blank tokens with zero
duration without advancing the encoder frame. The TDT update bypasses
the RNN-T frame update, which also skips its `max_symbols_per_step`
limit. Decoding can then consume the output token budget on one frame
and leave the remaining audio untranscribed.

This change applies the limit to consecutive non-blank, zero-duration
emissions. Once the limit is reached, decoding advances by one frame
and resets the counter. Normal frame advances also reset the counter,
and the forced advance is included in the recorded durations.

The implementation follows the fix proposed by @tomschott in the issue.
No new dependencies are required.

## Validation

Nine isolated CPU/PyTorch checks passed, covering the stall, advancement
at the configured limit, counter resets, independent batch counters,
duration tracking, and encoder completion.

These checks used stubbed generation bookkeeping. Repository tests and
end-to-end audio validation remain pending.

prs.title: Add LFM2 to the GGUF loading path
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49400)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Adds `lfm2` architecture to the new GGUF loading path, so LFM2/2.5 GGUF keep their weights packed and run on the ggml kernels instead of being dequantized when loading.

- `gguf_config_mapping.py`: `_lfm2_config` rebuilds the `Lfm2Config` from the file's metadata. One KV-head count per layer, zero for convolution layers, `layer_types` comes from that list and `num_key_value_heads` is its maximum. `block_auto_adjust_ff_dim=False` keeps the file's FFN width as is.
- `gguf_conversion_mapping.py`: `_lfm2` renames the ggml tensors to the transformers names. The only value transform is `Unsqueeze(1)` on the short-convolution kernel, which llama.cpp stores as 2D. No offset in norms; quantized weights stay packed.
- `test_gguf_integration.py`: `Lfm2GgufModelTest` on `LiquidAI/LFM2.5-230M-GGUF`, using `GgufModelIntegrationTesterMixin`.

The old-path LFM2 code (`GGUF_CONFIG_MAPPING["lfm2"]`, `Lfm2TensorProcessor`) is left in place, since `GGUF_CONFIG_MAPPING` is exported. It is no longer used for LFM2 files, so I can remove it here if you prefer.

### Test evidence

On an M4 Pro (torch 2.13.0, kernels 0.17.2, MPS):

- `RUN_SLOW=1 TRANSFORMERS_TEST_DEVICE=mps pytest tests/quantization/ggml/test_gguf_integration.py -k Lfm2`: 12 passed. The BF16 file matches the safetensors checkpoint bit for bit, every key is accounted for, the config matches the repo’s. Both the packed and dequantized Q4_K_M files complete "Berlin".
