prs.title: Fix MetalLinear batched inputs by flattening before kernel dispatch
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49398&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49398) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49398&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49398)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

`MetalLinear` calls `kernel.affine_qmm_t` which only computes batch element 0 correctly for 3D inputs. As a result, every row after the first in batched inference is corrupted. If we flatten the input to 2D before the kernel call and restore the leading dimensions afterwards:

```python
flat = input.reshape(-1, self.in_features)
output = kernel.affine_qmm_t(flat, ...)
...
return output.reshape(*input.shape[:-1], self.out_features)
```

we can fix the issue in transformers without waiting for a kernel release. The proposed change stays correct even if a proper kernel fix lands in kernels-community later, and is symmetric with how the `GgufLinear.forward` flattens the input.

### Test evidence:

Added a mocked CPU test that checks that 1D–4D and non-contiguous inputs reach the kernel as 2D. Also, an MPS test compares batched vs per-row outputs for 4/8 bits × fp16/bf16 × bias.
On an M4 Pro (torch 2.14.0, kernels 0.17.2): all MPS tests fail on main and pass with the fix.

`TRANSFORMERS_TEST_DEVICE=mps pytest tests/quantization/metal/test_metal.py`: 58 passed, 2 skipped.

Fixes #49337

The fix is to bump our minimum version to 2.6 (which was due anyway), and to add a util that guards that function correctly, then replace direct calls with the util!

Fixes #49380

prs.title: [Docker] Upgrade to torch 2.14/CUDA 13.0 and optimize FA2 build from source
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49381&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49381) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49381&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49381)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## Summary

- Bumps the flash-attn Docker image to **torch 2.14.0 / CUDA 13.0 / torchcodec 0.16.0**
- Replaces the old `pip install flash-attn --no-build-isolation` with a proper from-source build of FA2 v2.8.3.post1 (Dao-AILab stopped publishing wheels for torch≥2.9)

## Key FA2 build optimisations

| Optimisation | Reason |
|---|---|
| `ninja` | Enables parallel compilation; without it falls back to sequential make |
| `wheel` force-reinstall | Ubuntu 22.04 ships wheel 0.37.1 which uses `pkg_resources` removed in setuptools≥83 (pulled in by torch≥2.13) |
| `SKIP_CK_BUILD=True` | setup.py unconditionally compiles ~1100 ROCm composable_kernel `.cu` files on NVIDIA — useless and slow |
| `csrc/cutlass` only | Init only the CUTLASS submodule needed for headers; skip composable_kernel |
| `FLASH_ATTN_CUDA_ARCHS='80'` | Target Ampere only (SM 8.0/8.6 = A10G/A100); skips Hopper/Blackwell and cuts compile time ~4× |
| Dynamic `MAX_JOBS` | Derived from available RAM (`floor(RAM_GB/2.8)` capped at nproc, split with `NVCC_THREADS=4`) to avoid OOM |
| C++17 → C++20 | Required by torch≥2.14 |

FA3 and FA4 are not installed — they require Hopper/Blackwell GPUs; our CI runners use Ampere (A10G).

## Validation

Full Docker build completed successfully in ~27 min on `aws-general-8-plus` (32 vCPU, 123 GB RAM, `MAX_JOBS=8`). Run: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/actions/runs/37521855078

prs.title: [Docker] Optimize FA2/FA3/FA4 install in transformers-all-latest-gpu
prs.body:

[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49377&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49377) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49377&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49377)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## Summary

Replaces the slow/OOM-killing `pip install flash-attn --no-build-isolation` with an optimised build that:

- Installs **FA2** from source in ~15 min (was OOM-killed with exit 137 on CI)
- Installs **FA3** via pre-built wheel from PyTorch official index (seconds, no compile)
- Installs **FA4** via pure-Python wheel from PyPI (seconds, no compile)

### FA2 build optimisations

| Optimisation | Why |
|---|---|
| `ninja` | Enables parallel compilation; without it falls back to sequential `make` |
| `force-reinstall wheel` | Ubuntu 22.04 system wheel (0.37.1) imports `pkg_resources` removed in setuptools≥83 (torch≥2.13 pulls it in) |
| `SKIP_CK_BUILD=True` | Skips ROCm `composable_kernel` (~1100 extra `.cu` files useless on NVIDIA; `setup.py` hardcodes `False` for non-ROCm builds) |
| `csrc/cutlass` only | Init only the CUTLASS submodule needed for headers; skip composable_kernel |
| `FLASH_ATTN_CUDA_ARCHS='80'` | Ampere only (A10G/A100); skips Hopper (90) and Blackwell (100/120), ~4× faster |
| Dynamic `MAX_JOBS`/`NVCC_THREADS` | Derived from available RAM (`floor(RAM_GB/2.8)/4`) to avoid OOM on any runner |
| C++20 patch | torch≥2.14 headers require C++20; `setup.py` still defaults to C++17 |

### Tested on A10G runner (83 GB RAM pod limit)
- Peak RAM: ~34 GB
- Build time: ~15 minutes
- `import flash_attn` + forward pass: ✅

prs.title: [tests] Fix flaky CMVN tests in Speech2TextFeatureExtractionWithoutTorchaudioTest
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49374&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49374) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49374&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49374)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## What

Seeds `global_rng` before each of the 4 CMVN normalization test methods in `Speech2TextFeatureExtractionWithoutTorchaudioTest`.

## Why

The `WithoutTorchaudio` mel implementation has slightly different fp32 precision vs torchaudio. For rare random inputs (from the unseeded `global_rng = random.Random()` in `test_processing_common.py`), CMVN normalization leaves a residual mean just above the `1e-3` threshold, causing sporadic `AssertionError: np.False_ is not true` failures.

Observed failure rates (5000-run flakefinder, no fix):
- `test_cepstral_mean_and_variance_normalization`: ~1/6739 (~0.015%)
- `test_cepstral_mean_and_variance_normalization_np`: ~1/669 (~0.15%)
- `test_cepstral_mean_and_variance_normalization_trunc_max_length`: ~1/1962 (~0.05%)
- `test_cepstral_mean_and_variance_normalization_trunc_longest`: ~1/4635 (~0.02%)

Root cause: `trunc_max_length` truncates to 3 frames → fp32 sum not exactly zero → mean 1.47e-3 > 1e-3 threshold. Same mechanism for others.

Fix: override the 4 methods in the subclass to seed `global_rng(42)` before calling `super()`. The torchaudio class (`Speech2TextFeatureExtractionTest`) is unaffected — 0 failures across hundreds of runs.

Verified: `trunc_max_length` with seed → 5000/5000 passed.

cc @ebezzam
prs.author: ydshieh

prs.title: Fix Pixtral Flash Attention image boundaries after axial RoPE refactor
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49373&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49373) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49373&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49373)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## What does this PR do?

Fixes #49371

Pixtral passes axial RoPE coordinates shaped [total_patches, 2] to the Flash Attention packed-sequence detector. It flattens both coordinates, producing false image boundaries and a terminal cumulative length twice the number of Q/K/V tokens. A checkpoint-free Pixtral model raises a CUDA illegal memory access on Transformers 5.17.0, 5.18.0, and main at 571c5cc; smaller configurations can return incorrect output without crashing. The same reproduction passes on 5.16.1.

This change derives cumulative lengths and maximum lengths from the per-image patch grids, and passes them explicitly in the flash attention case. Keeping axial coordinates for rotary embeddings and preserve the existing block mask for other attention implementations. 

This follows the Qwen2-VL/Qwen3-VL vision-attention approach:
https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/571c5cc726d4a990def359fd44bcb57450e68990/src/transformers/models/qwen3_vl/modeling_qwen3_vl.py#L287-L298

## Related work / coordination

- #48105 introduced the axial-position change.
- Open #47342 normalizes 1D and 3D position IDs. Its current diff leaves this 2D [total_patches, 2] representation unchanged, so it does not fix this reproduction. This proposal instead supplies explicit image boundaries within Pixtral.
- Open #34542 adds SDPA support to Pixtral; it addresses a different problem.
- Searched open issues and PRs on 2026-10-06. No matching fix found

`prepare_distribute_model` raises as soon as `ep_size != tp_size`, before the expert plan is read. The check dates from #48857 and predates token dispatch, whose whole point is `ep_size != tp_size`. Since the stack merged, every dispatch config is rejected, including the new Qwen3-MoE default:

```python
DistributedConfig(fsdp_size=8, ep_size=8)
# ValueError: All-reduce expert parallelism requires `ep_size=tp_size` and identical tokens per EP group.
```

The style-aware version of the same check already runs in `DistributedConfig._validate_mesh_config` (`ep_router` + `moe_tp_experts` with `ep_size != tp_size` still raises), so this just drops the unconditional one.

<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## What

Adds `BitForImageClassification` to `EXPORT_SKIPS["onnx.exactness"]`, alongside its siblings `BitModel` and `BitBackbone` that were already skipped.

## Why

`BitForImageClassification` was missing from the exactness skip list. The same ORT fp32 accumulation through the BiT conv stack causes a ~0.0013 drift on the logits — just over the 1e-3 tolerance. This caused ~4-5% flaky failures on `test_onnx_export_static` (confirmed by 200-run flakefinder: 8 failures, all `BitForImageClassification`).

The max absolute diff observed: **0.00132** (threshold: 0.001), only 1/9 output elements affected. This is numerical noise, not a structural export issue.

cc @IlyasMoutawwakil

prs.title: Fix offloaded cache prefetch racing with the offloading copy
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49363&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49363) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49363&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49363)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

Fixes #48947

The prefetch stream never waited for the default stream, so a prefetch could read the pinned CPU buffer before the non-blocking offload copy had written it, and could reuse the previous prefetch's memory before `torch.cat` read it. One `wait_stream` before each prefetch fixes both.

Script from the issue, 1x H100, 8 runs: argmax now matches at every step on Qwen3.8-27B and Qwen3-8B (was 8/8 and 6/8 runs diverging), remaining diff is within no-offload run-to-run noise. Decode speed unchanged.

The new test fails 5/5 on main, passes 5/5 with the fix.

prs.title: Fix Phi3 LongRoPE cache rebuild at the context boundary
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49361&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49361) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49361&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49361)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## What does this PR do?

Fixes #49334.

When Phi3 generation crosses the original context limit, it clears the KV cache to recompute the prefix with the long RoPE factors. However, `next_sequence_length=1` still makes the base input preparation keep only the last token. I reset that argument alongside the cache so the forward pass receives the full prefix.

The regression compares each generation step with an uncached full-prefix forward before, at, and after the boundary, with and without a sliding window. Phimoe's existing copied method and both generated files are synchronized by `make fix-repo`.

Coordinated in [#49334](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/49334#issuecomment-6016670918). Searches of the issue timeline and open Phi3/LongRoPE PRs did not find an overlapping fix. AI assistance was used.

## Validation

- New regressions: **2 failed before the fix; 2 passed after**.
- `python -m pytest tests/models/phi3/test_modeling_phi3.py tests/models/phimoe/test_modeling_phimoe.py -m 'not slow' -q -o addopts= --disable-warnings`: **303 passed, 233 skipped, 101 deselected** on CPU. These are the two files selected by `utils/tests_fetcher.py`.
- Original issue reproduction: the reset forward receives all 9 prefix tokens, and the generated next tokens **[32, 26]** match the uncached reference.
- `make fix-repo`, `make check-repo`, `make style`, and `git diff --check`: passed.

GPU, distributed, and large-checkpoint slow tests were not run locally.

## Before submitting

- [x] Contributor guidelines and PR checks read.
- [x] Discussed with a maintainer in the linked issue.
- [x] Necessary regression tests added.
- Documentation: no API or configuration change.

prs.title: Fix data-dependent branch in _ignore_causal_mask_sdpa under compile
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49354&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49354) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49354&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49354)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

With a static cache, `q_offset` is a tensor. Under `torch.compile` (torch ≥ 2.14), the condition in `_ignore_causal_mask_sdpa` tests its value, which breaks the graph (`Unsupported: Data-dependent branching` with `fullgraph=True`). A traced `q_offset` now materializes the mask instead.

In `generate()`, this affects chunked prefill, the only path that runs multi-token inputs through the compiled forward. For the first chunk of an unpadded prompt, `prepare_inputs_for_generation` skips the mask because the cache is empty, so the compiled forward rebuilds it and hits that condition.

## Tests

- `test_static_cache_prefill_mask_under_compile` (new): fails on `main`, passes with the fix (torch 2.14.1).
- Compiled chunked prefill (static cache, `fullgraph=True`) fails on `main` with the error above; with the fix, it matches a dynamic-cache `generate()`.

@vasqu @Cyrilvallez

# What does this PR do?

GemmaTokenizer documents `add_bos_token` as defaulting to True, but it inherits the tokenizers backend's False.

A model checkpoint that omits the flag and ships a post-processor without BOS (like every Gemma 4 model repo does).
This tokenizes prompts without the <bos> the model was trained with, and generates poorly from raw text.

Repos that set the flag, either way (Gemma 1-3 True, PaliGemma False), are unchanged.

The ShieldGemma 2 processor test fixture omits the flag, so its prompt gains one token; its max_length is bumped to match.

# Tests

[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49349&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49349) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49349&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49349)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

`DataCollatorForLanguageModeling(tokenizer, seed=0)` silently ignores the seed. The check added in #36497 is `if self.seed and self.generator is None`, so `0` is treated as "no seed", no generator is created, and masking falls back to the global RNG. Any other seed works.

This PR changes both checks (`torch_call` and `numpy_call`) to `self.seed is not None`. That is the whole source change (2 lines).

## Reproducer

```python
import torch
from transformers import BertTokenizerFast, DataCollatorForLanguageModeling

tok = BertTokenizerFast("vocab.txt")  # any tokenizer with a mask token
feats = [{"input_ids": list(range(5, 105))} for _ in range(4)]

for seed in (0, 1, 42):
    for rt in ("pt", "np"):
        outs = []
        for _ in range(2):
            c = DataCollatorForLanguageModeling(tok, seed=seed, return_tensors=rt)
            outs.append(torch.as_tensor(c([dict(f) for f in feats])["input_ids"]))
        print(seed, rt, torch.equal(outs[0], outs[1]), c.generator is not None)
```

On `main` (475e93a):

```
seed=0 return_tensors=pt reproducible=False generator_created=False
seed=0 return_tensors=np reproducible=False generator_created=False
seed=1 return_tensors=pt reproducible=True generator_created=True
seed=1 return_tensors=np reproducible=True generator_created=True
seed=42 return_tensors=pt reproducible=True generator_created=True
seed=42 return_tensors=np reproducible=True generator_created=True
```

With this PR all six lines are `reproducible=True generator_created=True`.

## Tests

- Added `test_mlm_seed_zero_reproducibility` (covers `pt` and `np`). It fails on `main` and passes with the fix.
- `pytest tests/trainer/test_data_collator.py` → 81 passed.
- `make style` (ruff 0.14.10) → all 5 checks passed.

## Code Agent Policy

Disclosure: this bug was found, and the fix, test and this description were written, with a code agent (Claude Code). I am a first-time contributor to this repo, so I am leaving the box below unticked and understand if you would rather close this. There was no prior issue for this; I searched open and closed issues/PRs for the collator seed and found only #36357 / #36497, which introduced the feature.

prs.title: Load deep-gemm on Blackwell: skip the kernels arch check for it
prs.body:
DeepGEMM JIT-compiles its CUDA kernels for the running device, but its build metadata declares only the arch it was packaged on (9.0a), so the kernels arch check rejects it on sm_100 ("CUDA capability 10.0 ... is not supported by the architectures of the build: 9.0a"). The hub kernel mapping gains a per-kernel check_arch flag, off for deep-gemm.

prs.title: fix(pipelines): accept code_revision via model_kwargs without TypeError
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49340&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49340) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=49340&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49340)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

Fixes #49272

**What the user sees:** `pipeline("text-classification", model=..., model_kwargs={"code_revision": "abc123"})` — the documented way to pass extra kwargs to `from_pretrained` — crashes with `TypeError: AutoConfig.from_pretrained() got multiple values for keyword argument 'code_revision'` instead of working. Anyone pinning remote code via `model_kwargs` hits this.

**Root cause:** in `pipeline()` (`src/transformers/pipelines/__init__.py`), `code_revision` is popped from top-level `kwargs` into a local, but a `code_revision` entry inside `model_kwargs` is left in place. Both then reach `AutoConfig.from_pretrained(..., code_revision=code_revision, **model_kwargs)` as duplicate keyword arguments.

**Fix:** resolve `code_revision` from `model_kwargs` the same way `device_map` is already handled a few lines below: raise a clear `ValueError` if it's given in both places (they might conflict), otherwise pop it out of `model_kwargs` into the single resolved local. The three existing explicit call sites (`AutoConfig.from_pretrained`, `get_class_from_dynamic_module`) then receive it exactly once, however it was passed. Deliberately not touching the second half of #49272 (propagating top-level `code_revision` into every loader's `hub_kwargs`) — that's a behavior-design question for maintainers, this keeps the change obviously-correct and minimal.

**Tests:** reproduced the `TypeError` on pristine code with a local config dir (no Hub/torch needed — the crash happens at config-load time); after the patch the config load proceeds, conflicting both-places usage raises the new `ValueError`, and top-level-only usage is unchanged.
prs.author: aniketkrs

prs.title: Trainer: cast the model back in train() after an fp16/bf16 full eval
prs.body:
# What does this PR do?

### What's wrong

With `fp16_full_eval` / `bf16_full_eval`, `evaluation_loop` runs `model.to(dtype=..., device=...)` whenever it is called outside `train()`. `nn.Module.to` works in place, so `self.model` keeps the fp16/bf16 weights and buffers after `evaluate()` / `predict()` returns. A later `train()` (for example after a baseline `evaluate()`) then trains the cast model: parameters and AdamW states are fp16/bf16, there are no fp32 master weights, and `bf16=True` / `fp16=True` autocast changes nothing because the weights are already in half precision. The docstring says these flags "only apply during evaluation".

### Reproduction

```python
import tempfile

import torch
from datasets import Dataset

from transformers import LlamaConfig, LlamaForCausalLM, Trainer, TrainingArguments

config = LlamaConfig(vocab_size=128, hidden_size=64, intermediate_size=128, num_hidden_layers=2, num_attention_heads=4)
model = LlamaForCausalLM(config)  # fp32
ds = Dataset.from_dict({"input_ids": [list(range(16))] * 8, "labels": [list(range(16))] * 8})
args = TrainingArguments(
    tempfile.mkdtemp(), bf16=True, bf16_full_eval=True, max_steps=2, per_device_train_batch_size=4,
    use_cpu=True, report_to="none", save_strategy="no",
)
trainer = Trainer(model=model, args=args, train_dataset=ds, eval_dataset=ds)
trainer.evaluate()  # baseline eval before training
trainer.train()

weight = model.model.layers[0].self_attn.q_proj.weight
print("weight dtype after train():  ", weight.dtype)
print("Adam exp_avg dtype:          ", trainer.optimizer.state[weight]["exp_avg"].dtype)
print("rotary inv_freq dtype:       ", model.model.rotary_emb.inv_freq.dtype)
```

Output on `main` (50e35cc), CPU:

```
weight dtype after train():   torch.bfloat16
Adam exp_avg dtype:           torch.bfloat16
rotary inv_freq dtype:        torch.bfloat16
```

With `fp16=True, fp16_full_eval=True` the same three tensors end up in `torch.float16`.

### Impact

This hits any script that calls `evaluate()` or `predict()` before `train()` with `bf16_full_eval` or `fp16_full_eval`. It also hits `train()` -> `evaluate()` -> `train(resume_from_checkpoint=...)`. Training then runs fully in half precision, without any warning:

- Updates smaller than half a bf16 ulp are lost. gpt2 (fp32 checkpoint), `evaluate()` then one AdamW step at lr=2e-5 with `bf16=True`, CPU: on `main`, 4.9% of the weight elements change. With this PR, 99.4% change.
- Mixed-dtype models are hit too. With PEFT LoRA on a bf16 base, the fp32 adapters and their AdamW states become bf16.
- On top of that, the weights are rounded once: ||W - bf16(W)|| / ||W|| is 1.7e-3 for gpt2 (2.1e-4 for fp16). For Qwen3-0.6B it is 0, because the checkpoint is already bf16.

### Fix

- When `evaluation_loop` does the in-place cast outside `train()`, it first records the dtype of every parameter and buffer of `self.model`. Only the first such call records. Only dtypes are stored, no tensors.
- `train()` casts back each tensor whose dtype changed, logs a warning, and drops the record. The record is dropped without restoring when `model_init` builds a fresh model.
- The restore is per tensor, not a single `model.to(original_dtype)`. That way fp32 LoRA adapters on a bf16 base and `_keep_in_fp32_modules` get their own dtype back.
- Evaluation is unchanged: it still runs on the cast model, and eval memory is the same.
- DeepSpeed and FSDP are left out. Their sharded parameters can't be cast back one tensor at a time, and eval-before-train with them is handled separately (#44889, #44189).

Trade-off: casting back does not undo the one rounding of the weights and buffers (for example RoPE `inv_freq`), and the warning says so. An exact restore would need a full fp32 copy of the model, either a deep copy or kept CPU tensors, and full eval exists to avoid that memory cost. Raising an error in `train()` would also be simple, but it would break the evaluate-then-train pattern. This change keeps that pattern working, with fp32 weights and optimizer states. I'm happy to switch to an error if you prefer.

Not changed: `save_model()` right after a full eval still saves the cast weights. #49288 (closed) and #49294 covered `model.to(dtype)` casting buffers; this PR does not touch modeling code.

### Tests

- New `TrainerFullEvalMemoryTest::test_full_eval_before_train_keeps_training_dtype`, CPU, with fp16 and bf16 subtests. It runs `evaluate()` then `train()` and checks that `a` goes back to fp32, a bf16 `b` stays bf16, and `exp_avg` is fp32. Both subtests fail on `main` (`torch.float16 != torch.float32`, `torch.bfloat16 != torch.float32`) and pass with the fix.
- `test_trainer_evaluation.py`, `test_trainer_hyperparameter.py`, `test_training_args.py`: 33 passed, 10 skipped (GPU / slow / optuna / ray / wandb). With optuna installed, the 3 Optuna tests, including the `fp16_full_eval` one, pass.
- `test_trainer.py`, `test_trainer_checkpointing.py`, `test_trainer_callback.py`: 136 passed, 21 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is `TrainerNEFTuneTest::test_neftune`, which fails the same way on `main` on macOS (MPS placeholder storage error).
- `test_trainer_seq2seq.py`, `test_trainer_data.py`, `test_trainer_optimizers.py`, `test_trainer_accelerator.py`: 60 passed, 34 skipped.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (0.14.10) are clean.
- Not run: the GPU memory tests `test_{fp16,bf16}_full_eval` and DeepSpeed/FSDP.

prs.title: Keep float32 MoE router logits in float32 under autocast
prs.body:
# What does this PR do?

### What's wrong

The DeepSeek-V2/V3-style routers compute their logits as `F.linear(hidden_states.type(torch.float32), self.weight.type(torch.float32))`, and 23 other models copy or inherit these routers. Under `torch.autocast(dtype=torch.bfloat16)`, autocast runs `F.linear` in bf16 and undoes the casts. The logits come back in bf16, so the sigmoid/softmax, bias addition and top-k all run on bf16 scores. Trainer and Accelerate turn on autocast for `bf16=True` (outside DeepSpeed). As a result, a bf16 fine-tune of these models picks different experts than inference does with the same weights.

### Reproduction

```python
import torch
from transformers import DeepseekV3Config
from transformers.models.deepseek_v3.modeling_deepseek_v3 import DeepseekV3TopkRouter

torch.manual_seed(0)
config = DeepseekV3Config(hidden_size=256, n_routed_experts=64, num_experts_per_tok=8, n_group=8, topk_group=4)
router = DeepseekV3TopkRouter(config).eval()
torch.nn.init.normal_(router.weight, std=0.02)
torch.nn.init.normal_(router.e_score_correction_bias, std=0.01)
hidden_states = torch.randn(4096, config.hidden_size)

with torch.no_grad():
    logits, weights, indices = router(hidden_states)
    with torch.autocast("cpu", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
        logits_ac, weights_ac, indices_ac = router(hidden_states)

same_set = (indices.sort(-1).values == indices_ac.sort(-1).values).all(-1)
print("logits dtype:", logits.dtype, "| under autocast:", logits_ac.dtype)
print(f"tokens with a different expert set under autocast: {(~same_set).float().mean():.1%}")
```

On main (50e35cc):
```
logits dtype: torch.float32 | under autocast: torch.bfloat16
tokens with a different expert set under autocast: 10.5%
```
With this change: `torch.float32` and `0.0%`.

### Impact

The bug affects any bf16-autocast training or evaluation of axk1, axk2, bailing_hybrid, beam, deepseek_ocr2, deepseek_v2, deepseek_v3, deepseek_v32, dots1, exaone_moe, glm4_moe, glm4_moe_lite, glm4v_moe, glm5_next, glm_moe_dsa, hy_v3, hy_v4, kimi_linear, kolibri1, longcat_flash, mimo_v2_flash, muse_spark, nemotron_h, solar_open and unlimited_ocr. Ernie 4.5 MoE (text and VL) and Flint already disable autocast around their router matmul, and they behave correctly.

I measured this on `zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash` (glm4_moe_lite, 64 experts, top-4, sigmoid router) with these settings:
- the first 6 decoder layers, which include 5 MoE layers
- bf16 weights, on an RTX 5070 Ti
- 8,192 tokens of the wikitext-2-raw-v1 test split

Each cell is the share of tokens whose top-4 expert set changes under `torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)`:

| MoE layer | same router input | full forward |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.87% | 1.87% |
| 2 | 2.81% | 3.17% |
| 3 | 1.44% | 2.67% |
| 4 | 2.01% | 3.76% |
| 5 | 1.76% | 3.83% |

- When the expert set does not change, routing weights differ by 2e-3 to 4.5e-3 on average (absolute).
- Repeating the forward pass without autocast changes 0.00% of tokens, so GPU nondeterminism is not the cause.
- With this change, under autocast, 0.00% of tokens change in every layer.

### Fix

The router matmul now runs under `maybe_autocast(device_type=device_type, enabled=False)`, the same way `Ernie4_5_MoeTopKRouter` and `FlintTopKRouter` already do it. The explicit casts stay, because bf16 weights still need them when autocast is off.
- I edited the 8 modular roots that define these forwards: deepseek_v2, deepseek_v3, axk2, beam, hy_v3, kolibri1, longcat_flash and muse_spark. The other generated `modeling_*.py` files were regenerated from them.
- Only the matmul needs wrapping. Autocast does not cast `sigmoid`, `topk` or `gather`, and it already runs `softmax` in float32.
- `maybe_autocast` returns a `nullcontext` when autocast is off. Without autocast, outputs are unchanged and torch.compile gets no extra nodes. A `fullgraph=True` compile of the router works both with and without autocast.
- For Kolibri 1, only the `F.linear` branch is wrapped. Its `torch.mm(..., out_dtype=torch.float32)` fast path already returns float32 under CUDA autocast (checked).

Not changed here: routers that compute in the activations' dtype (Qwen3-MoE, Mixtral) don't ask for float32. `MiniMaxM2TopKRouter`, `MiniMaxM3VLTopKRouter` and `Step3p7TopKRouter` (step3p7 is generated from minimax_m3_vl) compute `F.linear(hidden_states.to(self.weight.dtype), self.weight)`, so they run in the gate's dtype.
- MiniMax checkpoints store the router weight in float32, and #50002 keeps it in float32 on load. With an fp32 gate under CPU bf16 autocast, these routers return bf16 logits, and 1.8–2.4% of tokens change expert set (random weights).
- The same wrap works for them unchanged. It runs the matmul in the gate's dtype and leaves bf16 gates as they are (checked). That PR adds it together with the float32 gate. muse_spark subclasses `MiniMaxM2TopKRouter`, but it has its own float32 forward, which is fixed here.

### Tests

- I added `test_router_ignores_autocast` to `tests/models/deepseek_v3` and `tests/models/deepseek_v2`. The test checks that the router output (logits, weights, indices) under `torch.autocast(torch_device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)` equals the output without autocast, and that the logits are float32.
  - On main, both tests fail on CPU with `AssertionError: torch.bfloat16 != torch.float32`.
  - With this change, both pass on CPU. The same test body also passes on CUDA, and fails there on main.
- I ran the existing tests of all 25 affected models (`-k "not slow"`, CPU, macOS): 3889 passed, 2830 skipped, 52 failed.
  - All 52 failures are the TP/EP tests of glm4_moe, glm4_moe_lite, glm4v_moe and glm_moe_dsa. They raise "Tensor parallelism is not supported on MPS devices", and main fails the exact same 52 tests on this machine.
- `utils/check_modular_conversion.py` reports the 25 models as consistent. `utils/check_copies.py` and `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` (ruff 0.14.10) pass on the changed files.

Note for `run-slow`: the unlimited_ocr integration tests wrap `generate` in bf16 autocast to match the reference implementation. The reference `MoEGate` has the same `F.linear(... float32 ...)` pattern, so under that autocast it actually routes in bf16. Those expected outputs may need an update. Suggested: `run-slow: deepseek_v2, deepseek_v3, glm4_moe, glm4_moe_lite, kolibri1, unlimited_ocr`.

Issues/PRs from first-time contributors that violate this rule will probably just be closed without review, and we might block you, especially if you open more than one or appear to be deliberately ignoring this. This creates lots of noise for reviewers and other users and will almost certainly get you blocked.

For more information, please read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

prs.title: Keep the MoE correction bias (and MiniMax-M2's router) in float32 when loading in bfloat16
prs.body:
# What does this PR do?

### What's wrong

These models route like DeepSeek-V3: they add `e_score_correction_bias` to the sigmoid scores, then take the top-k:
- MiniMax-M2 / M2.1 / M2.5
- MiniMax-M3 (through `minimax_m3_vl`)
- Step-3.7-Flash
- LongCat-Flash

More than 20 models with that router already declare `_keep_in_fp32_modules_strict = ["e_score_correction_bias"]`, including DeepSeek-V3, GLM-4.5/4.6/4.7, dots1 and MiMo-V2. These four don't. With `dtype=torch.bfloat16`, the bias is rounded to bf16.

For MiniMax and Step that breaks routing. Their checkpoints store the bias in float32, and its values are large but differ little between experts:

| checkpoint | bias mean (per layer) | spread between experts (std) | distinct values per layer, after bf16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| MiniMax-M2 / M2.1 / M2.5 | 1.5 – 8.6 | 0.02 – 0.18 | 9 – 41 of 256 |
| MiniMax-M3 | 4.9 – 7.9 | | 8 – 12 of 128 |
| Step-3.7-Flash (`router_bias`) | 5.8 – 8.7 | | 6 – 12 of 288 |

Near 8, bf16 values are 0.0625 apart, so the rounding error (up to 0.031) is larger than the gap between the sigmoid scores of competing experts. Expert selection then follows the rounding of the bias rather than the router.

MiniMax also stores the router weight (`gate.weight`) in float32. Its quantization config keeps it out of FP8 (`modules_to_not_convert: ["gate", "e_score_correction_bias", "lm_head"]`). The router already casts its input to the weight's dtype (`F.linear(hidden_states.to(self.weight.dtype), self.weight)`). Under `torch.autocast`, which Trainer turns on for `bf16=True`, that matmul still runs in bf16.

### Impact

Measured on MiniMax-M2.5's first MoE layer, using the real checkpoint tensors on 16,384 tokens (4 × 4096, prose and code):
- The embeddings and layer-0 attention come from the checkpoint (fp8, dequantized).
- Hidden states are computed once in bf16 with this library's MiniMax-M2 modules.
- Only the router's precision changes between rows.
- Each row is compared with routing that uses the checkpoint's float32 gate and bias.

| router | tokens with a different top-8 set | experts swapped per token (of 8) | busiest expert load / mean | idle experts |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| checkpoint (fp32 gate, fp32 bias) = this PR | 0 | 0 | 5.15 | 1 |
| main, `dtype=torch.bfloat16` | **99.7%** | **3.81** | **17.4** | **16** |
| bf16 gate, fp32 bias | 14.1% | 0.14 | 5.16 | 1 |
| fp32 gate, bf16 bias | 99.7% | 3.81 | 17.3 | 16 |

MiniMax-M2 gives the same picture:
- On main: 99.7% of tokens get a different set, 3.92 experts are swapped per token, the busiest expert carries 16.5× the mean load (6.03× from the checkpoint), and 17 experts get no tokens (1 from the checkpoint).
- With a bf16 gate and an fp32 bias: 12.5% of tokens get a different set.

So on main, almost every token has about half of its 8 expert slots filled by experts the float32 router would not pick. The bias causes almost all of this. The bf16 gate causes the remaining 13–14%, and the effect differs by checkpoint:
- **M2.5:** the gate weights are exactly representable in bf16. The loss comes from the router computing, and returning, its logits in bf16. A bf16 GEMM with float32 output gives 0%.
- **MiniMax-M3:** 99.998% of the gate weights change when rounded to bf16.

The router computes in the weight's dtype, so keeping the weight in float32 covers both cases.

LongCat-Flash's biases are centred near zero, so bf16 costs little there. It is included so the checkpoint's float32 values are kept as for the other models.

### Fix

- `MiniMaxM2PreTrainedModel`: `_keep_in_fp32_modules_strict = ["e_score_correction_bias", "mlp.gate.weight"]`. `MiniMaxM3VL` inherits it through the modular file.
- `Step3p7PreTrainedModel` and `LongcatFlashPreTrainedModel`: `_keep_in_fp32_modules_strict = ["e_score_correction_bias"]`.
- `MiniMaxM2TopKRouter` and `MiniMaxM3VLTopKRouter`: the matmul runs under `maybe_autocast(device_type, enabled=False)`, so it computes in the gate's dtype even under autocast. `Ernie4_5_MoeTopKRouter` already does this. Step-3.7's router is generated from M3-VL and gets the same wrapper; its gate is bf16 there, so it computes in bf16 as before. Without autocast, `maybe_autocast` is a `nullcontext`, and the outputs are unchanged.

The modeling files are regenerated from the modular files, and `utils/check_modular_conversion.py` passes. Step's `router_bias` is renamed to `e_score_correction_bias` before the keep-in-fp32 match, which the test covers through `save_pretrained` / `from_pretrained`.

### Tests

One new test per model (`test_router_and_correction_bias_kept_in_float32` for both MiniMax models, `test_e_score_correction_bias_kept_in_float32` for Step-3.7 and LongCat):
1. Fill the biases with `8.5 + 0.02 * arange(n)`.
2. `save_pretrained`, then `from_pretrained(..., dtype=torch.bfloat16)`.
3. Check that the biases are float32 and bitwise equal to what was saved, and for MiniMax that the gate weight is float32 and that the router returns float32 logits under `torch.autocast("cpu", dtype=torch.bfloat16)`.

Results:
- On main, all four fail (`torch.bfloat16 != torch.float32`); with the fix, all four pass.
- With the keep-in-fp32 lists but without the router wrapper, the two MiniMax tests still fail on the autocast check.
- The full test files of the four models: 703 passed, 677 skipped.
- `utils/check_modular_conversion.py` passes, and ruff 0.14.10 check and format are clean.

### Related

- #42580 (merged 2025-12-10) did the same for DeepSeek-V3, dots1, GLM4-MoE and GLM4V-MoE. Models added since then didn't get it.
- #49786 (open) changes MiniMax-M3-VL's key renaming and also edits `test_modeling_minimax_m3_vl.py`. Both PRs only add code there, so they shouldn't conflict. The keep-in-fp32 match runs on the renamed keys (`mlp.gate.weight`), which that PR keeps.
- I found no existing issue or PR for MiniMax-M2, Step-3.7 or LongCat.
- #50003 adds the same autocast wrapper to the routers that cast to float32 explicitly (DeepSeek-V3, GLM-4.x and 23 others).

## Code Agent Policy

The Transformers repo is currently being overwhelmed by a large number of PRs and issue comments written by code agents. These often are low-quality, or fix extremely minor issues that occur rarely or never in practice. As a result, we're instituting a rule that **first-time contributors should not use code agents to submit PRs or issues**. We'd also ask autonomous "OpenClaw"-like agents not to open any PRs or issues.

Issues/PRs from first-time contributors that violate this rule will probably just be closed without review, and we might block you, especially if you open more than one or appear to be deliberately ignoring this. We especially do not want new contributors to jump in on random issues to contribute an agent-written fix. This creates lots of noise for reviewers and other users and will almost certainly get you blocked.

For more information, please read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

prs.title: pipelines: defer eager model imports in text_to_audio and token_classification
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=50001)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## Problem

When any test file loads a pipeline class via `PipelineTesterMixin`, Python executes the entire pipeline source file at import time. Two pipeline files contained unconditional model imports that pull in unrelated model modules as transitive dependencies for **every** test that touches pipelines:

- `token_classification.py` line 7: `from ..models.bert.tokenization_bert_legacy import BasicTokenizer`  
  → causes `modeling_bert_legacy.py` (+ its imports) to be loaded for all pipeline tests
- `text_to_audio.py` inside `if is_torch_available()`: `from ..models.speecht5.modeling_speecht5 import SpeechT5HifiGan`  
  → causes 3 speecht5 source files to be loaded for all pipeline tests

These imports are **unconditional** — they do not go through `_LazyModule`, so there is no filtering mechanism to block them.

## Fix

Move both imports to the call site where they are actually needed:
- `BasicTokenizer` → moved inside `TokenClassificationPipeline.__init__`, just before it is used
- `SpeechT5HifiGan` → moved inside the `if self.model.__class__ in MODEL_FOR_TEXT_TO_SPECTROGRAM_MAPPING.values()` branch of `TextToAudioPipeline.__init__`, only executed when a spectrogram model is loaded

No behavior change for users — the imports happen at the same logical point (pipeline instantiation), just not at module-load time.

## Verification

Confirmed with a WIP runtime dependency recorder: before this fix, collecting `tests/models/vit/test_modeling_vit.py` recorded `speecht5` (3 files) and `tokenization_bert_legacy` as transitive imports. After this fix, those 4 files are gone from the collection-phase dependency list.

Tested on 4 unrelated model test files (vit, bert, gpt2, distilbert) — all confirmed.

## Context

This is **layer 2** of the case-6 spurious import issue: pipeline *source* files with direct eager model imports. Layer 1 (pipeline test files importing model classes at their top level) is a separate, larger problem tracked separately.

prs.title: [exporters] resolve @register_patch paths lazily to avoid eager model imports
prs.body:
## Summary

**Motivation:** `@register_patch` eagerly imports ~35 model modules at decoration time (when exporter files are first loaded). Because every `test_modeling_*.py` file transitively imports the exporter files via `ModelTesterMixin → ExportTesterMixin → test_export.py`, all ~511 test files end up with those model imports in their import graph. Because of these eager imports, a change to any one of those ~35 model modules would cause a WIP runtime dependency recorder (tracking which source files are actually imported when a test runs) to link all ~511 `test_modeling_*.py` files to those models — meaning a single model change would schedule all ~511 model tests.

**Verified:** running the recorder on `tests/models/vit/test_modeling_vit.py` — before the fix: 164 spurious non-vit model deps in the collection phase; after: 59 (105 removed, exactly matching the models registered via `@register_patch`). The 59 remaining are pipeline-related imports from `PipelineTesterMixin`, a separate issue.

**Root cause:** `@register_patch` previously called `_resolve_dotted_path` (which runs `importlib.import_module`) at **decoration time** — i.e., when each exporter file is first imported.  This eagerly loaded ~35 model modules the moment any exporter was imported.

Because `test_export.py` directly imports all 4 exporter files, and `test_modeling_common.py` imports `ExportTesterMixin` from `test_export.py` (making `ModelTesterMixin` inherit from it), every `test_modeling_*.py` file transitively triggers these eager imports — causing ~511 test files to record spurious source dependencies on those model modules.

**Fix:** store the dotted-path **string** in `_PATCHES` instead of the resolved object.  `apply_patches` now resolves each path just before installing the patch, at which point the model is already loaded anyway.  The silent-skip logic (path that can't resolve → skip) moves from `register_patch` to `apply_patches` via a walrus-operator filter.

Changes:
- `src/transformers/exporters/utils.py`: `_PATCHES` type hint, `register_patch` stores string, `apply_patches` resolves lazily
- `tests/exporters/test_utils.py`: update `test_register_patch_skips_unresolvable_path` to match new contract (string is stored; `apply_patches` still silently skips unresolvable paths — no patch installed, no exception)

`patch_attributes` itself and the direct `patch_attributes(config_patches)` call in `exporter_dynamo.py` (which passes already-resolved objects) are **unaffected**.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/exporters/test_utils.py::PatchRegistryEdgeCasesTest` passes locally
- [x] Real export tests pass on GPU CI (run [40376276872](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/actions/runs/40376276872/job/121762340060)): `test_torch_export_dynamic`, `test_torch_export_static`, `test_onnx_export_*` all PASSED for llama — these go directly through `apply_patches("dynamo")` / `apply_patches("onnx")` in `DynamoExporter.export()` / `OnnxExporter.export()`, confirming lazy resolution works correctly at actual export time

This adds a bot to check whether a PR requires docs and comments only if the answer is yes in order to catch missing docs earlier on rather than filling in the gaps later.

1. When a maintainer approves a PR, `docs-check-trigger.yml` saves the PR number

3. `check_pr_needs_docs.py`:

prs.title: Add MiMo V2 multimodal support, including MiMo-V2.5, MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL, MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL
prs.body: # What does this PR do? Adds Transformers support for the MiMo V2 multimodal family, including image, audio, and video understanding, shared preprocessing, and compatibility with the original checkpoint format. The following checkpoints share this implementation and provide their own model and preprocessing configurations: - [XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5](https://huggingface.co/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5) - [XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL](https://huggingface.co/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL) - [XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL](https://huggingface.co/XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL) Main changes: - Add MiMoV2VLForConditionalGeneration and its text, vision, audio, and learned audio-tokenizer components, with configuration classes and Auto API registrations. - Add MiMoV2Processor, MiMoV2ImageProcessor, MiMoV2VideoProcessor, and MiMoV2FeatureExtractor for image patching, video sampling and timestamps, waveform features, pre-tokenized audio, and audio/video interleaving. - Support legacy text and multimodal configuration selection without relying on repository names. Preserve text-only MiMo-V2-Flash compatibility and checkpoint-specific attention, normalization, and RoPE settings. - Load original TP-interleaved QKV and FP8/MXFP4 weights, including quantization scales stored in separate shards. Native exports can be reloaded through the standard Auto model and processor APIs. - Normalize image/audio/video URL content blocks before chat-template rendering and media loading without mutating the caller's messages. Preserve processor kwargs and assistant-mask alignment after placeholder expansion. - Correct segmented audio lengths and left-padding handling; retain FP32 audio codebooks and router correction biases; make RoPE initialization consistent across loading and reloading. - Reduce attention-sink memory use with query chunking and sliding-window key cropping, and preserve multimodal inputs for generation prefill and CPU-offloaded encoders. - Document image, audio, video, mixed-media generation, and saving/reloading using public media fixtures. ## Install ```bash uv venv .my-venv source .my-env/bin/activate # dependencies uv pip install "torch==2.9.1" "torchvision==0.24.1" "torchaudio==2.9.1" "torchcodec==0.9.1" "accelerate==1.12.0" pillow uv pip install -e . ``` ## Multi model forward ```bash import torch from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoProcessor checkpoint = "XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL" processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(checkpoint, trust_remote_code=False) model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained( checkpoint, device_map="auto", dtype=torch.bfloat16, trust_remote_code=False, ) print(type(model).__name__) # MiMoV2VLForConditionalGeneration messages = [ { "role": "user", "content": [ { "type": "image", "url": "http://images.cocodataset.org/val2017/000000039769.jpg", }, { "type": "audio", "url": "https://huggingface.co/datasets/hf-internal-testing/dummy-audio-samples/resolve/main/f2641_0_throatclearing.wav", }, { "type": "video", "url": "https://huggingface.co/datasets/hf-internal-testing/test-videos/resolve/main/tiny_video_320x240.mp4", }, { "type": "text", "text": ( "Describe these three independent media samples in order: " "the image, the audio, and the video. " "Respond in English with a separate section for each." ), }, ], } ] inputs = processor.apply_chat_template( messages, add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=False, tokenize=True, return_dict=True, return_tensors="pt", ).to(model.device) with torch.inference_mode(): generated_ids = model.generate( **inputs, max_new_tokens=10240, do_sample=False, logits_to_keep=1, ) # generate output ids new_token_ids = generated_ids[:, inputs.input_ids.shape[1]:] output_text = processor.batch_decode( new_token_ids, skip_special_tokens=True, clean_up_tokenization_spaces=False, )[0] print(output_text) ``` result: ## Before submitting - [ ] This PR fixes a typo or improves the docs (you can dismiss the other checks if that's the case). - [ ] Did you read the [contributor guideline](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/contributing) and the [Pull Request](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/pr_checks) checks? - [ ] Was this discussed/approved via a Github issue or the [forum](https://discuss.huggingface.co/)? Please add a link to it if that's the case. - [ ] Did you make sure to update the documentation with your changes according to the [guidelines](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/tree/main/docs)? - [ ] Did you write any new necessary [tests](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/testing)? ## Who can review? Anyone in the community is free to review the PR once the tests have passed. Feel free to tag members/contributors who may be interested in your PR.

This PR adds the DSpark speculation method.
Essentially it's DFlash with a sequential bias head on top. Hence we refactor a part of DFlash to make it usable in DSpark, which inherits from DFlash. Some parts are repeated rather than inherited to make the code more readable though. 

Right now it only supports the `vanilla` (ie. Markov) variant, drops the confidence head (because we dont really need it, but we will add it later) and the hardware-aware scheduling (that I am not sure we will add it?).
This PR adds DSpark as a standalone technique, ie. not part of a model release, but it might be needed for model releases in the future. Nevertheless, it adds an example script so that one can check it is working.

- [ ] confidence head support?

prs.title: [NeoMME] Keep special-token strings literal in retrieval text
prs.body:
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49995) # What does this PR do? ## Context `NeoMMEProcessor.apply_chat_template(tokenize=True)` renders the retrieval template to a string and then tokenizes that string. Special-token strings typed by the user are tokenized as special tokens: ```python from transformers import NeoMMEProcessor processor = NeoMMEProcessor.from_pretrained( "Hcompany/NeoMME-260M-Retriever", revision="481083153ac22931afbd614e672212bffbcb666e" ) def encode(text: str, task: str, **processor_kwargs) -> None: try: ids = processor.apply_chat_template( [[{"role": "user", "content": text}]], task=task, tokenize=True, return_dict=True, processor_kwargs=processor_kwargs, )["input_ids"][0] print(f"{len(ids)} ids, {ids.count(processor.tokenizer.mask_token_id)} masks") except Exception as error: print(f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}") encode("see here", task="document") encode("find and ", task="query") encode("word " * 50, task="query", max_length=20, truncation=True) ``` On `main`: ``` TemplateError: is reserved for image documents. 15 ids, 11 masks ValueError: Truncation removed NeoMME query expansion tokens; increase `max_length`. ``` - `` in document text raises, because the template reserves `` for image documents. - A query always ends with 10 `` expansion tokens, but `find and ` gets 11: the user's `` becomes a real mask id, and `` becomes the document marker. - A long query with `truncation=True` raises instead of truncating, because truncation cuts the expansion tokens. ## Changes
Click here to expand - **Literal user text** — `apply_chat_template(tokenize=True)` renders the template with an `unk_token` placeholder in place of each conversation's text. `__call__` then tokenizes the real text with `split_special_tokens=True` and splices its ids at the placeholder (`processing_neomme.py:215`). - **Text-only truncation** — truncation cuts the text and never the template, so the task marker and the 10 query expansion tokens stay. Rows without text (images, empty content) raise "`max_length` is too short" instead of being cut. - **Simpler checks** — removes the post-padding marker loop and the `` count check. The marker check now runs once per row before padding, which also fixes left padding with `return_attention_mask=False`. - **Core kwargs merge** — `ProcessorMixin.apply_chat_template` merges flat kwargs into `processor_kwargs` instead of replacing them (`processing_utils.py:2073`). Before, any flat kwarg dropped every nested one, including the private keys NeoMME passes. - **Docs** — `neomme.md` notes that raw text passed to the processor is tokenized as given. Retriever checkpoints keep it literal through `apply_chat_template(tokenize=True)`; with the base model, tokenize the text with `split_special_tokens=True` and prepend `document_token_id`.
## Manual tests Re-running the snippet from Context on this branch gives the expected output: no errors, exactly 10 masks per query, and the long query truncated to `max_length=20`. ``` 6 ids, 0 masks 19 ids, 10 masks 20 ids, 10 masks ``` ## Notes > [!WARNING] > - `apply_chat_template` now raises "passed two times" for every processor when the same key is given both flat and inside `processor_kwargs`, matching `processor.__call__`. Before, the nested value was silently dropped. > - On the NeoMME retrieval path, `return_token_type_ids`, `return_offsets_mapping`, `return_special_tokens_mask` and the other per-token outputs now raise. - Ids change for any retrieval text that contains special-token strings. Embeddings computed with the old processor on such text will differ. - With `tokenize=True`, the template must insert the text unchanged and join text items with nothing in between. A custom template that filters the text (for example `| lower`) has no effect on the ids. - When `max_length` leaves no room for text, a query becomes its marker plus the 10 masks. Before, this raised. ## Before submitting - [ ] This PR fixes a typo or improves the docs (you can dismiss the other checks if that's the case). - [x] Did you read the [contributor guideline](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/contributing) and the [Pull Request](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/pr_checks) checks? - [ ] Was this discussed/approved via a Github issue or the [forum](https://discuss.huggingface.co/)? Please add a link to it if that's the case. - [x] Did you make sure to update the documentation with your changes according to the [guidelines](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/tree/main/docs)? - [x] Did you write any new necessary [tests](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/testing)? ## Who can review? @zucchini-nlp

prs.title: Fix QuestionAnswering heads loading base weights from causal LM checkpoints
prs.body:
Fixes #49973

## Summary

`LlamaForQuestionAnswering` and the other QA heads that inherited `base_model_prefix = "transformer"` could not load the base weights from a causal-LM checkpoint: the checkpoint stores them as `model.*` while the QA model expects `transformer.*`, so every base layer was silently re-initialized.

This adds class-scoped `WeightRenaming` entries (`^model\.` → `transformer.`) for the 12 affected QA heads. The reverse transform keeps already-saved QA checkpoints under `transformer.*` loadable, and loading from a bare base-model checkpoint continues to work through the existing `base_model_prefix` handling.

## Verification

Reproduction before the fix (tiny Llama, loading a `LlamaForCausalLM` checkpoint into `LlamaForQuestionAnswering`):

```
MISSING count 22
base layer keys mismatched 15 of 20
```

After:

```
missing {'qa_outputs.bias', 'qa_outputs.weight'}
unexpected {'lm_head.weight'}
base layer keys mismatched 0 of 20
```

Regression test (fails before, passes after):

```
python -m pytest tests/models/llama/test_modeling_llama.py -k "test_question_answering_loads_causal_lm_weights" -q
1 passed
```

Related focused tests:

```

4 passed, 111 subtests passed
```

prs.title: Run the TP/EP mixin tests on every model and fix the failures
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49988)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## What does this PR do?

Stacked on #49986 (base: `tp-mixin-persistent-ranks`), which makes these tests fast enough to run on every model.

This PR removes the `TP_DISTRIBUTED_TEST_MODEL_TYPES` allowlist, so `test_tp_*` / `test_ep_*` from `TensorParallelTesterMixin` run on every model with a TP/EP plan. It also fixes what that surfaced. Enabling every model initially gave **234 failures across 25 models** in the CI image. All of them also fail with `main`'s spawn-per-test code, so they are pre-existing bugs, not caused by #49986.

**Result (CI image, every model):** 973 passed / 234 failed → **1216 passed / 0 failed**.

### Library fixes

**New TP styles** in `src/transformers/distributed/tensor_parallel.py` (documented in `perf_infer_gpu_multi.md`):
- `local_colwise`: shards a bare per-head parameter (e.g. attention `sinks`) and hands its owner module the local shard during forward. Before, `colwise` on a bare param left the owning attention module mixing `Tensor` and `DTensor`. Used by hy_v4, mimo_v2_flash, granite_swa, granitemoe_swa.
- `replicated_output`: marks a module's local output as a replicated DTensor. glm5_next's unsharded KDA layers share the `self_attn.o_proj: rowwise` rule with its head-sharded MLA layers; this lets the rowwise `o_proj` slice KDA's output locally.
- `replicate_input`: reduces a partial DTensor input once and runs the module on plain tensors. This is for a norm applied inside an `nn.Embedding` subclass's own forward (inkling, muse_glimmer, muse_spark).
- `all_reduce`: a module holding sharded params itself (inkling's shared experts, via `torch.bmm`) now runs on local params, with input grads all-reduced. inkling is the only model using `all_reduce`.

**Loading fixes**
- `core_model_loading.py` / `distributed/sharding_utils.py`: TP shard-on-read now slices checkpoint tensors in their source layout when a converter transposes, chunks or concatenates them along the sharded dim. `DtensorShardOperation` takes `source_placements`, built from a per-op `get_source_placements` hook (`Transpose`, `Chunk`, `Concatenate`). This fixes:
  - qwen3_vl_moe (transposed experts). This includes the loader part of #48373, so that PR can be closed or rebased on this.
  - hrm_text (fused `gqkv_proj`).
  - step3p7 (separate `gate_proj` / `up_proj`).
- `conversion_mapping.py`: the ShieldGemma2 prefix mapping is keyed on `ShieldGemma2ForImageClassification`, which owns it. `Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration` can now load shieldgemma2 checkpoints; before, every language-model weight came out unexpected/missing.
- `distributed/mixin.py`: when the `lm_head` is sharded, `embed_tokens` is sharded too, even if the base model has no TP plan. This fixes tied weights under EP for gpt_oss.
- `modeling_utils.py`: `set_experts_implementation` on a composite model whose experts live in a sub-model (kimi_k25, nemotron_h_omni) no longer raises at the top level.

**Model fixes**
- gemma4: the multimodal pad embedding is looked up through the embedding module instead of indexing its vocab-sharded weight.
- voxtral_realtime: an in-place `+=` on the TP embedding output (an autograd view) is now out of place.
- step3p7: `Step3p7Experts` keeps `@use_experts_implementation` (a `@no_inherit_decorator` was dropping it).
- qwen3_vl_moe: added `q_norm` / `k_norm` grad all-reduce to the plan.

### Test changes

**Mixin (`tests/test_tensor_parallel_mixin.py`)**
- Allowlist removed.
- A `_get_tp_extra_inputs` hook lets models that can't run on `input_ids` alone pass their extra inputs; voxtral_realtime uses it for `input_features`.
- The backward tests reseed before each forward, since phimoe samples its routing in training mode.
- `test_tp_generation_quantized` now scores the non-TP generation token by token and accepts a TP token only within the measured Float8 noise at that position. The old check compared free-running generations, so one near-tie flip mismatched every later token. Unquantized TP vs non-TP is unaffected and still checked at 1e-5 by the float tests.

**Skips**
- Removed 13 workaround skips: 10 quantized-generation skips (glm_moe_dsa, glm4_moe_lite, olmo_hybrid, starcoder2, jais2, gemma2, gemma3, exaone4, exaone_moe, deepseek_v2), olmo3's rope-theta override, and the 3 hrm_text "higher tols, FIXME" TP skips.
- Added 4:
  - inkling text-only `test_tp_forward_0/1` and `test_tp_generation`. TP shards the checkpoint tensor before conversion, and the `colwise` experts plan matches the multimodal checkpoint's interleaved `gate_up_proj`, while the text-only model stores gate rows then up rows. One config class serves both, so a real fix needs sharding after conversion; that's a follow-up.
  - hrm_text `test_tp_generation_quantized`: 48.6% token match. Unquantized TP generation matches exactly.

**Tester configs**
- gemma3 and ernie4_5_vl_moe VLM testers use 2 KV heads instead of 1. With TP=2, a single KV head can't be split across ranks.
- aria's tester uses 4 experts instead of 3, so they shard evenly across 2 EP ranks.

### CI replay (as in #49986: 6 nodes × 4 vCPU / 8 GB, `transformers-torch-light`, exact CI command)

| Configuration | Result | Slowest node |
|---|---|---|
| This PR, every model | 1234 passed, 0 failed | **2m15s** |
| Every model, on main's spawn-per-test, before these fixes | 100 failing | 15m17s |

prs.title: Standardize supported_aspect_ratios in tile-based image processors
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49987)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## What

Tile-based image processors rebuilt their list of supported tile grids on **every call**: 10 copies of `get_all_supported_aspect_ratios`, plus lfm2_vl's `_target_ratios`, phi4's inline set and llama4's `get_factors` + `find_supported_resolutions`. Mllama already did it the simple way, with the list stored in config and computed at conversion. All of them now follow that pattern:

```text
before                                          after
processor(images)                               Processor.__init__
  └─ get_optimal_tiled_canvas(min, max)           └─ supported_aspect_ratios: built once (if missing / bounds changed)
       └─ get_all_supported_aspect_ratios(...)           ↓ saved in preprocessor_config.json
            (lru_cache, 13 implementations)       processor(images)
                                                   └─ get_optimal_tiled_canvas(self.supported_aspect_ratios)
```

**Same shape in every processor:**

```python
init_only_kwargs = ("min_patches", "max_patches")   # the bounds the list is built from

def __init__(self, **kwargs):
    super().__init__(**kwargs)
    # build the grids for configs saved without them, or when `min_patches`/`max_patches` were changed
    tile_counts = [width * height for width, height in self.supported_aspect_ratios or [[0, 0]]]
    if (min(tile_counts), max(tile_counts)) != (self.min_patches, self.max_patches):
        self.supported_aspect_ratios = <this model's rule, in this model's order>
```

| Model | Bounds (`init_only_kwargs`) | Rule / order | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| got_ocr2 (+ internvl), deepseek_ocr2, unlimited_ocr, cohere2_vision | `min_patches`, `max_patches` | `min ≤ w·h ≤ max`, by area | got_ocr2, inherited via modular |
| ovis2 | `min_patches`, `max_patches` | same as got_ocr2 | hand-written |
| mllama | `max_image_tiles` | `h·w ≤ max`, unsorted (index = `aspect_ratio_id - 1`) | own |
| lfm2_vl | `min_tiles`, `max_tiles` | `sorted(set(...))` by area | own |
| phi4_multimodal | `dynamic_hd` | `sorted(set(...))` by area | own |
| llama4 | `max_patches` | factor pairs, grouped by ratio (same dict order) | own; grids × `size` at use |

The order is kept per model on purpose. For mllama it is the `aspect_ratio_id` (embedding row), and for the others it decides ties.

**Shared bits, written once:**
- `BaseImageProcessor.init_only_kwargs` (3 lines in `preprocess`) replaces 6 per-model `_validate_preprocess_kwargs` overrides.
- `supported_aspect_ratios` is documented once in `ImageProcessorArgs`.

## LOC

Every processor file shrinks except phi4 (+3). Total **+434 / −781**.

| File | Δ |
|---|---|
| llama4 | −66 |
| cohere2_vision modular / generated | −39 / −25 |
| got_ocr2 torch / pil | −31 / −32 |
| deepseek_ocr2 generated torch / pil | −33 / −31 |
| unlimited_ocr generated | −33 |
| mllama torch / pil | −18 / −15 |
| lfm2_vl | −10 |
| ovis2 torch / pil | −9 / −8 |
| phi4_multimodal | +3 |
| image_processing_utils / auto_docstring | +5 / +8 |

## Breaking: tile bounds are init-only

`min_patches` / `max_patches` / `max_image_tiles` / `min_tiles` / `max_tiles` / `dynamic_hd` now raise if passed per call with a **different** value than the init one. Passing the same value still works (vLLM's `mm_processor_kwargs`, LLaMA-Factory). `from_pretrained(..., max_patches=6)` rebuilds the list.

I searched GitHub for per-call usage. Every real caller (vLLM, LLaMA-Factory, phi4 fine-tuning scripts, NeMo, maxtext) passes the value at init or passes the init value. The only per-call changes were our `got_ocr2.md` example and 4 tests, all updated here.

⚠ Non-default bounds only: ovis2's covering mode and cohere2_vision used to ignore `min_patches`. They now respect it. The default is 1, so nothing changes by default.

## Verification

- Outputs are **bit-identical to `main`**: 18 processor/backend configs (including non-default bounds such as got_ocr2 3–9, phi4 `dynamic_hd=4`, llama4 `max_patches=5` + `resize_to_max_canvas`, lfm2_vl without splitting) × 13 image shapes, hashing every output tensor. 18/18 identical.
- The check is live: perturbing the stored list (reversed, or with the middle grids dropped, same bounds) changes the hash for got_ocr2, mllama, lfm2_vl, llama4 and ovis2 (both modes).
- `pytest tests/models/{got_ocr2,deepseek_ocr2,unlimited_ocr,internvl,ovis2,mllama,cohere2_vision,aya_vision,lfm2_vl,phi4_multimodal,llama4} -k "processing or processor"`: 564 passed, 0 failed. (InternVL `test_apply_chat_template_video_*` fail on `main` too.)
- `check_modular_conversion`, `check_copies`, `check_docstrings`, ruff: clean.

## Not in scope

- aria (`split_resolutions`) and llava_next / llava_onevision (`image_grid_pinpoints`) already store the list in config.
- minicpm (candidates depend on each image) and ultravbert (computes the grid directly) have no fixed list.
- #49012 (granite_for_docling) adds another copy; once this lands it can inherit got_ocr2's `__init__`.

prs.title: Reuse the TP/EP test ranks across tests instead of spawning them per test
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49986)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## What does this PR do?

Cuts the `tensor_parallel_ci` job time by ~4-5x, which is what makes running the TP/EP mixin tests on every model (instead of the `TP_DISTRIBUTED_TEST_MODEL_TYPES` allowlist) affordable.

### Where the time goes

Profiling one TP/EP test under CI conditions (4 vCPU, `pytest -n 4`, gloo): the process group init is ~11 ms, but each test `mp.spawn`s 2 fresh ranks that re-import torch + transformers while competing with the other xdist workers for the 4 cores. The median test takes **21.8 s**, of which the actual test (load TP + reference model, forward/backward) is **~0.7 s**.

### Fix

`_init_distributed` keeps its signature but now dispatches to a pool of `tp` long-lived ranks (one pool per `(world_size, backend)` per pytest/xdist worker process):
- ranks init the process group once and run the test functions they get from a queue;
- any rank error or crash kills the whole pool and re-raises, since the surviving ranks may be stuck in a collective, and the next test starts from fresh ranks;
- ranks `gc.collect()` (+ empty the accelerator cache off CPU) between tests, and exit by themselves if the parent dies.

### Benchmark: replay of the CircleCI `tensor_parallel_ci` job

6 nodes in parallel, each a Docker container pinned to 4 cores / 8 GB, `huggingface/transformers-torch-light` + the job's install steps, CI env vars (`OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`, `PYTEST_TIMEOUT=120`, ...), full-run test list and the exact CI pytest command (`-m is_tensor_parallel_test -n 4 --max-worker-restart=0 --random-order-bucket=module --reruns 5 ...`).

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Current allowlist: slowest node | 6m31s | **1m20s** (4.9x) |
| All models (`TP_DISTRIBUTED_TEST_MODEL_TYPES = None`): slowest node | 15m17s | **3m58s** (3.8x) |
| All models: total across 6 nodes | 65.8 min | **16.2 min** |
| Median TP/EP test | 21.8 s | **0.7 s** |
| Peak memory per node | 6.0-6.3 GiB | 6.2-6.3 GiB |
| Outcomes (all models) | 596 passed, 100 failed, 564 skipped | identical, test by test |

Notes:
- CircleCI splits by its timing history, which I don't have locally; I split round-robin by file, the same for both versions. The total across nodes doesn't depend on the split.
- The 100 failures with all models enabled already happen on `main` (20 models: mixed Tensor/DTensor ops, sharding-size errors, quantized generation mismatches, ...). This PR doesn't change the allowlist; enabling all models needs those fixed first.
- Re-validated after rebasing on current `main`: allowlist with `-n 4` on 4 cores gives 112 passed / 25 skipped in ~30 s, vs 4m00-4m13 on `main` (which also had one flaky failure in one of two runs).
- `tests/generation/test_continuous_batching.py`'s NCCL TP tests also go through `_init_distributed` and so use the pool now; I haven't run them.

prs.title: Fix BigBird crash with static cache / compiled generate
prs.body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49984)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## What's wrong

`BigBirdForCausalLM` with `attention_type="block_sparse"` crashes as soon as generation uses a static cache:

```python
model = BigBirdForCausalLM.from_pretrained("google/bigbird-roberta-base", attention_type="block_sparse", is_decoder=True)
model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=5, cache_implementation="static")
```

```
ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)
```

## Why

When the cache is compileable, `generate` builds the mask up front via `create_masks_for_generate`, which returns a **4D** mask. Block-sparse attention expects a **2D** one, so `BigBirdModel.forward` fails on `batch_size, seq_length = attention_mask.size()`.

## Fix

Override `create_masks_for_generate` in `BigBirdForCausalLM` to return the 2D mask unchanged.

**Why this is correct:** the hook only exists to build ahead of time the mask the model would have built for itself, and the mask BigBird wants is exactly the 2D one it already gets on every other path — so returning it unchanged restores the dynamic-cache behaviour rather than inventing a new one. It cannot copy BLOOM's override from #49481, which pads to the cache length for `build_alibi_tensor`: BigBird feeds the mask to `_pad_to_block_size`, which requires the length to match the *input* and stay `block_size`-aligned.

`bigbird_pegasus` is unaffected (its block-sparse code is encoder-side, and this hook is decoder-only).

## Tests

Added `test_generate_block_sparse_with_static_cache`, comparing dynamic-cache against static-cache generation. It fails without the change and passes with it, and the rest of the BigBird suite is unchanged. Nothing else can regress: the hook is only reachable when `past_key_values.is_compileable`, so eager and dynamic-cache runs never call it, and I checked their logits are bit-identical to `main`.

Worth flagging: BigBird permanently downgrades `attention_type` to `original_full` on its first generate, since the decode step is shorter than the block-sparse minimum. A test that just generates twice never exercises block-sparse the second time and passes even without the fix, so the test resets the attention type before each `generate`.

prs.title: Install the TP gradient all-reduce only when grad is enabled
prs.body: [![🤗 Transformers CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Transformers%20CI-333333?style=flat)](https://transformers-ci.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=49975) # Issue Module-level backward hooks create graph breaks when using `torch.compile` but not with parameter-level hooks. We can't add them during setup time as the parameters are empty placeholders that are going to be replaced with the loaded weights, discarding all previously attached hooks. So they are attached only on first forward pass. # Benchmark # Repro ```python """ torchrun --nproc-per-node 2 bench_inference.py """ import json import time import torch import torch._dynamo import torch.distributed as dist from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM from transformers.distributed.tensor_parallel import ReplicatedWithGradAllReduce MODEL = "Qwen/Qwen3-8B" SEQ_LENS = [1, 512] WARMUP, ITERS = 5, 20 def install_forward_before(self, module, mesh): """Implementation on the PR's base commit.""" def _all_reduce_grads(mod, grad_input, grad_output): for param in mod.parameters(recurse=False): if param.grad is not None: dist.all_reduce(param.grad, group=mesh.get_group()) module.register_full_backward_hook(_all_reduce_grads) return module install_forward_after = ReplicatedWithGradAllReduce.install_forward def time_forward(model, input_ids): """Mean milliseconds per forward.""" for _ in range(WARMUP): model(input_ids=input_ids) torch.cuda.synchronize() dist.barrier() start = time.perf_counter() for _ in range(ITERS): model(input_ids=input_ids) torch.cuda.synchronize() return (time.perf_counter() - start) / ITERS * 1e3 @torch.no_grad() def benchmark(install_forward): ReplicatedWithGradAllReduce.install_forward = install_forward model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(MODEL, tp_plan="auto", dtype=torch.bfloat16).eval() torch.manual_seed(0) inputs = {n: torch.randint(0, 1000, (1, n), device=model.device) for n in SEQ_LENS} results = {} torch._dynamo.reset() results["graph breaks"] = torch._dynamo.explain(model)(input_ids=inputs[SEQ_LENS[0]]).graph_break_count for n in SEQ_LENS: results[f"eager, {n} tok (ms)"] = time_forward(model, inputs[n]) torch._dynamo.reset() compiled = torch.compile(model) for n in SEQ_LENS: results[f"compiled, {n} tok (ms)"] = time_forward(compiled, inputs[n]) del model, compiled torch._dynamo.reset() torch.cuda.empty_cache() return results before = benchmark(install_forward_before) after = benchmark(install_forward_after) if dist.get_rank() == 0: print(f"\n{MODEL}, bf16, TP={dist.get_world_size()}, torch {torch.__version__}, no_grad") print(f"{'':<22}{'before':>10}{'after':>10}{'speedup':>10}") for key in before: b, a = before[key], after[key] if isinstance(b, int): print(f"{key:<22}{b:>10}{a:>10}{'-':>10}") else: print(f"{key:<22}{b:>10.1f}{a:>10.1f}{b / a:>9.2f}x") meta = {"model": MODEL, "tp": dist.get_world_size(), "torch": torch.__version__} with open("bench_inference.json", "w") as f: json.dump({"meta": meta, "before": before, "after": after}, f, indent=2) dist.destroy_process_group() ```
